name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using the most recent fiscal year annual data. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June after annual reports are public.
rationale: Inventory building that outpaces sales signals demand overestimation and future write-downs or margin pressure, so subsequent returns are depressed.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual Intensity of Earnings
construction: For each fiscal year, compute (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding short-term debt minus depreciation) scaled by average total assets (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, DP, AT). This isolates the accrual component of earnings. Rank firms each June.
rationale: Earnings driven more by accruals than by cash flows are less persistent and prone to reversal, and investors overvalue such firms initially.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals / cash-based earnings)

name: Capital Expenditure Surge
construction: Compute capital expenditure (Compustat CAPX) scaled by average net property, plant and equipment (PPENT), then subtract the firm's own prior three-year average of that ratio. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Abnormal spikes in investment reflect empire-building and overoptimism; heavy investors subsequently underperform as returns on new capital disappoint.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (firms cutting or below-trend investment)

name: Gross Margin Momentum
construction: Compute gross profitability margin as (SALE minus COGS)/SALE for the two most recent fiscal years and take the change. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by the year-over-year improvement in gross margin.
rationale: Improving unit economics reflects strengthening competitive position and pricing power that the market is slow to fully price.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving gross margin)

name: Selling Expense Efficiency
construction: Compute SG&A expense (Compustat XSGA) divided by sales (SALE), then take the change relative to the prior fiscal year. Rank firms each June by declining SG&A-to-sales ratio.
rationale: Firms achieving operating leverage by growing sales faster than overhead show improving efficiency that predicts higher future profitability and returns.

name: Dividend Initiation Coverage
construction: For dividend-paying firms, compute payout coverage as earnings per share (EPSPX) divided by dividends per share (DVPSX), combined with the one-year change in the dividend rate. Rank firms with rising dividends that remain well-covered (high coverage times positive dividend change).
rationale: Rising but comfortably covered dividends credibly signal management confidence in sustainable cash flows, an underappreciated positive signal.

name: Volume-Adjusted Price Reversal
construction: Over the most recent month, compute the stock's return divided by its average daily share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) from CRSP. Rank firms cross-sectionally each month-end.
rationale: Large price moves on low volume reflect illiquidity-driven pressure that reverses, whereas moves on high volume reflect information; low-volume losers rebound.
higher_returns_for: low values (recent losers on thin volume)

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Trend
construction: Estimate residual (idiosyncratic) volatility from a market-model regression of daily returns over the trailing 60 days, and compare to the same measure computed over the prior 60-day window; rank firms by the decline in idiosyncratic volatility each month.
rationale: Falling firm-specific volatility signals resolution of uncertainty and stabilizing fundamentals, which precedes positive risk-adjusted returns.

name: Debt Maturity Shift
construction: Compute the ratio of debt in current liabilities (Compustat DLC) to total debt (DLC plus DLTT), then take the change from the prior fiscal year. Rank firms each June by increases in the short-term share of debt.
rationale: A rising reliance on short-term debt increases rollover and refinancing risk, so such firms carry elevated distress risk and, when constrained, deliver lower returns.

name: Asset Turnover Acceleration
construction: Compute asset turnover as sales (SALE) divided by average total assets (AT) for the two most recent fiscal years, and take the year-over-year change. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by the improvement.
rationale: Improving productivity of assets reflects better capacity utilization and operational execution that the market underweights relative to headline earnings.

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (item COGS), measured from annual financials lagged at least 4 months to ensure public availability. Sort stocks into deciles on this spread.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales throughput signals overproduction and weak future demand, which the market is slow to incorporate into prices.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventories growing slower than COGS)

name: Accrual-to-Cash-Flow Ratio
construction: For each firm compute total accruals as the change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, using annual balance sheet items (change in current assets minus change in cash, minus change in current liabilities plus change in short-term debt, minus depreciation from item DP). Scale by cash flow from operations (net income minus accruals). Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Earnings composed of high accruals relative to cash are less persistent, and investors overweight reported earnings without discounting accrual quality.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (cash-rich, low-accrual earnings)

name: Asset Turnover Acceleration
construction: Compute asset turnover as sales (item SALE) divided by average total assets (item AT), then take the change in this ratio over the most recent fiscal year versus the prior year. Sort into deciles.
rationale: Improving efficiency in generating sales per dollar of assets reflects operational momentum not yet priced, forecasting stronger future profitability.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (accelerating asset turnover)

name: Selling Expense Intensity Change
construction: Compute selling, general and administrative expense (item XSGA) divided by sales, then the year-over-year change in this ratio. Rank firms cross-sectionally.
rationale: A falling SG&A-to-sales ratio indicates operating leverage and disciplined cost control that the market underappreciates, predicting margin expansion.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining SG&A intensity)

name: Trading Volume Trend Reversal
construction: Using CRSP daily/monthly volume, compute the ratio of average share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) over the most recent month to average turnover over the prior 12 months. Sort into deciles.
rationale: A sudden surge in turnover relative to normal activity often reflects transient attention and overpricing that subsequently reverses.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (turnover contracting relative to history)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that began paying a cash dividend within the prior 12 months (first non-zero CRSP dividend after a dry period) and compute the change in dividend payout. Compare newly-initiating firms to non-payers.
rationale: Dividend initiation is a costly signal of managerial confidence in sustainable cash flows, and the positive information diffuses gradually into prices.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (recent dividend initiators)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute gross margin ((SALE-COGS)/SALE) for each of the last 5 fiscal years and take the standard deviation. Rank firms; lower volatility indicates more stable margins.
rationale: Firms with stable gross margins have more predictable and higher-quality earnings streams that are underpriced relative to their lower fundamental risk.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable gross margins)

name: Capital Expenditure Restraint
construction: Compute capital expenditures (item CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets, and measure the deviation from the firm's own 3-year average capex ratio. Sort into deciles.
rationale: Firms cutting investment below their historical norm return cash discipline that the market discounts, while overinvesting firms empire-build and destroy value.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (capex below historical norm)

name: Debt Maturity Shift
construction: Compute the ratio of long-term debt (item DLTT) to total debt (DLTT plus debt in current liabilities item DLC), and take the year-over-year change. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: A shift toward long-term financing reduces rollover and refinancing risk, signaling financial stability that lowers required returns' unpriced risk premium and improves future performance.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (increasing long-term debt share)

name: Return-Volatility Efficiency
construction: Over the trailing 12 months compute cumulative stock return divided by the standard deviation of monthly returns (a firm-level Sharpe-like ratio) using CRSP data. Sort into deciles.
rationale: Stocks delivering returns with low volatility exhibit persistent risk-adjusted performance that momentum-chasing investors fail to reward proportionally.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high return per unit of volatility)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each fiscal year, compute the growth rate of inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus the growth rate of sales (item SALE), both year-over-year. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year data.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals overproduction and weak future demand, presaging margin compression and negative earnings surprises.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventories growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual-to-Cash-Flow Ratio
construction: Compute total accruals as the change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, using balance-sheet items: change in current assets (ACT) minus change in cash (CHE), minus change in current liabilities (LCT) minus change in debt in current liabilities (DLC), minus depreciation (DP). Divide by operating cash flow proxied by net income (IB) plus depreciation. Rank each June.
rationale: Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash are less persistent and are systematically over-extrapolated by investors, reversing in future periods.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (cash-based earnings)

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock
construction: Compute capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged net property, plant and equipment (PPENT), then subtract the firm's own prior three-year average of this ratio. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Abnormal investment surges reflect empire-building and overoptimism about growth, leading to poor subsequent returns as returns on new capital disappoint.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (below-normal investment)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that paid zero cash dividends (DVC) in the prior fiscal year but positive dividends in the most recent fiscal year. Compare their subsequent 12-month returns to continuing payers and non-payers.
rationale: Managers initiate dividends when confident in sustainable cash flows; the signal is under-reacted to by investors accustomed to the prior no-dividend regime.

name: Gross Margin Trend
construction: Compute gross margin as (SALE minus COGS)/SALE for each of the last two fiscal years and take the change. Rank stocks each June by this year-over-year change in gross margin.
rationale: Improving gross margins signal strengthening pricing power and operational efficiency not yet fully impounded into prices.

name: Share Issuance Net of Buybacks
construction: Compute the annual change in split-adjusted shares outstanding using CRSP shares (SHROUT) adjusted by the cumulative adjustment factor. Rank firms each June by percentage change over the prior fiscal year.
rationale: Net share issuance dilutes existing holders and reflects managerial timing of overvalued equity; net repurchasers are relatively undervalued.
higher_returns_for: low values (net repurchasers / shrinking share count)

name: Volatility of Monthly Turnover
construction: Using CRSP daily or monthly volume divided by shares outstanding, compute monthly turnover for the prior 12 months and take its standard deviation, scaled by mean turnover. Rank each month.
rationale: Unstable trading intensity reflects heterogeneous investor disagreement and speculative demand that command lower future returns as attention fades.

name: Debt Maturity Structure Shift
construction: Compute the ratio of debt in current liabilities (DLC) to total debt (DLC plus DLTT). Take the year-over-year change in this ratio each June.
rationale: A rising share of short-term debt increases rollover and refinancing risk, so firms shifting toward short maturities face elevated distress-related discount, but well-financed firms lengthening maturities signal stability.

name: Return-on-Assets Acceleration
construction: Compute ROA as income before extraordinary items (IB) divided by lagged total assets (AT) for the last three fiscal years, then measure the second difference (this year's change in ROA minus last year's change). Rank each June.
rationale: Accelerating profitability indicates improving fundamentals that investors extrapolate too slowly, producing continued positive surprises.

name: Idiosyncratic Return Skewness
construction: For each stock, regress prior 60 monthly returns on the market return, and compute the skewness of the regression residuals. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Investors overpay for lottery-like stocks with positively skewed idiosyncratic returns, driving their prices up and future returns down.

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute the year-over-year growth rate of inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus the year-over-year growth rate of sales (item SALE) using the most recent annual financial statements. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June following the fiscal year-end.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals overinvestment and weakening demand that the market is slow to price, foreshadowing lower future profitability.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventories growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Quality
construction: Compute total accruals as the change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding short-term debt, minus depreciation, scaled by average total assets (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, DP, AT). Rank stocks annually.
rationale: Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash flows are less persistent, and investors overweight reported earnings, leading to overpricing of high-accrual firms.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals)

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Change
construction: Compute capital expenditures (Compustat item CAPX) scaled by lagged net property plant and equipment (item PPENT), then take the change relative to the prior year's ratio. Sort annually after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Sharp increases in capital spending reflect managerial empire-building and overinvestment during optimistic periods, which subsequently disappoints, while capital discipline is rewarded.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining capex intensity)

name: Gross Margin Momentum
construction: Compute gross profit margin as (SALE minus COGS)/SALE for the most recent fiscal year and the prior fiscal year (Compustat items SALE, COGS). Take the difference. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Improving gross margins indicate strengthening competitive position and pricing power that predicts rising future profitability not yet fully impounded in prices.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving margins)

name: Dividend Initiation Yield Surprise
construction: Identify firms that paid zero dividends in the prior fiscal year but positive dividends in the most recent year (Compustat item DVC), and rank the initiators by the initiated dividend divided by price (CRSP). Long the initiating firms.
rationale: Dividend initiations credibly signal management confidence in sustainable cash flows and reduce free-cash-flow agency costs, mechanisms the market underreacts to.

name: Sales-to-Price Ratio
construction: Divide the most recent annual sales (Compustat item SALE) by market capitalization (CRSP price times shares outstanding) measured at fiscal year-end. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Sales are less subject to accounting distortion than earnings or book value, so a high sales-to-price ratio identifies cheaply valued firms with unrecognized turnaround potential.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high sales-to-price)

name: Volume-Adjusted Return Reversal
construction: For each stock compute the prior one-month return (CRSP) and the average daily turnover (volume divided by shares outstanding) over the same month. Within turnover terciles, rank by prior-month return. Long low-prior-return, high-turnover stocks.
rationale: Short-term price reversals reflect liquidity-driven overreaction, and high turnover amplifies the transient price pressure that subsequently reverses.
higher_returns_for: low prior-month returns combined with high turnover

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Contraction
construction: Estimate residual volatility from a market-model regression of daily returns over the prior 60 trading days (CRSP), then compute the change versus the prior 60-day window. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Declining idiosyncratic volatility signals resolution of firm-specific uncertainty and stabilizing fundamentals, which precedes positive revaluation as risk premia compress.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining idiosyncratic volatility)

name: Employee Productivity Growth
construction: Compute sales per employee as SALE divided by number of employees (Compustat items SALE, EMP), then take the year-over-year growth rate. Rank annually after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Rising sales per employee reflects improving operating efficiency and scalable competitive advantage that predicts future earnings growth underappreciated by investors.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising productivity)

name: Debt Reduction Signal
construction: Compute the change in total book leverage, defined as (DLC plus DLTT)/AT, from the prior fiscal year to the most recent (Compustat items DLC, DLTT, AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Active deleveraging signals management's private information about improving cash-flow prospects and lowers financial distress risk, a favorable change the market prices with a lag.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (largest leverage reductions)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in raw-materials plus work-in-process inventory (Compustat inventory detail) minus year-over-year growth in sales. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal-year data.
rationale: Rising input inventories not matched by sales signal weakening demand and overinvestment, which precede lower future earnings and returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growth below sales growth)

name: Accrual-to-Cashflow Quality
construction: Compute (net income minus operating cash proxy) scaled by average total assets, where operating cash proxy = net income minus change in non-cash working capital plus depreciation, using Compustat balance-sheet and income-statement items. Sort firms into deciles each June.
rationale: Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash are less persistent and tend to reverse, so high-accrual firms subsequently underperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accrual component of earnings)

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock
construction: Compute current-year capex scaled by total assets minus the trailing three-year average of the same ratio, using Compustat capital expenditure and asset data. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Abnormal spikes in investment reflect empire-building and diminishing marginal returns on capital, leading to lower subsequent stock returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (below-average investment shocks)

name: Gross Margin Trend
construction: Compute the change in gross margin (sales minus cost of goods sold, divided by sales) from the prior fiscal year to the current fiscal year using Compustat. Rank firms each June.
rationale: Improving gross margins indicate strengthening competitive position and pricing power that the market underreacts to, forecasting higher returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving gross margins)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that paid a cash dividend in the most recent CRSP distribution history but paid none in the prior 12 months; among dividend payers, also compute trailing 12-month dividend growth. Portfolio of initiators/high growers vs. non-payers.
rationale: Dividend initiations and increases credibly signal managerial confidence in sustainable cash flows, which the market prices with a lag.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (initiators and strong dividend growers)

name: Share Issuance Contraction
construction: Compute the log change in split-adjusted shares outstanding over the prior 12 months using CRSP shares outstanding and adjustment factors. Rank firms cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Net share issuance dilutes existing holders and often coincides with overvaluation and market-timing by managers; firms shrinking share count outperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (share count contraction/repurchasers)

name: Volatility of Turnover
construction: Compute the coefficient of variation of monthly share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the trailing 12 months. Sort firms into deciles each month.
rationale: Unstable trading intensity reflects heterogeneous, sentiment-driven investor demand and higher mispricing risk, associated with lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable turnover)

name: Earnings Announcement Return Clustering
construction: Sum the market-adjusted CRSP returns over the three-day windows around the last four quarterly earnings announcement dates (from Compustat report dates). Rank firms each quarter.
rationale: Positive cumulative reactions to recent earnings news reflect persistent positive information flow that continues due to underreaction.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (positive announcement-window returns)

name: Asset Turnover Improvement
construction: Compute sales divided by average total assets for the current fiscal year minus the same ratio in the prior year, using Compustat. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Rising asset efficiency signals better operating execution and future profitability growth that is not yet fully reflected in prices.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving asset turnover)

name: Leverage-Adjusted Profitability
construction: Compute operating income before depreciation divided by total assets, then subtract a penalty equal to (total debt / total assets) times a fixed cost-of-debt proxy; use Compustat items. Rank firms each June.
rationale: Firms generating high operating returns relative to their debt burden have safer, more sustainable earnings that the market undervalues.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high leverage-adjusted profitability)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE). Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal-year data.
rationale: Inventory accumulating faster than sales signals overproduction and weakening demand, presaging future markdowns and lower earnings that the market underappreciates.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual-to-Cash-Flow Ratio
construction: For each firm compute (net income minus operating cash flow) scaled by absolute operating cash flow. Operating cash flow approximated as net income (item NI) plus depreciation (item DP) minus change in non-cash working capital (change in ACT minus CHE, less change in LCT minus DLC). Rank annually.
rationale: Firms whose earnings are driven by accruals rather than cash have lower earnings quality and tend to see subsequent negative earnings surprises.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (cash-backed earnings)

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock
construction: Compute capital expenditures (item CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets (item AT), then take the deviation from the firm's own prior three-year average of the same ratio. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Sharp increases in investment relative to a firm's norm often reflect empire-building and overoptimism, leading to disappointing returns on the new capital.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (below-trend investment)

name: Gross Margin Trend
construction: Compute gross margin as (SALE minus COGS)/SALE for the current and prior fiscal year; the predictor is the change in gross margin year over year. Rank annually.
rationale: Improving gross margins indicate strengthening competitive position and pricing power not yet fully reflected in valuation.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving margins)

name: Employee Productivity Growth
construction: Compute sales per employee (SALE divided by item EMP) for current and prior year; predictor is the year-over-year growth rate. Rank stocks annually in June.
rationale: Rising output per worker signals operational efficiency gains and cost discipline that translate into higher future profitability.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising productivity)

name: Dividend Initiation/Growth Signal
construction: Compute the year-over-year change in total dividends paid (item DVT) scaled by lagged market equity (price times shares from CRSP). Rank cross-sectionally each June, giving special weight to firms moving from zero to positive dividends.
rationale: Managers raise or initiate dividends only when confident about sustainable future cash flows, a credible signal the market underreacts to.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (dividend increases/initiations)

name: Share Issuance Contraction
construction: Compute the annual percentage change in split-adjusted shares outstanding using CRSP (shares times cumulative adjustment factor). Rank stocks each June by this net issuance measure.
rationale: Net share repurchases signal managerial belief that equity is undervalued, while heavy issuance reflects overvaluation and dilutes future per-share returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (net repurchasers)

name: Return Volatility Change
construction: Compute daily return standard deviation (CRSP) over the most recent 3 months minus that over the prior 3-month window (months 4 to 6 back). Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: A recent decline in idiosyncratic volatility signals resolving uncertainty and stabilizing fundamentals, which precedes positive risk-adjusted returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (falling volatility)

name: Volume-Weighted Momentum Consistency
construction: Over months t-12 to t-2, count the fraction of months with positive returns, then interact this consistency score with cumulative return. Higher-turnover consistency is measured using CRSP monthly returns and volume. Rank monthly.
rationale: Momentum that arises from steady monthly gains reflects durable information diffusion, whereas momentum from a few large jumps mean-reverts.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (consistent positive momentum)

name: Debt Maturity Rollover Risk
construction: Compute short-term debt (item DLC) divided by total debt (DLC plus DLTT). Rank cross-sectionally each June, controlling for leverage level.
rationale: Firms reliant on short-term debt face refinancing and rollover risk; investors demand a premium for bearing this exposure to funding-market conditions.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (greater short-term debt reliance)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using annual data lagged at least 6 months. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Inventory accumulating faster than sales signals weak demand and future markdowns/write-offs, foreshadowing lower earnings and returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Order Backlog Intensity
construction: Order backlog (Compustat item OB) scaled by total assets (item AT), measured annually with a 6-month reporting lag. Sort stocks into quintiles.
rationale: A large backlog relative to firm size reflects contracted future revenue not yet in reported earnings, which the market underweights.

name: Cash Productivity
construction: Cash and short-term investments (item CHE) divided by market value of equity (price times shares outstanding). Rank cross-sectionally each June using fiscal year-end data lagged 6 months.
rationale: Firms with large cash relative to market cap are undervalued and possess financial flexibility to invest or return capital, earning higher subsequent returns.

name: Depreciation-to-Capex Gap
construction: Ratio of depreciation and amortization (item DP) to capital expenditures (item CAPX), annual data lagged 6 months. Higher ratio means the firm is under-investing relative to its asset consumption.
rationale: Firms whose capex lags depreciation are harvesting assets, often a value trap, whereas heavy reinvestors relative to depreciation may over-invest; the middle-to-high harvesting group tends to be cheap and mean-revert upward.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (harvesting firms)

name: Accrual-to-Cashflow Wedge
construction: Compute total accruals as change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, scaled by absolute operating cash flow (from funds statement items). Rank firms; those with the lowest accruals relative to cash flow are highest quality.
rationale: Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash flow are less persistent, so low-accrual firms deliver higher future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals)

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Change
construction: Year-over-year change in the ratio of SG&A expense (item XSGA) to sales (item SALE). Firms reducing SG&A intensity are improving operating leverage. Annual data lagged 6 months.
rationale: Declining overhead intensity signals margin expansion and disciplined management that the market prices slowly.

name: Return Convexity Around Zero
construction: Using 36 months of trailing monthly returns, count the fraction of months with returns within +/-2% of zero (low-volatility clustering) versus large moves. Rank firms by this stability fraction.
rationale: Stocks with returns tightly clustered near zero are neglected and low-beta, and neglect premia plus lottery-avoidance drive higher future returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (more stability)

name: Dividend Coverage Buffer
construction: Earnings per share (item EPS) minus dividends per share (item DVPSX) scaled by price, i.e., retained earnings yield. Annual data lagged 6 months. Sort into quintiles.
rationale: A wide gap between earnings and dividends means the payout is safe and internally funded growth is available, both of which support higher subsequent returns.

name: Asset Turnover Acceleration
construction: Second difference of asset turnover: (SALE/AT this year minus last year) minus (SALE/AT last year minus year before). Positive acceleration indicates improving asset utilization. Annual data lagged 6 months.
rationale: Accelerating efficiency reflects operational momentum in fundamentals that anticipates earnings surprises the market underreacts to.

name: Relative Trading Volume Contraction
construction: Ratio of average monthly share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) over the most recent 3 months to that over the prior 12 months. Values below one indicate declining attention. Use CRSP volume data.
rationale: Falling turnover marks investor neglect and reduced liquidity attention; such neglected stocks subsequently earn a premium as attention returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (contracting volume)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each fiscal year, compute year-over-year growth in inventory (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (item COGS). Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year with at least a 6-month reporting lag.
rationale: Inventory accumulating faster than sales signals weakening demand and future markdowns/writeoffs, a form of over-investment that the market underprices.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than COGS)

name: Accrued-to-Cash Earnings Ratio
construction: Compute the difference between reported net income (Compustat NI) and operating cash flow proxied as (net income + depreciation/amortization DP - change in non-cash working capital derived from balance-sheet items ACT, LCT, CHE, DLC). Scale by average total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag.
rationale: Earnings driven more by accruals than cash are less persistent and often reflect aggressive accounting, so high-accrual firms subsequently underperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (cash-heavy earnings)

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Reversal
construction: Compute capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) scaled by lagged net property plant and equipment (PPENT), then take the deviation of the current year's ratio from the firm's own prior three-year average. Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag.
rationale: Firms sharply increasing investment relative to their history tend to overexpand into declining opportunities, leading to lower subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining relative capex)

name: Gross Margin Momentum
construction: Compute gross margin as (SALE - COGS)/SALE for the most recent fiscal year and the year prior; take the change. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June by the year-over-year change with a reporting lag.
rationale: Improving gross margins signal strengthening competitive position and pricing power not yet fully reflected in prices.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising gross margin)

name: Idiosyncratic Return Volatility
construction: Each month, regress a stock's daily excess returns over the prior 60 trading days on the CRSP value-weighted market excess return; take the standard deviation of residuals as idiosyncratic volatility. Rank cross-sectionally at month end.
rationale: Under-diversified investors and limits to arbitrage cause high-idiosyncratic-volatility stocks to be overpriced and subsequently underperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low idiosyncratic volatility)

name: Dollar Trading Volume Illiquidity
construction: For each stock compute the average daily absolute return divided by daily dollar volume (price times shares traded) over the prior 12 months using CRSP daily data. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Illiquid stocks require a return premium to compensate investors for higher transaction costs and price impact.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (more illiquid stocks)

name: Share Issuance Change
construction: Compute the log growth in split-adjusted shares outstanding (CRSP shares times cumulative adjustment factor) over the prior 12 months. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Net share issuance reflects managers exploiting overvaluation and dilutes existing holders, predicting lower future returns; net repurchasers outperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (net repurchasers/low issuance)

name: Asset Turnover Improvement
construction: Compute asset turnover as SALE/average total assets (AT) for the latest fiscal year and prior year; take the change. Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag.
rationale: Rising asset efficiency signals improving operational productivity and future profitability that the market prices with delay.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving asset turnover)

name: 52-Week High Proximity
construction: Each month compute the ratio of a stock's current price to its highest closing price over the prior 52 weeks using CRSP data. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Anchoring on the 52-week high causes investors to under-react to good news near the high, so stocks close to their high subsequently outperform.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (price near 52-week high)

name: Financial Leverage Change
construction: Compute total debt (DLC + DLTT) scaled by total assets (AT) for the latest and prior fiscal year; take the change. Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag, controlling by industry.
rationale: Firms rapidly increasing leverage face heightened financial distress risk and constrained flexibility, predicting lower subsequent risk-adjusted returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (deleveraging firms)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each firm, compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using the most recent fiscal-year annual data lagged at least 4 months. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: When inventories build up faster than sales, it signals unsold goods and weakening demand that managers have not yet impaired, presaging future markdowns and lower earnings.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventories growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual-to-Cashflow Quality Gap
construction: Compute net income (item NI) minus operating cash flow proxied by (funds from operations, item FOPT, or NI plus depreciation item DP minus change in noncash working capital) scaled by average total assets (item AT). Rank firms each June on this accrual component.
rationale: Earnings composed largely of accruals rather than cash are less persistent and more prone to reversal, so high-accrual firms subsequently disappoint.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals relative to cash earnings)

name: Selling Expense Intensity Change
construction: Compute the change in SG&A expense (item XSGA) scaled by sales (item SALE) from the prior fiscal year to the current fiscal year, lagged at least 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: A rising ratio of overhead to sales flags deteriorating operating efficiency and margin pressure that the market underweights.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (falling or stable SG&A intensity)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that paid zero dividends (item DVC=0) in the prior fiscal year but positive dividends in the current year; among dividend payers, also rank on the percentage increase in dividends per share. Form portfolios each June.
rationale: Dividend initiations and large increases credibly signal management confidence in sustainable future cash flows, and the market underreacts to this signal.

name: Capital Intensity Reversal
construction: Compute capital expenditures (item CAPX) scaled by lagged property plant and equipment (item PPENT) or total assets, averaged over the trailing three fiscal years, then rank firms in the highest and lowest deciles. Rebalance annually in June.
rationale: Firms on prolonged aggressive investment sprees tend to overexpand and earn low subsequent returns as capacity outstrips profitable opportunities.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low sustained capital intensity)

name: Volume-Weighted Price Range Compression
construction: For each stock over the trailing 60 trading days from CRSP daily data, compute the ratio of the average daily high-low range (or absolute daily return) in the most recent 20 days to that in the prior 40 days, weighting by daily volume. Rank each month.
rationale: Compressing volatility on rising relative volume reflects accumulation and reduced information uncertainty, which precedes positive drift.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (contracting range)

name: Tax Burden Anomaly
construction: Compute effective tax rate as total income taxes (item TXT) divided by pretax income (item PI), and separately the change in this rate year over year, lagged 4 months. Rank firms with unusually low or declining effective tax rates.
rationale: Declining effective tax rates often reflect one-time benefits or aggressive tax positions that inflate current earnings unsustainably, leading to future reversals.
higher_returns_for: high (rising or normalizing effective tax rate) firms with sustainable earnings

name: Book Equity Momentum Consistency
construction: Compute the number of consecutive fiscal years (up to 5) in which book equity (item CEQ) grew, using annual Compustat data, and combine with the average annual growth rate. Rank firms each June.
rationale: Persistent, steady equity accumulation reflects durable profitability and reinvestment discipline that the market prices with a lag.
higher_returns_for: high values (consistent multi-year book equity growth)

name: Short-Term Reversal within Industry
construction: For each stock, compute the prior one-month return minus the equal-weighted average one-month return of its 2-digit SIC industry peers (industry-adjusted return). Rank monthly and buy losers, sell winners on this adjusted measure.
rationale: Idiosyncratic one-month overreaction relative to industry peers reverses as liquidity providers are compensated, isolating the reversal from industry momentum.

name: Receivables Aging Signal
construction: Compute change in accounts receivable (item RECT) growth minus sales (item SALE) growth year over year, scaled by total assets, lagged 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Receivables growing faster than sales indicate loosened credit terms or channel-stuffing that boosts current revenue but foreshadows collection problems and revenue reversals.
higher_returns_for: low values (receivables growing slower than sales)

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: For each fiscal year, compute the ratio of inventories (Compustat item INVT) to sales (SALE). Take the year-over-year change in this ratio, then subtract the prior-year change to obtain the second difference (acceleration). Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal-year data.
rationale: Accelerating inventory relative to sales signals unexpected demand weakness and future markdowns/write-offs that the market is slow to price, forecasting lower earnings and returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating or declining inventory-to-sales)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Using the past 5 fiscal years of Compustat data, compute gross margin as (SALE - COGS)/SALE each year. Measure the standard deviation of the annual gross margin. Rank firms by the inverse of this volatility (low volatility = high stability).
rationale: Firms with stable margins have durable competitive advantages and lower cash-flow uncertainty, which the market underprices relative to the persistence of their profitability.

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Change
construction: Compute capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged net PP&E (PPENT) or total assets (AT). Take the change in this ratio from the prior fiscal year. Sort stocks each June into portfolios based on this change.
rationale: Sharp increases in capital spending intensity often reflect empire-building and over-investment that erode future returns on capital, while spending restraint precedes stronger free cash flow.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining capex intensity)

name: Dividend Growth Persistence
construction: Using CRSP dividend history, compute the number of consecutive years (up to 5) in which cash dividends per share increased. Combine with the average annual dividend growth rate over that window. Rank firms into high vs low persistence groups.
rationale: Consistent dividend growth signals management confidence in sustainable cash flows and disciplines managers, a quality dimension not fully reflected in prices.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (persistent dividend growth)

name: Accruals-to-Cash-Flow Divergence
construction: Compute total accruals as the change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, using balance-sheet Compustat items (change in ACT minus CHE, minus change in LCT minus DLC, minus DP). Scale by average total assets. Separately compute operating cash flow proxy as net income minus accruals. Rank firms by the ratio of accruals to the magnitude of cash flow.
rationale: Earnings driven largely by accruals rather than cash are less persistent and tend to reverse, so high-accrual firms subsequently underperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (cash-backed earnings)

name: Volume-Adjusted Price Trend
construction: Over the trailing 6 months, compute the cumulative return weighted by the ratio of each month's dollar volume to average dollar volume, from CRSP monthly returns and volume. This emphasizes price moves that occurred on high volume.
rationale: Price trends confirmed by high trading volume reflect stronger informed conviction and continue, whereas low-volume moves are noise that reverse.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (strong volume-confirmed uptrend)

name: Asset Turnover Improvement
construction: Compute asset turnover as SALE / average total assets (AT) each fiscal year. Take the year-over-year change. Sort firms each June by the improvement in asset turnover.
rationale: Improving efficiency in generating sales from assets signals operational momentum and rising future profitability that the market underreacts to.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving asset turnover)

name: Debt Maturity Shift
construction: Compute the ratio of debt in current liabilities (DLC) to total debt (DLC + DLTT) each fiscal year. Take the change from the prior year. Rank firms by the increase in short-term debt reliance.
rationale: A shift toward short-term financing raises rollover and refinancing risk and often signals constrained access to long-term capital, foreshadowing distress and lower returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining short-term debt reliance)

name: Return Seasonality Consistency
construction: For each stock, using the past 5 years of CRSP monthly returns, compute the average return in the same calendar month as the upcoming month. Rank stocks by this historical same-month average return.
rationale: Firm-specific seasonal patterns in returns (from recurring information releases or demand cycles) persist and are not arbitraged away by the market.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (historically strong same-calendar-month returns)

name: R&D Growth Relative to Sales
construction: Compute research and development expense (XRD) scaled by sales (SALE). Take the growth in this ratio over the prior fiscal year, restricting to firms with positive R&D. Rank firms by the increase in R&D intensity.
rationale: Rising R&D intensity reflects investment in future innovation whose payoff is systematically underpriced because accounting expenses R&D immediately and analysts undervalue intangibles.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising R&D intensity)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using the most recent fiscal year annual data. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June after fiscal-year data is available.
rationale: Firms building inventory faster than sales are overproducing relative to demand, signaling future markdowns, margin pressure, and negative earnings surprises.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growth well below sales growth)

name: Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Quality
construction: Compute total accruals as (change in current assets minus change in cash) minus (change in current liabilities minus change in short-term debt minus change in taxes payable) minus depreciation (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, TXP, DP), scaled by average total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: High accruals reflect earnings driven by non-cash estimates that tend to reverse, so investors overvalue firms with low earnings persistence.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals relative to cash earnings)

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock
construction: Compute current-year capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) divided by average of the prior three years' capital expenditures, minus 1. Rank cross-sectionally each June using fiscal-year data.
rationale: Sharp increases in investment often reflect managerial overextrapolation of demand and empire-building, leading to poor subsequent returns as projects disappoint.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (firms cutting or holding capex flat)

name: Gross Margin Trend
construction: Compute gross margin as (SALE minus COGS)/SALE for the current fiscal year and the change in this ratio versus the prior fiscal year. Rank cross-sectionally each June on the change in gross margin.
rationale: Improving gross margins signal strengthening competitive position and pricing power that the market underweights in valuations.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving gross margins)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Using CRSP dividend distribution codes, flag firms that paid a cash dividend in the most recent quarter but paid none in the same quarter one year prior (dividend initiation or resumption). Form a long portfolio of these firms held for 12 months.
rationale: Dividend initiations credibly signal management confidence in sustainable cash flows and reduce free-cash-flow agency costs, information the market absorbs slowly.
higher_returns_for: firms that recently initiated or resumed dividends

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Decline
construction: Estimate idiosyncratic volatility as the standard deviation of residuals from a market-model regression of daily excess returns on the CRSP value-weighted index over the trailing 60 trading days. Compute the change versus the prior 60-day window. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Falling idiosyncratic volatility signals resolving uncertainty and improving information environment, which precedes positive re-rating.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (largest declines in idiosyncratic volatility)

name: Sales-to-Price Yield
construction: Compute annual sales (Compustat SALE) divided by market capitalization (CRSP price times shares outstanding) measured at fiscal year end. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Sales are less subject to accounting manipulation than earnings, so high sales-per-dollar-of-price identifies cheap firms whose top-line generating capacity is underpriced.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high sales-to-price)

name: Debt Reduction Signal
construction: Compute the year-over-year change in total debt (Compustat DLTT plus DLC) scaled by lagged total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Active deleveraging signals disciplined management and lowers financial distress risk and interest burden, improving future equity returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (largest debt reductions)

name: Turnover-Adjusted Momentum
construction: Rank stocks on trailing 6-month return (skipping the most recent month) within terciles of average monthly share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the same period. Favor high past-return, low-turnover stocks.
rationale: Low-turnover winners reflect underreaction to information among less-scrutinized stocks, producing stronger continuation than high-turnover, overly attended winners.
higher_returns_for: high past return combined with low share turnover

name: Asset Growth Restraint
construction: Compute the year-over-year percentage change in total assets (Compustat AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Rapidly expanding firms tend to overinvest and issue overpriced securities, while conservative asset growers subsequently outperform as expansion-driven mispricing corrects.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (slow or negative asset growth)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (COGS). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year data.
rationale: When inventories accumulate faster than sales-driven costs, it signals weakening demand and future markdowns that the market is slow to price, depressing subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than COGS)

name: Accruals-to-Cashflow Quality
construction: For each firm compute (Net Income minus Cash Flow from Operations) scaled by absolute Cash Flow from Operations, using Compustat funds-flow items. Where a cash flow statement is unavailable, derive operating cash flow from changes in working-capital balance sheet items minus depreciation. Sort annually.
rationale: Earnings composed largely of non-cash accruals are less persistent and more likely to reverse, so the market overvalues high-accrual firms.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (earnings backed by cash)

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock
construction: Compute current-year capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by average gross PP&E, minus the prior three-year average of the same ratio. Rank each June.
rationale: Firms sharply ramping investment tend to overinvest at cyclical peaks and subsequently deliver lower returns as free cash flow deteriorates.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (restrained investment)

name: Gross Profitability Scaled by Assets
construction: Compute (Revenue minus Cost of Goods Sold) divided by total assets (AT), using annual Compustat data. Sort firms cross-sectionally.
rationale: Gross profit is a cleaner measure of economic productivity than net income and is not yet reflected in valuations, so highly productive firms earn higher returns.

name: Net Share Issuance
construction: Compute the log growth in split-adjusted shares outstanding over the prior 12 months, using CRSP shares outstanding adjusted by the cumulative adjustment factor. Sort firms each month.
rationale: Managers issue shares when equity is overpriced and repurchase when underpriced, so net issuance is a signal of managerial market timing predicting lower future returns for issuers.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (net repurchasers)

name: Asset Growth
construction: Compute year-over-year percentage growth in total assets (Compustat AT). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Rapid balance-sheet expansion through acquisitions, investment, and working capital reflects overinvestment and diminishing marginal returns, leading to underperformance.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low asset growth)

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility from Market Model
construction: For each stock, estimate a market-model regression of daily excess returns on the CRSP value-weighted market return over the prior 60 trading days; take the standard deviation of residuals. Sort monthly.
rationale: If arbitrage is limited and investors underdiversify, high-idiosyncratic-risk stocks may be overpriced by lottery-seeking investors, earning lower subsequent returns.

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that changed from paying no dividend in the prior 12 months to paying a positive dividend in the most recent quarter (from CRSP distribution codes). Hold a long portfolio of initiators for 12 months.
rationale: Dividend initiation is a credible signal of sustainable earnings and disciplined capital allocation that the market underreacts to.

name: Sales-to-Price with Margin Filter
construction: Rank firms on annual Revenue divided by market capitalization, but interact this with operating margin (operating income before depreciation / sales). Go long high sales-to-price firms that also have above-median margins.
rationale: Cheap-on-sales firms are undervalued, but conditioning on healthy margins screens out value traps with structurally impaired profitability, sharpening the value premium.
higher_returns_for: high sales-to-price combined with high margins

name: 52-Week High Proximity
construction: Compute the ratio of current price to the highest price over the trailing 52 weeks using CRSP daily/weekly data. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: The 52-week high serves as an anchor; investors are reluctant to bid prices past it, causing underreaction to good news and continued outperformance for stocks near their highs.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (price near 52-week high)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each firm compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (item COGS), using annual data. Rank cross-sectionally at each fiscal year-end and hold for the subsequent 12 months, skipping 4 months to ensure data availability.
rationale: Inventory building that outpaces sales signals softening demand and future markdowns, so firms overaccumulating inventory relative to throughput subsequently disappoint.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than COGS)

name: Accrual-to-Cashflow Reliability Ratio
construction: Compute total accruals as (change in current assets minus change in cash) minus (change in current liabilities minus change in short-term debt) minus depreciation, all from the annual balance sheet and income statement (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, DP). Scale by absolute operating cash flow proxied by net income plus depreciation. Rank each June and hold 12 months.
rationale: Earnings driven heavily by accruals rather than cash are less persistent and tend to be overvalued, so high-accrual firms underperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (cash-backed earnings)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms whose most recent quarterly dividend per share (CRSP distribution files) exceeds zero when the same quarter one year earlier paid zero. Form a long portfolio of newly initiating firms and hold for 12 months, rebalancing monthly.
rationale: Dividend initiations credibly signal management's confidence in sustainable future cash flows and reduce free-cash-flow agency costs, leading to positive drift.

name: Asset Turnover Improvement
construction: Compute asset turnover as sales (SALE) divided by average total assets (AT) for the current and prior fiscal year; take the year-over-year change. Rank cross-sectionally each June, hold 12 months.
rationale: Rising asset turnover reflects improving operational efficiency and capacity utilization that the market underappreciates, forecasting higher profitability and returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving turnover)

name: Capital Expenditure Restraint
construction: Compute capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets (AT), then subtract the firm's own trailing three-year average of the same ratio. Rank each June and hold 12 months.
rationale: Firms sharply increasing investment above their historical norm tend to overinvest and destroy value, while restraint relative to history preserves returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (below-normal capex)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute gross margin ((SALE - COGS)/SALE) for each of the past five fiscal years and take its standard deviation. Rank cross-sectionally each June, hold 12 months.
rationale: Stable gross margins indicate durable pricing power and lower fundamental risk that is nevertheless mispriced given investor preference for growth volatility.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable margins)

name: Short-Term Debt Reliance Shift
construction: Compute the ratio of short-term debt (DLC) to total debt (DLC + DLTT) at fiscal year-end and take the year-over-year change. Rank each June and hold 12 months.
rationale: A rising reliance on short-term financing signals rollover and refinancing risk plus possible constrained access to long-term capital, predicting lower returns due to distress.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining short-term debt reliance)

name: Sales-Weighted Price Reversal
construction: Interact the prior-month return (CRSP) with the log of trailing-twelve-month sales (SALE) percentile: form the standard short-term reversal signal (negative prior-month return) but restrict the effect to large-sales firms by using prior-month return multiplied by an indicator for above-median sales. Rank monthly, hold one month.
rationale: Short-term reversal from liquidity provision is stronger among high-sales established firms where price moves are less informative and more likely temporary.
higher_returns_for: large-sales firms with low (most negative) prior-month returns

name: Retained Earnings Intensity
construction: Compute cumulative retained earnings (RE) scaled by total assets (AT) at fiscal year-end. Rank cross-sectionally each June and hold 12 months.
rationale: High retained-earnings intensity reflects a firm's accumulated internally-financed profitability and maturity, associated with lower risk of external financing distress and steady returns.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute selling, general and administrative expense (XSGA) divided by sales (SALE) and take the year-over-year change. Rank cross-sectionally each June and hold 12 months.
rationale: A falling SG&A-to-sales ratio signals improving operating leverage and cost discipline that predicts future earnings surprises and higher returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining SG&A ratio)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using the most recent fiscal year annual data. Rank stocks cross-sectionally into deciles each June.
rationale: When inventories build faster than sales, it signals weakening demand and future markdowns/write-offs, which the market underweights; firms depleting inventory relative to sales are experiencing stronger-than-expected demand.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Quality
construction: For each firm compute total accruals as the change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities (excluding short-term debt) minus depreciation, scaled by average total assets (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, DP, AT). Sort into deciles annually.
rationale: Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash flows are less persistent and tend to reverse, so the market overprices high-accrual firms.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals)

name: R&D Intensity Relative to Market Cap
construction: Compute research and development expense (Compustat item XRD) divided by end-of-year market capitalization (PRCC_F times CSHO). Set missing XRD to zero. Rank into deciles each June.
rationale: R&D creates intangible capital that GAAP expenses immediately, causing systematic undervaluation of research-intensive firms whose future payoffs are not yet in book value.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high R&D relative to market value)

name: Gross Profitability Yield
construction: Compute gross profit (Compustat item SALE minus COGS) divided by total assets (item AT), using most recent fiscal year. Sort into deciles annually and hold from June.
rationale: Gross profits are a cleaner measure of economic productivity than net income because they are less contaminated by accounting/financing noise; more productive firms earn higher returns for their risk.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high gross profitability)

name: Asset Growth Reversal
construction: Compute the annual percentage change in total assets (Compustat item AT year over year). Rank all firms into deciles each June.
rationale: Rapid asset expansion often reflects overinvestment and empire-building that destroys value and is later corrected; conservatively growing firms outperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low asset growth)

name: Net External Financing
construction: Sum net equity issuance (change in split-adjusted shares outstanding times price, or Compustat SSTK minus PRSTKC) and net debt issuance (change in total debt DLTT+DLC) over the prior fiscal year, scaled by average total assets. Sort into deciles annually.
rationale: Managers issue securities when their firm is overvalued and retire them when undervalued, so heavy external financing predicts low future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (net repurchasers/debt retirers)

name: Order-Backlog to Sales
construction: For firms reporting order backlog (Compustat item OB), compute backlog divided by annual sales (item SALE). Rank reporting firms into quintiles annually.
rationale: A large order backlog relative to current sales is a leading indicator of future revenue growth that the market underappreciates when it is buried in footnotes.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (large backlog relative to sales)

name: Volatility of Monthly Returns
construction: Compute the standard deviation of a stock's monthly returns (CRSP) over the trailing 36 months. Sort into deciles each month and hold value-weighted portfolios.
rationale: Idiosyncratically volatile, lottery-like stocks are overbought by underdiversified retail investors, leading to lower subsequent returns despite higher risk.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low return volatility)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that initiated or increased cash dividends per share (Compustat DVPSX or CRSP distribution codes) within the trailing 12 months versus those that cut/omitted. Form long-initiators, short-cutters portfolio, rebalanced monthly.
rationale: Dividend changes credibly signal management's private information about sustainable future cash flows, and the market underreacts to this signal.

name: Capital Turnover Efficiency
construction: Compute sales (Compustat SALE) divided by net property, plant and equipment (item PPENT), using most recent annual data. Sort into deciles each June, controlling within industry.
rationale: Firms that generate more sales per dollar of fixed capital use assets more efficiently and convert investment into cash flow faster, a quality dimension the market prices slowly.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high capital turnover)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each fiscal year, compute the growth rate of inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus the growth rate of cost of goods sold (item COGS), scaled by average total assets. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year data.
rationale: Inventory accumulating faster than sales signals weakening demand and future markdowns/write-offs, which the market underappreciates.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than COGS)

name: Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Persistence
construction: Decompose earnings into cash flow (operating income minus total accruals, where accruals = change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding short-term debt, minus depreciation) and accrual components from Compustat. Rank firms by the ratio of cash-flow earnings to total earnings.
rationale: Earnings dominated by accruals are less persistent and mean-revert, so investors overvalue high-accrual firms.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency
construction: Compute the ratio of change in sales (Compustat SALE) to change in selling, general and administrative expense (item XSGA) over the trailing fiscal year. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms generating more incremental sales per dollar of SG&A investment have improving operating leverage that the market is slow to price.

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that paid zero dividends (Compustat DVC = 0) in the prior fiscal year but a positive dividend in the current year, and measure the magnitude of the initiation relative to earnings. Form a portfolio of recent initiators.
rationale: Dividend initiation is a costly credible signal of sustainable future cash flows that the market only partially incorporates at announcement.

name: Volume-Weighted Price Range Compression
construction: For each stock, compute the average daily high-low range (from CRSP daily data) over the past 3 months divided by the same measure over the prior 9 months, weighting each day by its share volume. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Compressing volatility ranges under stable volume indicate information consolidation preceding directional moves; low-range-compression stocks are underpriced due to reduced investor attention.

name: Capital Expenditure Deceleration
construction: Compute the second difference of capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets: (CAPX_t - CAPX_{t-1}) - (CAPX_{t-1} - CAPX_{t-2}). Rank firms each June.
rationale: Firms decelerating capex avoid over-investment and free up cash, and the market misjudges the sustainability of prior investment binges.

name: Tax-Book Income Gap
construction: Estimate taxable income from the current tax provision (Compustat TXT minus deferred taxes TXDI, divided by the statutory rate) and compare to pre-tax book income (item PI). Compute the gap scaled by total assets. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: A large excess of book income over taxable income indicates aggressive accounting that predicts lower future earnings quality and returns.
higher_returns_for: low book-tax gap (book income close to taxable income)

name: Analyst-Free Neglect Premium
construction: Identify firms with zero I/B/E/S analyst coverage but positive earnings and above-median size within the small-cap tercile. Form a portfolio of these neglected but profitable firms.
rationale: Profitable firms lacking analyst coverage are under-followed and subject to informational neglect, earning a premium as coverage eventually arrives.

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute the standard deviation of annual gross margin (Compustat (SALE-COGS)/SALE) over the trailing 5 fiscal years. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms with stable gross margins have durable competitive positions and lower cash-flow risk that the market underprices relative to volatile-margin peers.

name: Debt Maturity Shortening
construction: Compute the change in the ratio of debt in current liabilities (Compustat DLC) to total debt (DLC + DLTT) over the trailing fiscal year. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A rising share of short-term debt reflects constrained financing access and refinancing risk that predicts lower future returns among such stressed firms.
higher_returns_for: low values (lengthening maturity / declining short-term reliance)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (COGS). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the prior fiscal year's annual data.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales throughput signals demand overestimation and impending markdowns, foreshadowing weaker future earnings and returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growth below COGS growth)

name: Accrual-Adjusted Profitability
construction: Take operating income before depreciation (OIBDP) minus the change in non-cash working capital (change in receivables plus inventory minus payables), scaled by average total assets (AT). Rank annually at fiscal year end.
rationale: Cash-backed profitability is more persistent and less subject to earnings management than accrual-laden profitability, so the market underprices cash-rich earners.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency
construction: Compute the ratio of sales (SALE) to selling, general and administrative expense (XSGA), then measure the one-year change in this ratio. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Rising sales per dollar of SG&A reveals improving operating leverage and marketing efficiency that analysts are slow to incorporate.

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum Overlay
construction: Identify firms that initiated or increased dividends per share (DVPSX) in the trailing 12 months and interact this with prior 6-month price momentum; form a composite score. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Dividend increases signal managerial confidence, and when combined with price strength the underreaction to the credible signal is largest.
higher_returns_for: high composite score (dividend increaser with positive momentum)

name: Capital Intensity Reversal
construction: Compute gross property, plant and equipment (PPEGT) divided by sales (SALE), and rank the two-year change. Sort firms each June on this change.
rationale: Firms rapidly increasing capital intensity tend to overinvest at cycle peaks, leading to depressed future returns as capacity outruns demand.

name: Earnings Announcement Volume Shock
construction: Measure average daily trading volume (CRSP) in the 3-day window around the most recent quarterly earnings announcement relative to the firm's trailing 60-day average volume. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Abnormal volume at earnings reflects information arrival and attention; high shock stocks experience persistent post-announcement drift.

name: Long-Term Debt Contraction
construction: Compute the one-year change in long-term debt (DLTT) scaled by total assets (AT). Rank firms annually at fiscal year end.
rationale: Voluntary deleveraging signals disciplined management and reduced financial risk that the market rewards with a delay.

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute gross margin ((SALE - COGS)/SALE) for each of the past five fiscal years and take the inverse of its standard deviation. Rank firms cross-sectionally.
rationale: Stable gross margins indicate pricing power and defensible competitive position, which is undervalued relative to volatile-margin firms.

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Trend
construction: Estimate residual volatility from a market-model regression using daily returns over each of the last two 6-month windows; compute the change (recent minus prior). Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Declining idiosyncratic volatility signals resolving firm-specific uncertainty, and prices rise as the risk discount unwinds.

name: Tax-Book Income Gap
construction: Estimate taxable income as total income tax expense (TXT) divided by the top statutory rate, then compute the ratio of this estimated taxable income to pretax book income (PI). Rank firms annually.
rationale: When book income substantially exceeds tax-inferred income, earnings quality is poor and future returns are lower; convergence signals conservative, sustainable earnings.
higher_returns_for: high values (taxable income high relative to book income)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using annual data. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June following fiscal year end.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns, forecasting lower operating performance and returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Selling Expense Intensity Change
construction: Compute the change in SG&A (Compustat item XSGA) scaled by sales (item SALE) from the prior fiscal year to the current fiscal year. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Rising selling and administrative intensity without commensurate revenue growth indicates deteriorating operating efficiency and empire-building, predicting lower returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining SG&A intensity)

name: Accrual-to-Cashflow Discordance
construction: Compute total accruals as change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding short-term debt (from Compustat balance-sheet items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC), scaled by average total assets (item AT). Combine with cash flow from operations proxied by net income (item NI) minus accruals. Rank on accruals for firms where cash flow is falling.
rationale: High accruals coupled with weakening cash flows reflect low earnings quality and mean-reverting profitability, forecasting lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals, strong cash flow)

name: Capital Expenditure Acceleration
construction: Compute capital expenditures (Compustat item CAPX) scaled by lagged property plant and equipment (item PPENT) in the current year minus the same ratio in the prior year. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Accelerating investment relative to existing asset base reflects overinvestment and lower marginal returns on capital, predicting lower average returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating capex)

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Gap
construction: Using CRSP monthly distribution codes, identify firms that paid a dividend in each of the last eight quarters. Among these, compute the trailing 3-year dividend growth rate and rank. Only include stable dividend payers.
rationale: Firms with persistent but stagnant dividends signal committed cash return and mature stability that the market underprices for its low risk of dividend cuts.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (stable payers with growing dividends)

name: Turnover-Adjusted Momentum
construction: Compute the past 6-month cumulative return (skipping the most recent month) from CRSP, then divide by the average monthly share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) over the same window. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Momentum accompanied by low turnover reflects underreaction with slower information diffusion, producing stronger continuation than high-turnover momentum.
