higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high momentum per unit turnover)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute gross margin (Compustat (SALE - COGS)/SALE) for each of the past five fiscal years; take the standard deviation of gross margin across those years. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms with stable gross margins possess durable pricing power and predictable cash flows that the market undervalues relative to volatile-margin firms.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable margins)

name: Financing Deficit Reliance
construction: Compute the sum of net equity issuance (change in item CEQ adjusted for retained earnings) and net debt issuance (change in items DLTT and DLC) scaled by total assets (item AT) over the fiscal year. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms funding operations through heavy external financing tend to overinvest and dilute owners, forecasting lower subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low external financing)

name: Analyst Coverage Scarcity Value
construction: Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts providing FY1 earnings estimates. Within size deciles (CRSP market cap), rank firms by residual coverage relative to size expectation; select firms with abnormally low coverage.
rationale: Stocks with sparse analyst coverage relative to their size are underfollowed and subject to slower information incorporation, earning a neglect premium.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low analyst coverage for their size)

name: Earnings Torpedo Sensitivity
construction: Using I/B/E/S, compute the dispersion of FY1 analyst estimates (standard deviation) scaled by absolute mean estimate, combined with the trailing sign of estimate revisions over 3 months. Rank cross-sectionally each month, favoring low dispersion with upward revisions.
rationale: Low forecast dispersion signals consensus clarity, and when paired with positive revisions indicates reliably improving fundamentals that are underpriced, while high dispersion firms face torpedo risk of large negative surprises.

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each fiscal year, compute the growth rate of inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus the growth rate of sales (item SALE), both year-over-year. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June after the reporting lag. Restrict to firms carrying meaningful inventory (exclude financials and pure service firms).
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns, while lean inventory relative to sales signals efficient operations and hidden demand strength.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growth well below sales growth)

name: Accrued Working Capital Intensity
construction: Compute the annual change in non-cash working capital = change in (current assets - cash) minus change in (current liabilities - short-term debt), scaled by average total assets, using Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, AT. Rank each June.
rationale: Large non-cash working-capital accruals reflect low-quality earnings that revert, so firms bloating working capital tend to underperform relative to those generating cash-backed earnings.

name: Capital Expenditure Acceleration
construction: Compute the ratio of current-year capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) to the three-year prior average of CAPX, then subtract the industry-median of this ratio. Rank each June after reporting lag.
rationale: Firms sharply accelerating investment tend to overinvest at cyclical peaks and subsequently disappoint, consistent with q-theory and empire-building frictions.

name: Gross Margin Trend Stability
construction: Using quarterly Compustat, compute gross margin = (SALEQ - COGSQ)/SALEQ for the last 8 quarters, then take the slope of a linear trend divided by the standard deviation of the quarterly margins. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: A steadily rising, low-volatility gross margin signals durable competitive positioning that the market underappreciates, while deteriorating margins forecast earnings shortfalls.

name: Trading Volume Trend Decay
construction: For each stock, compute average daily share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the most recent 3 months minus average turnover over months 4 through 12. Rank monthly.
rationale: Declining relative turnover reflects fading investor attention and neglect, and neglected stocks earn a premium as attention eventually re-normalizes.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining turnover)

name: Return Convexity to Market
construction: Regress a stock's monthly excess returns on market excess returns and squared market excess returns over trailing 60 months. Rank stocks by the coefficient on the squared term (coskewness proxy).
rationale: Stocks whose returns are convex in the market provide crash protection that investors overpay for, so low-convexity stocks command higher expected returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the convexity coefficient

name: Debt Maturity Concentration
construction: Compute the fraction of total debt maturing within one year = DLC / (DLC + DLTT) from Compustat. Rank each June, controlling for leverage quintile.
rationale: High reliance on short-term debt exposes firms to rollover and refinancing risk that is not fully priced, commanding a risk premium.

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Gap
construction: Identify firms that have paid dividends (CRSP distribution codes) for at least 3 consecutive years but whose payout ratio (dividends/earnings) declined in the most recent year while earnings rose. Flag this divergence as a binary/continuous signal.
rationale: Managers holding payout flat while earnings grow are conservatively signaling and building slack, and such quietly strengthening firms are underpriced relative to full-payout peers.
higher_returns_for: firms with rising retained earnings and lagging payout

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Compression
construction: Estimate idiosyncratic volatility as the standard deviation of residuals from a market-model regression over the trailing 12 months, and separately over the prior 12 months. Compute the ratio (recent/prior). Rank monthly.
rationale: A sharp compression in idiosyncratic volatility signals resolution of firm-specific uncertainty and stabilizing fundamentals that the market prices with delay.
higher_returns_for: low values of the ratio (volatility falling)

name: Analyst Coverage Scaled by Size
construction: Compute the number of I/B/E/S analysts issuing FY1 estimates divided by the log of market capitalization (CRSP price times shares). Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Low coverage relative to firm size indicates neglect and weaker information flow, and such under-followed stocks earn a premium as information asymmetry resolves.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (under-covered for their size)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each firm, compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using annual data lagged at least 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: When inventory builds faster than sales, it signals overproduction and weakening demand that management has not yet recognized, presaging future markdowns and disappointing earnings.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual Reversal Score
construction: Compute total accruals as (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding debt minus depreciation) scaled by average total assets, from Compustat balance-sheet items. Rank firms into deciles annually.
rationale: High accruals reflect low-quality, less persistent earnings that mean-revert, so market participants over-extrapolate accrual-driven earnings and are subsequently disappointed.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (low accruals)

name: Analyst Coverage Neglect
construction: Count the number of I/B/E/S analysts issuing FY1 EPS estimates in the most recent month, orthogonalized against log market capitalization via cross-sectional regression; take the residual. Low residual = neglected relative to size.
rationale: Stocks under-followed relative to their size are less efficiently priced and carry an information/neglect premium that resolves as coverage catches up.

name: Gross Profitability to Assets
construction: Compute (revenue minus cost of goods sold) from Compustat (SALE minus COGS) divided by total assets (AT), using annual data lagged 4+ months. Sort into deciles.
rationale: Gross profit is a cleaner measure of economic productivity than bottom-line earnings and captures profitable firms whose value is not fully reflected in price.

name: Cash Flow Volatility Discount
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly operating cash flow (approximated by net income plus depreciation, items IBQ + DPQ) scaled by total assets over the trailing 20 quarters. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Firms with more stable cash flows are less risky and easier to value, but investors under-price the persistence advantage of low-volatility cash generators.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable cash flows)

name: Order Flow Momentum from Volume-Weighted Signs
construction: Using daily CRSP data, sum signed daily dollar volume (volume times the sign of the daily return times price) over the trailing 3 months, scaled by average dollar volume. Rank into deciles monthly.
rationale: Persistent net buying pressure reflects gradual information incorporation and institutional accumulation that continues over subsequent months.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (positive net buying pressure)

name: Debt Maturity Rollover Risk
construction: Compute the ratio of debt in current liabilities (Compustat DLC) to total debt (DLC + DLTT). Rank firms; higher ratio means more short-term debt requiring near-term refinancing.
rationale: Firms with heavy near-term refinancing needs bear rollover and liquidity risk, demanding a return premium, especially in tightening credit environments.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (more short-term debt reliance)

name: Sales-to-Price Efficiency
construction: Compute annual sales (SALE) divided by market capitalization (CRSP price times shares). Sort into deciles, lagging accounting data 4+ months.
rationale: Sales are harder to manipulate than earnings, so a high sales-to-price ratio identifies fundamentally cheap firms whose revenue base the market undervalues.

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Reversal
construction: Compute capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets, then subtract the firm's trailing 3-year average of the same ratio. Rank the deviation cross-sectionally.
rationale: Abnormal investment surges tend to reflect empire-building and over-optimism that erode future returns on capital, disappointing investors.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (below-normal investment)

name: Earnings Announcement Return Persistence
construction: Cumulate the abnormal (market-adjusted) CRSP return over the 3-day window around each of the four most recent quarterly earnings announcements, and average them. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Consistently positive market reactions to earnings news reflect a pattern of positive surprises that the market underweights, leading to continued outperformance.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (consistently positive announcement reactions)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each fiscal year, compute the growth rate of inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus the growth rate of sales (item SALE), both year-over-year. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year data.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns, foreshadowing declining earnings; the market underreacts to this operational signal.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual-Adjusted Profitability
construction: Compute operating income (item OIADP) scaled by total assets (item AT), then subtract total accruals scaled by assets, where accruals = change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding short-term debt and taxes payable (Compustat balance-sheet items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, TXP). Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: High profitability backed by cash rather than accruals reflects sustainable earnings quality that the market values with a lag.

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Identify firms that paid zero cash dividends (item DVC=0) in the prior fiscal year but a positive dividend in the current year. Construct an indicator equal to 1 for such initiators, refreshed annually.
rationale: Dividend initiations credibly signal managers' confidence in persistent future cash flows, and prices adjust gradually to this reduction in information asymmetry.

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity Reversal
construction: Compute the ratio of capital expenditures (item CAPX) to total assets (item AT), and rank firms by the three-year average of this ratio each June.
rationale: Firms with persistently high investment tend to overexpand and subsequently earn lower returns as growth options fail to deliver, an agency-driven overinvestment effect.

name: Sales-per-Employee Trend
construction: Compute sales (item SALE) divided by number of employees (item EMP). Take the year-over-year change and rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Improving labor productivity is a leading indicator of margin expansion and operational efficiency that is only slowly incorporated into prices.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising sales per employee)

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Contraction
construction: For each stock, estimate the residual variance from a market-model regression of daily returns (CRSP) over months t-12 to t-7, and again over months t-6 to t-1. Compute the ratio of recent to prior residual variance. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: A decline in firm-specific volatility reflects resolving uncertainty and lower future risk premia demanded, but sluggish repricing yields temporarily elevated returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the ratio (contracting idiosyncratic volatility)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute gross margin = (SALE - COGS)/SALE for each of the past five fiscal years, then take the negative of the standard deviation of these margins. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Stable gross margins indicate durable competitive advantage and pricing power, characteristics associated with lower distress risk yet underpriced growth persistence.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (more stable margins)

name: Short-Term Debt Reliance
construction: Compute debt in current liabilities (item DLC) divided by total debt (DLC + DLTT). Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Heavy reliance on short-term financing exposes firms to rollover and refinancing risk, commanding a risk premium the market only partially prices.

name: Turnover-Adjusted Momentum
construction: Compute the 12-month past return (skipping the most recent month) using CRSP, then divide by the average monthly share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) over the same window. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Momentum accompanied by low trading activity reflects gradual information diffusion among inattentive investors and stronger continuation, whereas high-turnover momentum is more prone to reversal.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (strong momentum with low turnover)

name: Tax-Book Income Gap
construction: Estimate taxable income as the current tax expense (item TXT minus deferred taxes item TXDI) grossed up by the statutory corporate tax rate, then subtract this from pretax book income (item PI). Scale the difference by total assets and rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A large excess of book income over estimated taxable income indicates aggressive accounting or non-recurring items that overstate earnings quality, predicting lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (small book-tax gap)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute the year-over-year growth in raw-materials inventory minus the year-over-year growth in finished-goods inventory, using Compustat inventory detail items (INVRM, INVFG). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal-year data.
rationale: Rising raw-materials relative to finished-goods inventory signals management's private expectation of future demand and production ramp-up, whereas finished-goods buildup signals unsold output.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (raw-materials growth exceeding finished-goods growth)

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Change
construction: Compute SG&A expense (Compustat XSGA) scaled by sales for the current fiscal year minus the same ratio for the prior year. Rank firms by the change in this ratio.
rationale: Firms achieving falling selling-cost intensity are gaining operating leverage and competitive scale that the market prices slowly.

name: Trade Credit Extension Ratio
construction: Compute accounts receivable (RECT) scaled by sales, then take the change from the prior fiscal year, netted against the change in accounts payable (AP) scaled by cost of goods sold. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Aggressive extension of receivables relative to payables can inflate current sales through channel-stuffing and predicts subsequent reversals in earnings.
higher_returns_for: low values (firms tightening receivables relative to payables)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Flag firms that paid a common dividend (DVC>0) in the current fiscal year but paid zero in the prior year. Within initiators, rank by the prior-6-month return. Long the highest-momentum initiators.
rationale: Dividend initiation is a costly signal of durable earnings, and combining it with price momentum isolates initiations the market underreacts to.
higher_returns_for: high values (recent initiators with strong prior momentum)

name: Capital Intensity Reversal
construction: Compute gross PP&E (PPEGT) scaled by total assets. Compute the 3-year change in this ratio. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by the change.
rationale: Firms sharply increasing capital intensity tend to over-invest at cyclical peaks, and the market fails to discount subsequent low returns on new capital.

name: Turnover Acceleration
construction: Compute average monthly share turnover (volume/shares outstanding from CRSP) over the most recent 3 months minus the average monthly turnover over the prior 9 months. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Accelerating turnover reflects rising investor disagreement and speculative attention, which is associated with overpricing and lower subsequent returns.

name: Tax-Book Income Gap
construction: Estimate taxable income as current federal tax expense (TXFED) divided by the statutory rate (0.35), then compute pretax book income (PI) minus estimated taxable income, scaled by total assets. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A large excess of book income over taxable income indicates aggressive accruals and lower-quality earnings likely to reverse.

name: Volatility of Analyst-Free Fundamentals Ratio
construction: Compute the trailing 5-year standard deviation of annual return-on-assets (net income NI / total assets AT), scaled by mean ROA over the same window. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms with unstable fundamental profitability are harder to value and carry a distress/uncertainty premium under-recognized in prices.

name: Equity Issuance Absorption
construction: Compute the 1-year growth in split-adjusted shares outstanding from CRSP, then interact with the firm's book-to-market rank. Long low-issuance firms among value stocks; short high-issuance firms among value stocks.
rationale: Share issuance dilutes returns and is especially informative among value firms where managers exploit temporary overvaluation of otherwise cheap stocks.
higher_returns_for: low values (low share-count growth, particularly within value)

name: Seasonal Earnings Persistence
construction: Regress the most recent four quarterly earnings surprises (actual quarterly EPS from Compustat quarterly EPSPXQ minus same-quarter-prior-year EPS) and take the sum of the two most recent same-fiscal-quarter surprises. Rank firms by this same-quarter cumulative surprise.
rationale: Some firms exhibit calendar-quarter-specific earnings strength that recurs, and the market underreacts to this seasonal component of earnings news.

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each firm, compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), measured at fiscal year end and matched to returns with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Inventories accumulating faster than sales signal overproduction and weak future demand, foreshadowing markdowns and earnings disappointments.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growth below sales growth)

name: Depreciation-to-CapEx Aging
construction: Compute the ratio of accumulated depreciation (Compustat item DPACT) to gross PP&E (item PPEGT), and separately depreciation expense (item DP) to capital expenditures (item CAPX). Average the two into an asset-aging score, updated annually with a 6-month reporting lag.
rationale: Firms with old, underinvested asset bases face lower reinvestment needs and higher free-cash-flow yields, and the market underprices this hidden efficiency.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (older asset base, low reinvestment)

name: Selling-Expense Operating Leverage
construction: Compute SG&A expense (Compustat item XSGA) scaled by sales (item SALE), then take the change in this ratio versus the prior fiscal year. Combine with total-asset turnover (SALE/AT). Rank on the interaction of high SG&A intensity and improving turnover, lagged 6 months.
rationale: High fixed selling-cost bases create operating leverage; when turnover improves, earnings rise disproportionately, a mispriced nonlinearity.
higher_returns_for: high SG&A intensity combined with improving asset turnover

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Gap
construction: Using CRSP distribution codes, identify firms that raised their regular cash dividend in each of the prior three fiscal years. Score = number of consecutive annual increases. Match to monthly returns.
rationale: A multi-year record of dividend increases signals durable cash-flow quality that investors extrapolate too weakly, leaving positive drift.
higher_returns_for: high values (longer streak of consecutive dividend increases)

name: Share-Count Stability
construction: Compute the standard deviation of month-end shares outstanding (CRSP SHROUT) over the trailing 36 months, scaled by mean shares. Lower dispersion indicates absence of dilution and equity issuance.
rationale: Firms that neither dilute nor repeatedly issue equity tend to be self-financing and undervalued; volatile share counts flag financing distress or empire-building.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable share count)

name: Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Momentum
construction: Compute standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) from Compustat quarterly EPS (item EPSPXQ) using a seasonal-random-walk expectation, then subtract the current-quarter total accruals scaled by assets (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, from the funds-flow statement). Rank on the cash-based SUE.
rationale: Earnings surprises backed by cash rather than accruals are more persistent, so cash-adjusted momentum predicts stronger post-announcement drift.

name: Trading-Volume Trend Reversal
construction: For each stock compute average daily dollar volume (CRSP price times volume) in the most recent month divided by average daily dollar volume over the trailing 12 months. Rank cross-sectionally, monthly.
rationale: A sharp recent surge in relative volume often reflects unsustainable attention and overpricing that subsequently reverses.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (recent volume below its longer-run norm)

name: Book Leverage Change Quality
construction: Compute year-over-year change in the ratio of total debt (Compustat DLTT + DLC) to total assets (AT). Rank firms; those reducing leverage while maintaining or growing assets score highest. Lag 6 months.
rationale: Voluntary deleveraging signals management confidence and reduced financial risk that the market recognizes only gradually.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining book leverage)

name: Gross-Margin Trend Stability
construction: Compute gross margin ((SALE - COGS)/SALE) for each of the past four fiscal years, then take the trailing four-year slope minus its standard deviation. High score means steadily rising, low-volatility margins. Lag 6 months.
rationale: Consistently expanding margins indicate widening competitive advantage that investors underweight relative to headline earnings.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising, stable gross margins)

name: Idiosyncratic Return Skewness
construction: For each stock, regress daily excess returns on the market over the trailing 12 months and compute the skewness of the regression residuals. Rank cross-sectionally, monthly.
rationale: Investors overpay for lottery-like positive-skewness stocks, so negatively skewed idiosyncratic returns command a premium.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (negative idiosyncratic skewness)

name: R&D Growth Acceleration
construction: Using Compustat annual data, compute R&D expense (XRD) scaled by total assets (AT). Calculate the year-over-year change in this ratio, then the change in that change (second difference) over three consecutive fiscal years. Rank stocks cross-sectionally at each June formation date using data lagged at least six months.
rationale: Accelerating R&D intensity signals firms ramping investment in growth options that the market underappreciates due to expensing of R&D and slow updating of expectations about intangible payoffs.
higher_returns_for: high values of R&D growth acceleration

name: Inventory-to-Sales Divergence
construction: From Compustat, compute the growth rate of inventory (INVT) minus the growth rate of sales (SALE) over the trailing fiscal year. Standardize cross-sectionally. Form portfolios at June using data lagged six months.
rationale: When inventories grow faster than sales, it signals demand overestimation and future markdowns/writeoffs, so such firms underperform, while firms drawing down inventory relative to sales face improving operations.
higher_returns_for: low values (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Order-Backlog Intensity
construction: From Compustat, take order backlog (OB) divided by total assets (AT), measured at fiscal year-end. Rank stocks cross-sectionally among firms reporting backlog. Form portfolios in June with a six-month reporting lag.
rationale: A large order backlog relative to assets represents contracted-but-unrecognized future revenue that is not yet reflected in earnings-based valuation, leading to positive future returns as the backlog converts to sales.

name: Dividend Initiation Consistency Streak
construction: Using CRSP dividend distribution codes, count the number of consecutive years a firm has paid a dividend without a cut, then interact with the dividend yield relative to its own five-year average. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: A long uninterrupted dividend streak combined with a yield above the firm's own history signals financial discipline and temporary undervaluation, capturing a quality-plus-value effect not yet formalized.
higher_returns_for: high streak with elevated relative yield

name: Return Seasonality in Fiscal-Report Months
construction: For each stock, identify the calendar months in which it historically reported earnings (from Compustat report dates over the prior five years). Compute the average excess return the stock earned in those same-report months historically, cross-sectionally ranked.
rationale: Firms with recurring positive returns in their information-release months exhibit persistent under-reaction to predictable seasonal information flow, generating repeatable outperformance.

name: Asset Turnover Momentum
construction: Compute asset turnover as sales (SALE) divided by average total assets (AT) for the trailing year and the prior year from Compustat. Take the change in asset turnover. Rank cross-sectionally at June with a six-month lag.
rationale: Improving asset utilization is a leading indicator of margin expansion and operating efficiency that the market prices with a delay, driving positive future returns.

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Trend
construction: Estimate monthly idiosyncratic volatility as the standard deviation of market-model residuals from daily CRSP returns each month. Compute the slope of a regression of monthly IVOL on time over the trailing 12 months. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Rising idiosyncratic volatility signals increasing information uncertainty and deteriorating fundamentals, so firms with rising IVOL trends subsequently underperform relative to those with declining uncertainty.

name: Share Issuance Acceleration
construction: From CRSP, compute the change in split-adjusted shares outstanding over the trailing 12 months, and separately over the 12 months before that. Take the difference (acceleration in net issuance). Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Accelerating share issuance indicates managers exploiting rich equity valuations and dilution not yet impounded, extending the issuance anomaly to its second-order dynamics.

name: Cash Productivity
construction: Compute sales (SALE) divided by cash and short-term investments (CHE) from Compustat, measured at fiscal year-end. Rank cross-sectionally at June with a six-month lag, within industry.
rationale: Firms generating more sales per dollar of cash hold less idle capital and deploy resources efficiently; excess cash hoards signal agency problems and lower future returns.

name: Analyst Coverage Change Relative to Size
construction: Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts issuing FY1 estimates in the current month minus the count 12 months prior, then divide by the log of market capitalization from CRSP. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Rising analyst attention relative to firm size predicts increasing institutional demand and information incorporation, driving prices upward as coverage-driven visibility expands the investor base.

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Using Compustat annual data, compute the year-over-year growth rate of inventories (item INVT) minus the year-over-year growth rate of sales (item SALE). Form the measure at fiscal year end and hold from June of year t+1. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: When inventory builds faster than sales, it signals overproduction and weak future demand, leading to markdowns and disappointing earnings that the market underappreciates.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Order Backlog Intensity
construction: From Compustat, take order backlog (item OB) scaled by total assets (item AT) at fiscal year end. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A large order backlog relative to assets reflects strong committed future demand that is not yet capitalized in current earnings, so backlog-rich firms are undervalued.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Shift
construction: Compute the change in selling, general and administrative expense (item XSGA) divided by sales (item SALE) from the prior fiscal year to the current fiscal year. Measure = SGA/Sales(t) - SGA/Sales(t-1). Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: A rising SG&A-to-sales ratio signals deteriorating operating discipline and margin pressure that predicts lower future profitability and returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining SG&A intensity)

name: Trading Volume Acceleration
construction: Using CRSP daily data, compute average daily dollar volume over the most recent month divided by average daily dollar volume over the prior 11 months. Rank cross-sectionally each month-end.
rationale: A sharp acceleration in trading activity reflects heightened investor attention and speculative interest that tends to reverse, producing lower subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating volume)

name: Idiosyncratic Return Skewness
construction: Regress daily stock excess returns on the market excess return over the trailing 12 months using CRSP data; compute the skewness of the daily residuals. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Investors overpay for lottery-like stocks with positive idiosyncratic skewness, leading such stocks to earn lower average returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (negative idiosyncratic skewness)

name: Capital Expenditure Persistence
construction: From Compustat, compute the ratio of current capital expenditure (item CAPX) to the three-year trailing average of capital expenditure, all scaled by lagged total assets. Measure captures a spike above the firm's own investment norm. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Investment spikes above a firm's historical norm reflect managerial overextrapolation of demand and empire building, which the market overvalues and subsequently corrects.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (investment below own trend)

name: Gross Margin Momentum
construction: Compute gross profit (item SALE minus item COGS) divided by sales for the current and prior fiscal year; the measure is the year-over-year change in gross margin. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Improving gross margins reflect strengthening pricing power and cost control that persist and are only slowly incorporated into prices.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving gross margin)

name: Dividend Initiation Surprise Drift
construction: Using CRSP distribution codes and Compustat, flag firms that pay a cash dividend in the current fiscal year but paid none in the prior three years. Assign an indicator and hold long positions for 12 months after the announcement.
rationale: Dividend initiations credibly signal management confidence in sustainable cash flows, and the market underreacts to this signal, producing a post-initiation drift.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (recent dividend initiators)

name: Accrual Volatility
construction: Compute total accruals (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding debt, minus depreciation) scaled by average total assets for each of the past five fiscal years; the measure is the standard deviation of these annual accruals. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: High volatility of accruals indicates low earnings quality and greater information risk, so investors demand higher returns to hold such stocks.

name: Relative Bid-Ask Spread Trend
construction: Using CRSP daily closing bid and ask (or NASDAQ quotes), compute the average relative quoted spread ((ask-bid)/midpoint) over the recent quarter minus that over the prior year. Measure is the change in liquidity. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Stocks whose spreads are narrowing are experiencing improving liquidity, and the liquidity premium declines gradually, so worsening-liquidity stocks require compensation via higher future returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (widening spreads)

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (item COGS), using annual data with a 6-month reporting lag. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Inventory building that outpaces sales growth signals demand overestimation by management and future markdowns, leading to lower subsequent earnings and returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventories growing slower than COGS)

name: Accrued Interest Burden Ratio
construction: Interest expense (Compustat item XINT) scaled by total debt (item DLTT + DLC) at fiscal year end, then take the change in this implied cost-of-debt from year t-1 to year t, with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: A rising effective borrowing cost reflects deteriorating creditworthiness perceived by lenders before it is fully priced by equity holders, predicting lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the change in implied cost of debt

name: Selling Intensity Ramp
construction: SG&A expense (Compustat item XSGA) divided by sales (item SALE); compute the two-year change in this ratio with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms sharply increasing selling/administrative spending relative to revenue often mask declining organic demand, foreshadowing margin compression and weak returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the two-year change in SG&A/sales

name: Dividend Coverage Stability
construction: Compute the ratio of operating cash flow (Compustat item OANCF, or income before extraordinary items + depreciation if unavailable) to common dividends paid (item DVC), averaged over the trailing three fiscal years, restricted to dividend payers. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Firms whose cash flows comfortably and consistently cover dividends are financially resilient and less prone to dividend cuts that trigger price declines.
higher_returns_for: high values of the coverage ratio

name: Volume-Weighted Price Reversal
construction: For each stock, regress daily returns on daily share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) over the prior 60 trading days using CRSP data; take the estimated slope coefficient. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: A strongly negative return-volume slope indicates transient liquidity-driven price pressure that mean-reverts, so these stocks earn higher subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: low (most negative) values of the slope

name: Earnings Announcement Volatility Premium
construction: Using CRSP daily data, compute the ratio of the average absolute return in the 3-day window around the last four quarterly earnings announcements to the average absolute daily return in non-announcement periods over the same year. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Stocks with disproportionately large announcement-period moves carry elevated information-event risk that investors demand compensation to bear.

name: Capital Intensity Shift
construction: Gross property, plant & equipment (Compustat item PPEGT) scaled by total assets (item AT); compute the year-over-year change with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Rapid increases in fixed-asset intensity reflect aggressive expansion that historically precedes overcapacity and disappointing returns on capital.
higher_returns_for: low values of the change in capital intensity

name: Tax-Book Income Gap
construction: Estimate taxable income as current tax expense (Compustat item TXT - deferred taxes TXDI) divided by the statutory rate (35%), then compute the difference between pretax book income (item PI) and this estimated taxable income, scaled by total assets. Rank cross-sectionally with a 6-month lag.
rationale: A large excess of book income over taxable income signals aggressive accounting or low-quality earnings that reverse and depress future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the book-minus-taxable income gap

name: Order-Flow Persistence Signature
construction: Compute the first-order autocorrelation of daily signed volume (return sign times volume) over the prior 120 trading days using CRSP data. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: High persistence in signed order flow indicates ongoing informed accumulation, and such stocks continue to drift in the direction of that flow.
higher_returns_for: high values of signed-volume autocorrelation combined with positive recent flow

name: Receivables Quality Deterioration
construction: Compute accounts receivable (Compustat item RECT) divided by sales (item SALE), and take the two-year change with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Receivables growing faster than sales suggest channel-stuffing or loosening credit terms that overstate current revenue and forecast negative earnings surprises.
higher_returns_for: low values of the two-year change in receivables/sales

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: For each firm, compute the ratio of inventories (Compustat INVT) to sales (SALE) at fiscal year end. Then take the change in this ratio from t-2 to t-1 minus the change from t-3 to t-2, i.e. the second difference (acceleration) of the inventory-to-sales ratio. Rank cross-sectionally each June using the most recent annual data.
rationale: Accelerating inventory buildup relative to sales signals demand disappointment and future markdowns/writeoffs that the market underappreciates, while decelerating inventory signals tightening supply and pricing power.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating inventory-to-sales)

name: Order Backlog Yield
construction: Take reported order backlog (Compustat OB) scaled by market capitalization (PRCC_F times CSHO) at fiscal year end. Rank firms cross-sectionally; firms with no reported backlog are excluded. Reform portfolios each June.
rationale: Order backlog represents contracted future revenue not yet in reported earnings; a high backlog-to-price ratio reflects undervalued future cash flows that the market prices with delay.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high backlog yield)

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute the ratio of SG&A expense (Compustat XSGA) to sales (SALE) for each of the last three fiscal years. Fit the slope of this ratio over time (or take the two-year change). Standardize cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A declining SG&A-to-sales ratio indicates improving operating leverage and management discipline that predicts positive future earnings surprises not yet capitalized.

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Score
construction: Using CRSP distribution codes, identify firms that initiated or resumed a cash dividend within the trailing 12 months, and scale the annualized initiated dividend by prior-year earnings (Compustat IB). Rank initiators by this payout intensity each month; non-initiators score zero.
rationale: Dividend initiations credibly signal management confidence in sustainable earnings, and the size of the initiation relative to earnings sharpens the signal; the market underreacts to this commitment.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (large-intensity initiators)

name: Cash Flow Volatility Discount
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly operating cash flow (Compustat OANCF, or IB plus depreciation DP for quarters) scaled by average total assets (AT) over the trailing 12–16 quarters. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Firms with more volatile cash flows are harder to value and carry higher distress/financing risk, so they must offer a return premium to compensate holders.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high cash flow volatility)

name: Analyst Coverage Change Momentum
construction: Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts issuing FY1 EPS estimates in the current month versus 12 months prior. Compute the net change in coverage. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Rising analyst coverage reflects growing institutional attention and improving information flow that precedes positive price drift as the investor base broadens.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (increasing coverage)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute gross margin (SALE minus COGS, divided by SALE) for each of the last five fiscal years and take the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by mean). Rank cross-sectionally each June; low CV means stable margins.
rationale: Stable gross margins indicate durable competitive advantage and lower fundamental risk, and the market underprices the earnings predictability such firms provide.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable margins)

name: Debt Maturity Refinancing Pressure
construction: Compute the ratio of debt in current liabilities (Compustat DLC) to total debt (DLC plus DLTT) at fiscal year end, interacted with leverage (total debt over AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms with a large fraction of short-term debt face near-term rollover and refinancing risk; this exposure commands a risk premium especially when overall leverage is high.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high short-term refinancing pressure)

name: Tax Expense Surprise
construction: Compute the effective tax rate (Compustat TXT divided by pretax income PI) for the current year and the trailing three-year average. Take the current rate minus the average. Rank cross-sectionally each June; unusually low current rate is a positive score.
rationale: An abnormally low current-year effective tax rate often reflects favorable, persistent operating changes or credits that the market treats as transitory, causing subsequent positive earnings surprises.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (effective tax rate below its own history)

name: Capital Expenditure Deceleration
construction: Compute capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) scaled by lagged property, plant and equipment (PPENT). Take the change in this investment rate from the prior year to the current year. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms cutting their investment rate free up cash flow and signal capital discipline, and the market underappreciates the resulting improvement in free cash flow yield relative to firms ramping investment.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating capex)

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: For each firm, compute the ratio of inventories (Compustat item INVT) to sales (SALE) at fiscal year-end. Measure the change in this ratio over the most recent year minus the change over the prior year (a second difference, i.e., acceleration). Form portfolios sorted on this acceleration measure, updated annually with a 6-month reporting lag.
rationale: Accelerating inventory relative to sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns, which the market underappreciates until earnings disappoint.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating/shrinking inventory relative to sales)

name: Selling Expense Efficiency
construction: Compute the ratio of selling, general and administrative expense (Compustat XSGA) to gross profit (SALE minus COGS). Rank firms cross-sectionally each year, using a 6-month lag. The predictor is the level of this ratio.
rationale: Firms converting each dollar of gross profit into more selling overhead are managerially inefficient; efficient firms (low ratio) generate higher future returns as profitability persists and is undervalued.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (lean SG&A relative to gross profit)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Identify firms that moved from zero dividends in the prior fiscal year to positive cash dividends (Compustat DVC) in the current year. Among these initiators, hold for the subsequent 12 months. Compare against non-initiators. Updated quarterly from dividend declaration data (CRSP distributions).
rationale: Dividend initiation is a costly credible signal of durable future cash flows that the market incorporates only gradually, generating post-initiation drift.

name: Capital Expenditure Volatility
construction: Compute the standard deviation of the ratio of capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) to total assets (AT) over the trailing 5 fiscal years. Sort firms into portfolios on this volatility, annually with a 6-month lag.
rationale: Erratic investment reflects poor managerial discipline and higher operating uncertainty; stable investors compound value more reliably, so low volatility earns higher risk-adjusted returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable capital spending)

name: Order Backlog to Assets
construction: Compute reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) divided by total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally each year with a 6-month reporting lag. Restrict to firms that report backlog.
rationale: Order backlog is a forward-looking indicator of contracted future sales not yet in earnings; the market underweights this off-balance-sheet demand signal.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (large backlog relative to assets)

name: Trading Volume Trend Divergence
construction: For each stock, regress daily log dollar trading volume on a time trend over the trailing 12 months. The predictor is the sign and magnitude of the trend slope, orthogonalized against past return momentum. Sort monthly.
rationale: Declining trading interest amid stable prices signals waning investor attention and forthcoming neglect-premium, while rising volume predicts overextension; declining-volume neglected stocks earn higher subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining trading-volume trend)

name: Accrual Reversal Consistency
construction: Decompose total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, from balance-sheet items) for each of the past 4 years. Count how many of those years had negative (income-decreasing) accruals. The predictor is this consistency count.
rationale: Firms that persistently report conservative (negative) accruals have higher earnings quality that the market fails to fully price, yielding higher future returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (consistently conservative accruals)

name: R&D Growth Relative to Peers
construction: Compute research and development expense (Compustat XRD) growth over the trailing year, then subtract the median R&D growth of firms in the same 2-digit SIC industry. Sort annually with a 6-month lag; set missing R&D to zero.
rationale: Firms outgrowing industry peers in innovation investment build undervalued intangible capital whose payoff is delayed and underpriced by the market.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (above-peer R&D growth)

name: Return Skewness Asymmetry
construction: Estimate the skewness of daily returns over the trailing 6 months for each stock. Sort cross-sectionally monthly into portfolios.
rationale: Investors overpay for lottery-like positively skewed stocks, driving their prices up and expected returns down, while negatively skewed stocks carry a discount and higher subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (negative return skewness)

name: Financing Gap Signal
construction: Compute the firm's free cash flow deficit: capital expenditures (CAPX) plus dividends (DVC) minus operating cash flow (approximated by income before extraordinary items IB plus depreciation DP), scaled by total assets (AT). Sort annually with a 6-month lag.
rationale: Firms that internally fund investment (low or negative financing gap) avoid dilutive equity issuance and costly debt, signaling financial strength that is rewarded with higher returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (internally-funded firms with no financing gap)

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: Compute inventory (Compustat item INVT) scaled by sales (SALE) for the two most recent fiscal years. Take the year-over-year change in this ratio, then subtract the prior year's change to get the second difference (acceleration). Sort stocks cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Accelerating inventory relative to sales signals demand deterioration and future markdowns that the market underprices, foreshadowing negative earnings surprises.
higher_returns_for: low values of inventory-to-sales acceleration (stable or declining inventory buildup)

name: Order Backlog Intensity
construction: Use Compustat order backlog (item OB) divided by average total assets (AT). Rank firms cross-sectionally each year among firms reporting order backlog; missing OB treated as separate group.
rationale: A large reported backlog reflects locked-in future revenue that analysts and investors discount too heavily due to uncertainty about conversion timing, creating undervaluation.

name: Advertising Persistence Ratio
construction: Compute advertising expense (Compustat item XAD) scaled by sales for each of the last three fiscal years. Measure persistence as the minimum of the three annual ratios divided by the maximum. Rank cross-sectionally among firms reporting XAD.
rationale: Firms that sustain steady advertising build durable intangible brand capital that is expensed rather than capitalized, so their true asset base and future profitability are understated.

name: Dividend Initiation-to-Payout Speed
construction: Identify firms that initiated a dividend within the last 12 months (first nonzero DVC after prior zeros). Scale first-year total dividends (DVC) by operating cash flow (OANCF). Rank recent initiators by this ratio.
rationale: Dividend initiations signal management confidence; those committing a larger cash share signal stronger conviction about sustainable earnings, which the market fully appreciates only gradually.
higher_returns_for: high initiation payout speed among recent initiators

name: Capital Expenditure Smoothness
construction: Take capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) scaled by lagged property plant and equipment (PPENT) over the last five fiscal years. Compute the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by mean) of this annual ratio. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Firms with lumpy, volatile investment face higher adjustment costs and greater information uncertainty, commanding a risk premium relative to smooth investors.
higher_returns_for: high capex volatility (high coefficient of variation)

name: Trade Credit Reliance
construction: Compute accounts payable (Compustat AP) divided by cost of goods sold (COGS), annualized. Take the change relative to the prior year. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Rising reliance on supplier financing can indicate constrained access to formal capital markets, and constrained firms earn higher expected returns as compensation for financing risk.
higher_returns_for: high increase in trade credit reliance

name: Return-Volume Elasticity
construction: Using daily data over the prior 12 months from CRSP, regress absolute daily returns on daily turnover (volume/shares outstanding). The slope coefficient measures price impact per unit of trading. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Stocks whose prices move a lot per unit of volume are less liquid and less resilient, so investors demand a premium for bearing this illiquidity.

name: Seasonal Earnings Consistency
construction: From Compustat quarterly data, compute year-over-year change in quarterly EPS for the last eight quarters. Count the fraction of quarters with positive year-over-year growth. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: A long streak of consistent seasonal earnings improvement reflects durable business momentum that investors underextrapolate, leading to continued positive surprises.

name: Asset-Composition Tangibility Shift
construction: Compute net PP&E (PPENT) divided by total assets (AT) for the current and prior fiscal year, and take the change. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A shift toward tangible assets increases collateralizable capacity and reduces distress risk, but the market slowly incorporates this improved financial flexibility, temporarily underpricing such firms.
higher_returns_for: low change in tangibility (shift toward intangible/less collateral)

name: Cash Flow Volatility-Adjusted Yield
construction: Compute operating cash flow (OANCF) to price (market cap) for the latest fiscal year. Divide this yield by the standard deviation of the annual OANCF-to-assets ratio over the prior five years. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: High cash flow yield delivered with low cash flow volatility represents cheap, stable-quality firms that the market discounts too heavily relative to their reliability.

name: Inventory Growth Divergence
construction: For each firm, compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using annual financials lagged at least 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: When inventory builds faster than sales, it signals demand overestimation and future writedowns or margin pressure, which the market is slow to price.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Order Backlog to Assets
construction: Divide reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) by total assets (item AT), using annual data lagged 4 months. Form cross-sectional deciles.
rationale: Order backlog is a forward-looking demand indicator that is disclosed but underweighted by investors relative to reported earnings.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Change
construction: Compute the change in the ratio of SG&A expense (item XSGA) to sales (item SALE) from the prior fiscal year to the current one; measure = -(current ratio minus prior ratio). Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Improving operating efficiency (falling overhead per dollar of sales) signals management execution not yet reflected in valuation multiples.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (improving efficiency)

name: Deferred Tax Signal
construction: Compute the change in the net deferred tax liability (from Compustat deferred taxes item TXDB) scaled by lagged total assets, annual data lagged 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Large increases in deferred tax liabilities often reflect aggressive book-vs-tax accounting that inflates reported earnings and reverses later.

name: Capital Expenditure Acceleration
construction: For each firm compute capex (item CAPX) scaled by lagged property plant and equipment (item PPENT) minus the firm's own 3-year average of that ratio. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Spikes in investment relative to a firm's normal pace tend to be followed by disappointing returns as overinvestment erodes future free cash flow.

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Momentum
construction: Flag firms that paid a dividend (item DVC > 0) in each of the trailing 3 years with strictly non-decreasing dividends per share, and rank remaining firms by the compound growth rate of dividends per share over that window.
rationale: Consistently rising dividends credibly signal sustainable cash flows and managerial confidence that the market underappreciates.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (steadily rising dividends)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly gross margin (GP = SALE minus COGS, divided by SALE, using Compustat quarterly items SALEQ and COGSQ) over the trailing 12 quarters; measure = -stddev. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Stable gross margins indicate durable competitive advantage and lower cash-flow risk that is only partially compensated by the market.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (more stable margins)

name: Turnover-Adjusted Momentum
construction: Take standard 12-month minus 1-month past return, and within each momentum decile sort further by average monthly share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the same 12 months; measure = momentum residualized on turnover, favoring low-turnover winners.
rationale: Momentum on low-attention (low-turnover) stocks reflects slower information diffusion and continues longer than high-turnover momentum.
higher_returns_for: high past return combined with low turnover

name: Cash Productivity
construction: Compute operating cash flow proxy (item IB plus item DP, income before extraordinary items plus depreciation) divided by market value of equity (CRSP price times shares), annual data lagged 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Cash-based profitability relative to price is harder to manipulate than accrual earnings yield and captures genuine value the market discounts.

name: Analyst Coverage Deficit
construction: Regress number of covering analysts (IBES) on log market cap and log book-to-market cross-sectionally each month; measure = negative of the residual (firms with fewer analysts than their size/value peers predict).
rationale: Stocks with abnormally low coverage relative to observable characteristics are underfollowed, carry higher information risk, and earn a premium as coverage catches up.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (coverage deficit)

name: Inventory Efficiency Divergence
construction: For each fiscal year, compute the ratio of inventory growth (Compustat item INVT year-over-year change) to sales growth (SALE year-over-year change). Rank firms cross-sectionally; the measure is inventory growth minus sales growth, scaled by lagged total assets (AT). Rebalance annually four months after fiscal year end.
rationale: Inventory building that outpaces sales signals weakening demand and future write-downs or margin pressure that the market is slow to fully price.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Accrual-Weighted Earnings Volatility
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly earnings (Compustat IBQ scaled by lagged assets ATQ) over the prior 12 quarters, then multiply by the ratio of total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, from balance-sheet items) to net income for the most recent fiscal year. Rank cross-sectionally, rebalance quarterly.
rationale: Firms with volatile earnings driven by high accruals have low-quality, less persistent earnings that investors overvalue, leading to lower subsequent returns.

name: Order Backlog Intensity
construction: For firms reporting order backlog (Compustat item OB), compute backlog scaled by total sales (SALE) for the most recent fiscal year, and the year-over-year change in this ratio. The predictor is the change in scaled backlog. Rebalance annually four months after fiscal year end; universe limited to firms disclosing OB.
rationale: Rising order backlog relative to sales is a leading indicator of future revenue growth that is not yet reflected in reported earnings and is underweighted by investors.

name: Capital Expenditure Acceleration
construction: Compute the second difference of capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX): (CAPX_t - CAPX_{t-1}) minus (CAPX_{t-1} - CAPX_{t-2}), scaled by lagged total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally, rebalance annually.
rationale: Accelerating investment reflects managerial overconfidence and empire-building that tends to precede disappointing returns as overinvestment erodes future profitability.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating capex)

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Gap
construction: For firms paying dividends (DVC > 0), compute the ratio of dividends paid to free cash flow (operating cash flow OANCF minus CAPX). Combine with the number of consecutive years of dividend increases. The predictor ranks firms by the gap between dividend commitment and free-cash-flow coverage. Rebalance annually.
rationale: Firms sustaining dividends with weak free-cash-flow coverage signal management confidence in future cash flows or, alternatively, unsustainable payouts; the well-covered persistent payers earn a quality premium.
higher_returns_for: high free-cash-flow coverage of a persistent dividend

name: Selling Expense Operating Leverage
construction: Compute selling, general and administrative expense (Compustat XSGA) as a fraction of sales (SALE), then take the year-over-year change in this ratio during a period of positive sales growth. The predictor is the negative of the change (i.e., SG&A ratio falling while sales rise). Rebalance annually.
rationale: Declining SG&A intensity during revenue expansion reveals improving operating leverage and cost discipline not yet capitalized into prices.
higher_returns_for: high values (falling SG&A ratio amid growth)

name: Return-on-Equity Trend Consistency
construction: Compute quarterly ROE (IBQ divided by lagged common equity CEQQ) for the prior 8 quarters. Fit the sign consistency of quarter-over-quarter changes: the measure is the fraction of quarters with non-decreasing ROE. Rank cross-sectionally, rebalance quarterly.
rationale: Monotonically improving profitability reflects durable competitive advantage that the market underappreciates relative to a single-period ROE level.

name: Asset-Liquidity Mispricing
construction: Compute the fraction of total assets held as cash and short-term investments (CHE / AT), and interact it with the book-to-market ratio. The predictor identifies value firms (high B/M) that also hold large liquid balances. Rank cross-sectionally, rebalance annually.
rationale: High cash holdings within apparently cheap value firms indicate hidden financial flexibility and downside protection that the market discounts excessively.

name: Share Issuance Timing Signal
construction: Compute the year-over-year change in split-adjusted shares outstanding (Compustat CSHO adjusted by AJEX) over the prior fiscal year, and combine with the firm's prior 12-month stock return. The predictor is negative net issuance following high returns (i.e., low share growth after price run-ups). Rebalance annually.
rationale: Managers issue equity when they perceive their stock is overvalued; firms that refrain from issuing after strong price appreciation signal management belief in continued undervaluation.
higher_returns_for: low share issuance following high past returns

name: Tax-Book Income Divergence
construction: Estimate taxable income as current tax expense (Compustat TXT minus deferred tax TXDI) divided by the statutory tax rate, then compute the ratio of this estimated taxable income to reported pre-tax book income (PI). The predictor is one minus this ratio (book-tax gap), scaled. Rank cross-sectionally, rebalance annually.
rationale: A large excess of book income over taxable income signals aggressive accrual-based earnings management and lower earnings quality, predicting lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low book-tax income gap (book income close to taxable income)

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: Using annual Compustat data, compute the ratio of inventories (item INVT) to sales (item SALE) for the three most recent fiscal years. Define the predictor as the change in the year-over-year growth rate of this ratio: [(INVT/SALE)_t / (INVT/SALE)_{t-1} - 1] minus [(INVT/SALE)_{t-1} / (INVT/SALE)_{t-2} - 1]. Rebalance annually four months after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Accelerating inventory buildup relative to sales signals overproduction and weakening demand that managers are slow to acknowledge, foreshadowing markdowns and negative earnings surprises.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating inventory buildup)

name: Trade Credit Dependence
construction: From annual Compustat, compute accounts payable (item AP) divided by cost of goods sold (item COGS), a proxy for days payable outstanding scaled. Rank stocks cross-sectionally within industry. Rebalance annually four months after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms extended more trade credit by suppliers are viewed as creditworthy by informed counterparties, and this private information about firm quality is not immediately impounded into prices.

name: Dispersion of Monthly Return Signs
construction: Over the trailing 24 months, count the number of positive-return months minus negative-return months, divided by 24, using CRSP monthly returns. This measures directional consistency independent of magnitude.
rationale: Persistent directional agreement reflects gradual information diffusion and underreaction, while erratic sign flipping reflects noise-driven trading that mean-reverts.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (consistently positive months)

name: Capital Expenditure Volatility
construction: Using the trailing five annual Compustat observations, compute the standard deviation of capital expenditures (item CAPX) scaled by average total assets (item AT), over that five-year window. Rebalance annually.
rationale: Lumpy, unpredictable investment reflects poor managerial planning and heightened operational uncertainty for which investors demand compensation, or alternatively signals overinvestment episodes that destroy value.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (smooth capital spending)

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Identify firms that first paid a cash dividend (item DVC transitions from zero to positive) within the trailing 12 months using Compustat/CRSP distribution data. Assign an indicator and hold for 12 months post-initiation.
rationale: Dividend initiations are a costly, sticky signal of sustainable future earnings that the market underappreciates, generating drift as the commitment is validated.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Change
construction: From annual Compustat, compute SG&A (item XSGA) divided by sales (item SALE) for the two latest fiscal years, and take the year-over-year change (improvement is negative). Rebalance annually four months after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Falling selling expense ratios signal improving operating leverage and management discipline that translates into future margin expansion not yet reflected in valuation.
higher_returns_for: low values of the change (improving expense efficiency)

name: Turnover-Adjusted Illiquidity
construction: For each stock compute the trailing 12-month average of absolute daily return divided by daily dollar volume (Amihud-style), then multiply by the trailing 12-month average share turnover to adjust for float. Use CRSP daily data.
rationale: The interaction captures illiquidity that persists even among actively traded names, isolating a compensated liquidity risk premium distinct from raw illiquidity.

name: Depreciation-to-CapEx Gap
construction: From annual Compustat, compute depreciation and amortization (item DP) minus capital expenditures (item CAPX), scaled by total assets (item AT). Rebalance annually four months after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms depreciating faster than they reinvest are harvesting existing assets, a conservative posture that signals underappreciated free cash flow, whereas aggressive reinvestors overextend.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (depreciation exceeding capex)

name: Earnings Announcement Return Clustering
construction: Sum the CRSP three-day cumulative abnormal returns around the four most recent quarterly earnings announcement dates (from Compustat quarterly RDQ field), measured relative to the market. Update after each announcement.
rationale: Consistent positive reactions across recent announcements indicate a firm systematically beating expectations, and this quality persists due to analyst and investor anchoring.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (positive cumulative announcement returns)

name: Asset Growth Deceleration
construction: From annual Compustat, compute total asset growth (AT_t/AT_{t-1} - 1) for each of the last three years, then define the predictor as the second difference: the change in the growth rate. Rebalance annually four months after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms whose balance-sheet expansion is decelerating are transitioning from empire-building to discipline, which the market rewards, while accelerating growth presages overinvestment underperformance.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating asset growth)

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: For each firm, compute the ratio of inventories (Compustat item INVT) to sales (SALE) at fiscal year-end. Measure the change in this ratio from year t-1 to t minus the change from year t-2 to t-1 (second difference, i.e., acceleration). Rank cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year data.
rationale: Accelerating inventory buildup relative to sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns, so managers who let inventory accelerate destroy value that the market underappreciates.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating/shrinking inventory-to-sales)

name: Depreciation Rate Change
construction: Compute depreciation expense (DP) divided by gross PP&E (PPEGT) for each fiscal year. Take the year-over-year change in this depreciation rate. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A declining depreciation rate can signal earnings management that inflates current profits by stretching asset lives, so firms lowering their depreciation rate should subsequently underperform.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising depreciation rate)

name: Dispersion of Segment Profitability
construction: Using Compustat business segment data, compute for each firm the sales-weighted standard deviation of operating margin (segment operating profit / segment sales) across reported segments. Standardize by number of segments. Rank annually.
rationale: Firms with widely dispersed segment margins likely cross-subsidize weak divisions, indicating agency-driven capital misallocation that depresses future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (uniform segment profitability)

name: Order Backlog to Market Cap
construction: Take reported order backlog (Compustat item OB when available) divided by market capitalization at fiscal year-end. Rank cross-sectionally each June among firms reporting backlog.
rationale: A large backlog relative to price represents contracted future revenue the market fails to fully capitalize, generating positive drift as backlog converts to sales.

name: Trading Volume Concentration
construction: Using daily CRSP volume over the prior 12 months, compute the Herfindahl index of monthly volume shares (sum of squared monthly volume fractions). Higher values mean volume is concentrated in few months. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Concentrated trading indicates episodic informed-trading events and lower steady-state liquidity, so investors demand a premium for holding such stocks.

name: Accrual-Cashflow Divergence Persistence
construction: For each firm compute earnings minus operating cash flow (total accruals, scaled by total assets) for each of the last three fiscal years. Count the number of consecutive years accruals exceeded the firm's own trailing median. Rank annually.
rationale: Persistently high accruals relative to cash generation reflect entrenched aggressive accounting or deteriorating quality, predicting mean-reversion in earnings and lower returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (few consecutive high-accrual years)

name: Relative R&D Momentum
construction: Compute R&D expense (XRD) scaled by sales for each firm, then take the two-year growth rate in this ratio. Within each industry (SIC 3-digit), demean the growth rate. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms increasing R&D intensity faster than industry peers are building intangible capital that is expensed immediately and undervalued, yielding delayed positive returns.

name: Dividend Smoothing Deviation
construction: Estimate each firm's dividend payout as dividends (DVC) over earnings (IB). Compute the absolute deviation of the current-year payout ratio from the firm's trailing five-year average payout ratio. Rank annually among dividend payers.
rationale: Large deviations from a firm's established payout policy signal financial stress or unstable cash flows that the market underprices, so stable payers outperform.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (stable payout)

name: Return Skewness Asymmetry
construction: Using daily CRSP returns over the past 12 months, compute the ratio of the average of positive daily returns to the absolute average of negative daily returns (gain/loss asymmetry). Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Investors overpay for lottery-like stocks with large positive skewness in daily returns, so high positive-asymmetry stocks subsequently earn lower returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (negative/less positive skew)

name: Working Capital Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle = days inventory (INVT/COGS*365) + days receivable (RECT/SALE*365) - days payable (AP/COGS*365) for each fiscal year. Take the three-year change (improvement is negative change). Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms improving operational efficiency by shortening their cash conversion cycle free up capital and signal better management, predicting higher future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (shrinking cash conversion cycle)

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: Compute the year-over-year change in the ratio of inventories (Compustat item INVT) to sales (SALE), then take the second difference (acceleration) across two consecutive fiscal years. Rank cross-sectionally each June using the most recent annual data.
rationale: Accelerating inventory buildup relative to sales signals unanticipated demand weakness and future margin pressure that the market is slow to price.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (decelerating inventory relative to sales)

name: Order Backlog Growth Deflated by Assets
construction: Use reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) scaled by total assets (AT), measured as the year-over-year change. Rank firms each June; restrict to firms that report nonzero backlog.
rationale: Growing backlog reflects strong committed future demand not yet in earnings, and investors underreact to this forward-looking soft signal.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising backlog-to-assets)

name: Employee Productivity Momentum
construction: Compute sales per employee (SALE / EMP) and take the two-year growth rate. Rank cross-sectionally each June using annual Compustat data.
rationale: Rising revenue per worker signals operating efficiency gains and restructuring benefits that translate into future profitability improvements underappreciated by the market.

name: Dispersion Between Cash and Accrual Earnings Trends
construction: For each firm compute the 3-year trend (slope of regression on time) in cash flow from operations scaled by assets and separately the trend in total accruals scaled by assets. Take the difference (cash trend minus accrual trend). Rank each June.
rationale: Firms whose cash-based earnings are strengthening while accruals shrink have higher-quality, more persistent earnings that the market undervalues.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (cash improving relative to accruals)

name: Volume-Weighted Price Range Compression
construction: For each stock compute the average daily high-low range (from CRSP daily data) divided by closing price over the prior 3 months, then compute its change relative to the range over the prior 12 months. Rank monthly.
rationale: Compressing intraday ranges indicate declining uncertainty and information resolution, preceding positive drift as risk premia normalize downward.
