higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (compressing range)

name: Capital Expenditure Deviation from Industry Norm
construction: Compute capex (CAPX) scaled by lagged assets, subtract the contemporaneous industry (2-digit SIC) median, and rank the firm-specific deviation each June.
rationale: Firms investing far above industry norms tend to over-invest and destroy value, generating lower subsequent returns due to overextrapolation of growth.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (below-industry capex)

name: Financing Gap Indicator
construction: Compute the ratio of (capital expenditures + dividends + change in working capital minus operating cash flow) to total assets, a measure of external financing need. Rank firms each June.
rationale: Firms with a large internal financing shortfall must access capital markets and face higher scrutiny and dilution risk, producing lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (self-financing firms)

name: Return-on-Assets Stability
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly ROA (net income / total assets, from Compustat quarterly) over the trailing 12 quarters, inverted so that stable firms score high. Rank each quarter.
rationale: Stable operating profitability signals durable competitive advantage and lower cash-flow risk that investors underprice relative to volatile-earnings firms.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (stable ROA)

name: Tax-Book Income Divergence
construction: Estimate taxable income from the current tax expense (TXT minus deferred tax TXDI) divided by the statutory rate, and compare to pretax book income (PI). Compute the ratio of estimated taxable income to book income; rank each June.
rationale: When taxable income is high relative to book income, book earnings are less likely inflated by discretionary accruals, indicating higher earnings quality and future returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (taxable income high relative to book)

name: Turnover-Adjusted Reversal
construction: Compute the prior 1-month stock return and interact its sign with abnormal share turnover (monthly volume/shares outstanding relative to its own 12-month average) using CRSP data. Short recent winners with abnormally high turnover and buy recent losers with abnormally low turnover; rank the composite.
rationale: Short-term reversal is stronger among stocks with liquidity-driven, high-turnover price moves, which reflect temporary price pressure rather than information.
higher_returns_for: low prior return combined with low abnormal turnover (past losers with quiet volume)

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: From 10-K segment and cost-of-goods footnotes, estimate the fraction of COGS attributable to the largest identifiable input category or supplier (using SIC-based input-output linkages from BEA use tables mapped to firm supplier disclosures). Rank firms by concentration; rebalance annually after fiscal year-end filings.
rationale: Firms dependent on few suppliers bear undiversified input-cost and disruption risk that is imperfectly priced, requiring a return premium.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: Using Compustat data item for order backlog (OB), compute year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by lagged sales. Form portfolios sorted on the change in backlog-to-sales, rebalanced quarterly after earnings.
rationale: Rising backlog signals future revenue that analysts underweight, producing a gradual drift as demand converts to earnings.

name: Working Capital Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle (days inventory + days receivables - days payables) from Compustat quarterly items. Measure the trailing four-quarter change (improvement = shortening). Sort firms on the change, rebalance quarterly.
rationale: Improving operational efficiency reflects managerial quality and future free-cash-flow gains that the market prices slowly.
higher_returns_for: large decrease in cash conversion cycle

name: Intraday Range Compression
construction: For each stock over the prior 60 trading days, compute the average daily (high-low)/close range from CRSP daily data, then take the ratio of the most recent 20-day average range to the prior 40-day average range. Sort cross-sectionally, rebalance monthly.
rationale: Volatility compression precedes directional resolution and reflects declining disagreement; low-range firms tend to experience subsequent underpricing correction and outperform.
higher_returns_for: low recent range relative to prior range (strong compression)

name: Deferred Revenue Buildup
construction: From Compustat balance sheet, measure year-over-year growth in deferred/unearned revenue scaled by total assets. Sort firms annually after fiscal-year filings.
rationale: Growing deferred revenue represents prepaid future sales and customer commitment not yet reflected in earnings, an underappreciated leading indicator.

name: Capex Acceleration Divergence
construction: Compute the second difference (acceleration) of capital expenditures scaled by lagged assets over trailing three fiscal years, and subtract the industry median acceleration. Sort firms on relative capex acceleration, rebalance annually.
rationale: Firms accelerating investment beyond industry peers may signal overexpansion; empirically decelerating investors are cheaper and outperform.
higher_returns_for: low (negative) capex acceleration relative to industry

name: Insider Net Purchase Breadth
construction: Using SEC Form 4 filings (available via EDGAR), count distinct insiders making open-market purchases minus those making sales over the trailing six months, scaled by number of reporting insiders. Sort on breadth of net buying, rebalance monthly.
rationale: Broad consensus insider buying aggregates dispersed private information more reliably than dollar volume from a single insider.

name: Analyst Coverage Deceleration
construction: From I/B/E/S, compute the change in the number of covering analysts over the trailing 12 months. Sort firms on the decline in coverage, controlling for size, rebalance quarterly.
rationale: Firms losing analyst coverage become neglected and underpriced, earning a subsequent recovery premium akin to a neglect/liquidity effect.

name: Gross Profit Volatility
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly gross profit (sales minus COGS) scaled by average assets over the trailing 16 quarters from Compustat. Sort firms on this volatility, rebalance annually.
rationale: Firms with volatile gross margins face greater fundamental uncertainty that commands a risk premium not captured by return volatility alone.

name: Tax Expense Surprise
construction: Estimate expected income tax expense from lagged effective tax rate applied to current pretax income, and compute the residual (actual minus expected tax) scaled by market equity. Sort firms on the surprise, rebalance quarterly after filings.
rationale: Unexpected declines in tax burden signal improving deferred tax positions or credits that boost future net income and are slowly incorporated by investors.
higher_returns_for: low (negative) tax surprise, i.e., taxes below expectation

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: From the 10-K, count the number of major suppliers or customers disclosed under SFAS 131 segment/customer disclosures. Compute a Herfindahl index of revenue dependence on the largest disclosed customers (percent of sales to customers exceeding 10% threshold). Rank firms cross-sectionally by this concentration each June using prior fiscal-year filings.
rationale: Firms dependent on few large customers bear concentrated demand and bargaining-power risk that is underpriced by investors focused on aggregate revenue growth.
higher_returns_for: high customer concentration (as compensation for undiversified demand risk)

name: Accrual Volatility
construction: For each firm compute total accruals (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding short-term debt, minus depreciation) scaled by average total assets for each of the prior 5 fiscal years. Take the standard deviation of this series. Rank firms cross-sectionally in June.
rationale: Unstable accruals signal low earnings quality and estimation uncertainty; investors underappreciate the persistence advantage of firms with smooth accrual generation.

name: Order Backlog Growth
construction: Extract reported order backlog (Compustat item ORDB or from 10-K where available) and compute year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by lagged total assets. Form deciles each June.
rationale: Backlog is a forward-looking demand indicator that is slowly incorporated into prices because it is not a headline income-statement figure.

name: R&D Acceleration
construction: Compute the change in R&D-to-sales ratio between the two most recent fiscal years minus the change over the prior two years (second difference of R&D intensity). Rank firms with positive R&D cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Accelerating innovation investment predicts future intangible payoffs that markets discount too heavily given conservative accounting expensing of R&D.

name: Working Capital Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle (days inventory + days receivables - days payables) for the current and prior fiscal year. Measure the year-over-year improvement (decrease). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by improvement.
rationale: Managers who tighten working capital signal operational discipline and free up cash flow that the market recognizes only gradually.
higher_returns_for: large improvement (decrease) in cash conversion cycle

name: Dispersion of Intraday Return Signs
construction: Using daily CRSP data over the prior 12 months, compute the fraction of positive-return days minus negative-return days, then measure how clustered runs are versus random using a runs-test z-statistic. Rank firms by the runs-test statistic each month.
rationale: Non-random clustering of return signs reflects sluggish information diffusion among a limited investor base, predicting continued drift.

name: Seasonality-Adjusted Volume Shock
construction: For each month compute average daily dollar volume, deseasonalize by subtracting the same calendar-month average over the prior 3 years, and scale by its historical standard deviation. Rank firms each month by this volume z-score.
rationale: Abnormal volume relative to a stock's own seasonal norm reveals arriving information not yet reflected in price, generating short-horizon continuation.

name: Deferred Revenue Buildup
construction: Compute year-over-year change in deferred/unearned revenue (Compustat) scaled by lagged sales. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Growth in deferred revenue represents prepaid future sales already collected in cash, an underappreciated leading indicator of recognized revenue and cash-flow quality.

name: Capital Expenditure Smoothness
construction: Compute capex-to-assets for each of the prior 5 years and take the coefficient of variation. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by inverse volatility.
rationale: Firms with steady, disciplined investment programs avoid value-destroying overinvestment cycles; markets overweight lumpy expansion stories.

name: Gross Margin Stability Premium
construction: Compute gross margin (sales minus COGS over sales) for the prior 8 quarters and take the standard deviation. Combine into a signal that ranks firms by low margin volatility conditional on above-median margin level, each June.
rationale: Persistent, stable gross margins indicate durable competitive moats and pricing power that the market undervalues relative to reported growth.
higher_returns_for: low gross margin volatility with high margin level

name: Supplier Concentration Risk
construction: From annual 10-K segment and MD&A disclosures, count the number of major customers/suppliers a firm reports as accounting for >10% of revenues or purchases. Construct a concentration index equal to 1 minus the Herfindahl of disclosed customer revenue shares; rank cross-sectionally each June and rebalance annually.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk and hold-up risk that is not fully priced by investors focused on aggregate fundamentals.
higher_returns_for: high customer-concentration (more dependent) firms, as compensation for concentration risk

name: Accrual Reversal Acceleration
construction: Compute working-capital accruals (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding debt, from Compustat) for the most recent quarter minus the same quarter one year prior, scaled by average total assets. Rank the change in the accrual rate (second difference of accruals) cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Accelerating accruals signal deteriorating earnings quality and impending reversals faster than the level of accruals alone, so investors underreact to the rate of change.

name: Inventory-to-Sales Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventory minus year-over-year growth in sales, using quarterly Compustat data averaged over the last four quarters. Rank the divergence cross-sectionally each quarter and rebalance.
rationale: When inventory builds faster than sales, it foreshadows future markdowns, weak demand, and negative earnings surprises that the market is slow to incorporate.
higher_returns_for: low divergence (inventory growing slower than sales) firms

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Score
construction: Track the number of consecutive quarters a firm has paid dividends and whether the most recent dividend was raised, using CRSP distribution data. Build a score combining streak length and recent increase; rank firms with new or growing dividend commitments each quarter.
rationale: Firms establishing a durable, growing dividend signal credible future cash flows, and the market underappreciates the informational value of sustained payout commitment versus one-time payments.

name: Capital Expenditure Volatility
construction: Compute the standard deviation of annual capital expenditures scaled by total assets over the trailing five fiscal years from Compustat. Rank cross-sectionally each June and rebalance annually.
rationale: Lumpy, unpredictable investment reflects poor internal planning and higher real-option uncertainty; smooth investors underreact to the elevated risk embedded in erratic capex.
higher_returns_for: high capex-volatility firms, as risk compensation

name: Analyst Coverage Decline
construction: Using I/B/E/S, compute the change in the number of analysts covering a firm over the trailing 12 months. Rank firms by net analyst departures each month and form portfolios.
rationale: Losing analyst coverage increases information asymmetry and reduces investor recognition, raising expected returns as neglected stocks command a premium.
higher_returns_for: firms with the largest declines in analyst coverage

name: Selling Expense Efficiency
construction: Compute the ratio of gross profit growth to SG&A growth over the trailing year using Compustat annual data, restricted to firms with positive SG&A. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms generating profit growth without proportional increases in selling and administrative spending exhibit operating leverage and management discipline that predict future profitability improvements the market underreacts to.
higher_returns_for: high efficiency (profit growth exceeding SG&A growth) firms

name: Share Issuance Timing Relative to Price Run-up
construction: For each firm, compute net share issuance (change in split-adjusted shares outstanding from CRSP) over the trailing year, interacted with the firm's trailing 12-month return. Flag firms that issued heavily after strong price appreciation; rank the interaction term each month.
rationale: Managers opportunistically issue equity when they perceive their stock is overvalued after run-ups, so heavy issuance following gains signals overvaluation and predicts low returns.
higher_returns_for: low values (net repurchasers or non-issuers after run-ups)

name: Effective Tax Rate Change
construction: Compute the change in the effective tax rate (tax expense divided by pretax income) from the prior fiscal year to the current, using Compustat, winsorizing extreme values and excluding loss firms. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: A declining effective tax rate can boost reported earnings unsustainably and reflects aggressive tax positions or timing benefits that reverse, so investors overvalue the temporary earnings lift.
higher_returns_for: firms with rising effective tax rates (conservative earnings)

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: Using the order backlog item disclosed in Compustat (BACKLG), compute year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by sales, for firms reporting the item. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter and rebalance.
rationale: Growing order backlog is a forward-looking indicator of future revenue that is buried in footnotes and underweighted by investors focused on current earnings.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using 10-K disclosures under SFAS 131 segment reporting and item disclosures of major customers, compute the fraction of firm revenue attributable to its single largest customer (customers accounting for >10% of sales must be disclosed). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by this concentration ratio, using the most recent fiscal-year filing.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk and hold-up risk; investors underprice this fragility until shocks materialize, so it commands a risk premium.

name: Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration
construction: Compute the change in the ratio of inventory (Compustat INVT) to sales (SALE) over the trailing four quarters, then the change in that change (second difference) across the last two fiscal quarters. Sort stocks cross-sectionally each quarter after earnings release.
rationale: Accelerating inventory buildup signals demand overestimation and future markdowns/write-offs that the market is slow to incorporate, predicting lower returns.

name: R&D Reversal Growth
construction: Scale R&D expense (Compustat XRD) by lagged total assets (AT), then compute the two-year change in this ratio. Each June, form deciles on the magnitude of the increase in R&D intensity, restricting to firms with positive R&D in both years.
rationale: Rising R&D intensity reflects intangible investment expensed immediately, understating current earnings and book value; the market undervalues the option-like future payoff, yielding higher subsequent returns.

name: Dispersion of Intra-Year Return Volatility
construction: For each stock, compute monthly realized volatility from daily returns (CRSP) for each of the trailing 12 months, then take the standard deviation of those 12 monthly volatilities. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Volatility-of-volatility captures instability in the firm's risk environment that is not spanned by average volatility; uncertainty-averse investors demand compensation, so high vol-of-vol earns higher returns after controlling for level.

name: Deferred Revenue Momentum
construction: Compute the year-over-year growth in deferred revenue / unearned revenue (Compustat balance-sheet items, current plus long-term) scaled by total assets. Sort firms each quarter after filing; restrict to firms reporting nonzero deferred revenue.
rationale: Growing deferred revenue represents cash collected for undelivered goods/services, a forward-looking indicator of contracted future sales that the market underweights relative to reported revenue.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency
construction: Compute the ratio of gross profit (SALE minus COGS) to selling, general & administrative expense (XSGA), then take its trailing-four-quarter change. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each quarter after earnings.
rationale: Improving gross profit generated per dollar of SG&A signals operating leverage and managerial efficiency gains not yet reflected in valuation, predicting higher returns.

name: Order Flow Persistence Asymmetry
construction: Using TAQ intraday data, classify trades via the Lee-Ready algorithm and compute the ratio of net buy-initiated to sell-initiated dollar volume over the trailing 60 trading days, then measure its serial autocorrelation over the same window. Rank stocks monthly.
rationale: Persistent one-sided order flow reflects gradual institutional accumulation or distribution ahead of public information, so high positive buy-side persistence predicts higher returns.

name: Pension Underfunding Surprise
construction: From 10-K pension footnotes (SFAS 87/132), compute the change in the funded status of defined-benefit plans (fair value of plan assets minus projected benefit obligation) scaled by market equity, year over year. Sort firms annually each June.
rationale: Deteriorating pension funded status is an off-income-statement liability the market processes slowly; worsening funding predicts lower future returns as the obligation is eventually recognized.

name: Analyst Coverage Loss
construction: Using I/B/E/S, count the number of distinct analysts issuing FY1 estimates each month and compute the twelve-month change in coverage count, scaled by prior coverage. Rank stocks monthly, focusing on firms experiencing coverage declines.
rationale: A drop in analyst coverage reduces information production and increases neglect; if not driven by fundamentals, neglected stocks become underpriced and earn higher subsequent returns.

name: Capital Expenditure Smoothness
construction: Compute the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by mean) of annual capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) scaled by total assets over the trailing five fiscal years. Rank firms each June, requiring five years of positive capex.
rationale: Firms with lumpy, volatile investment face higher adjustment costs and financing frictions, embedding real-option and risk premia; erratic investors underprice such firms so high capex volatility earns higher returns.

name: Supplier Concentration Risk
construction: From 10-K filings, count the number of distinct major suppliers disclosed (firms with concentrated purchasing report reliance on few suppliers). Construct a Herfindahl-style measure using the fraction of cost of goods sold attributable to the top disclosed suppliers; where explicit percentages are unavailable, use a dummy for disclosed dependence on a single supplier providing >10% of inputs. Rank cross-sectionally annually.
rationale: Firms dependent on few suppliers bear input-disruption and hold-up risk that is underappreciated and slowly incorporated, commanding a risk premium.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: Using Compustat data item order backlog (BACKLOG), compute the year-over-year change in backlog scaled by lagged total assets. Form cross-sectional deciles each fiscal year on the change.
rationale: Rising order backlog signals accelerating future demand not yet in reported earnings, and investors underreact to this leading indicator of revenue.

name: Deferred Revenue Growth
construction: Compute the year-over-year growth in the deferred/unearned revenue balance sheet liability, scaled by lagged total assets. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter using the most recent quarterly balance.
rationale: Growth in deferred revenue reflects prepaid future sales (a hidden order book), signaling demand strength that the market underweights because it sits in liabilities.

name: Advertising-to-Sales Surprise
construction: Compute advertising expense (Compustat XAD) divided by sales. Regress this ratio on its own industry-year average and firm history; take the residual as the abnormal advertising intensity. Rank cross-sectionally annually.
rationale: Abnormally high advertising builds intangible brand capital not capitalized on the balance sheet, leading to underpricing of future cash flows.

name: Effective Tax Rate Volatility
construction: Using the last 5 years of annual data, compute the standard deviation of the firm's effective tax rate (total income taxes / pretax income), winsorized to [0,1]. Rank cross-sectionally each year.
rationale: Volatile effective tax rates proxy for opaque earnings management and tax-planning uncertainty, generating a risk premium and mispricing.

name: Employee Productivity Trend
construction: Compute sales per employee (SALE/EMP) and take its two-year change scaled by the prior level. Rank firms cross-sectionally annually.
rationale: Accelerating labor productivity signals operational improvement and operating leverage that is slowly reflected in prices.

name: Capital Expenditure Acceleration
construction: Compute the second difference (acceleration) in capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets: (CAPX_t - CAPX_{t-1}) minus (CAPX_{t-1} - CAPX_{t-2}). Rank cross-sectionally annually.
rationale: Sharply accelerating investment tends to precede overexpansion and subsequent low returns, capturing empire-building and overinvestment beyond the level of investment.

name: Inventory-Sales Divergence
construction: Compute the difference between year-over-year inventory growth (INVT) and year-over-year sales growth (SALE). Positive values indicate inventory building faster than sales. Rank cross-sectionally annually.
rationale: Inventory outpacing sales signals demand weakness and future markdowns, predicting lower returns as the deterioration becomes visible.
higher_returns_for: low inventory-sales divergence (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Intra-Year Return Consistency
construction: Over the past 12 months, compute the fraction of months with positive returns minus fraction with negative returns, holding total 12-month return roughly constant by residualizing against past 12-month cumulative return. Rank the consistency residual cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Steady, consistent gainers reflect stable improving fundamentals that continue, whereas lumpy returns reflect one-off events; the market underprices smooth improvers.

name: Pension Funding Change
construction: Compute the year-over-year change in pension funded status (fair value of plan assets minus projected benefit obligation, from pension footnotes) scaled by lagged total assets. Rank cross-sectionally annually.
rationale: Improving pension funding frees future cash flows and signals reduced hidden leverage that investors are slow to reprice given footnote opacity.
higher_returns_for: high improvement in pension funded status

name: Order Backlog Growth
construction: From the annual 10-K, take the disclosed order backlog dollar amount (item often reported in the business/MD&A section). Compute year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by total assets: (Backlog_t - Backlog_{t-1}) / Average Total Assets. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Order backlog reflects contracted future demand not yet in revenue; the market underreacts to this leading indicator of future sales and earnings.

name: Deferred Revenue Change
construction: From the balance sheet, take the change in deferred (unearned) revenue over the trailing fiscal year, scaled by total assets: (DeferredRev_t - DeferredRev_{t-1}) / Total Assets. Sort stocks into deciles each June.
rationale: Rising deferred revenue signals customers prepaying for future delivery, a hard-cash leading indicator of future recognized revenue that investors underweight.

name: R&D Momentum
construction: Compute the trailing three-year growth rate in R&D expense (Compustat XRD), scaled by lagged sales: geometric mean growth of XRD/Sales over three years. Rank cross-sectionally annually, restricting to firms with positive R&D.
rationale: Sustained increases in innovation investment presage future productivity and product-cycle gains that are mispriced due to conservative expensing of intangibles.

name: Supplier-Concentration Risk
construction: From 10-K disclosures of major customers (SFAS 131 segment/customer data), compute the fraction of revenue from customers each representing >10% of sales. Define concentration as the sum of these fractions. Sort into quintiles annually.
rationale: Firms dependent on few large customers bear elevated cash-flow risk and bargaining-power disadvantage, commanding a risk premium.

name: Working-Capital Efficiency Improvement
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle (Days Inventory + Days Receivable - Days Payable) each year from Compustat. Take the year-over-year decline in the cash conversion cycle. Rank cross-sectionally; higher rank = larger improvement (larger decline).
rationale: Shortening the cash conversion cycle reflects operational improvements and freed-up cash that the market is slow to capitalize.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (larger reductions in the cycle)

name: Intraday Range Volatility Compression
construction: For each stock, compute the average daily (High-Low)/Close range over the trailing 60 trading days, and the same over days 120-61. Define compression as the ratio of the recent range to the prior range; rank so that lower ratios (compressing ranges) rank high.
rationale: Compression of intraday trading ranges reflects declining disagreement and pending resolution of uncertainty, preceding positive drift as information stabilizes.
higher_returns_for: low values of the ratio (greater compression)

name: Pension Plan Funding Change
construction: From the pension footnote (SFAS 132), compute the change in funded status (plan assets minus projected benefit obligation) scaled by market equity, year-over-year. Rank into deciles annually.
rationale: Improving pension funding status frees future corporate cash flows from mandatory contributions and signals asset-management quality that investors overlook.

name: Selling-Expense Leverage
construction: Compute the ratio of change in sales to change in SG&A expense over the trailing year: (Sales_t - Sales_{t-1}) / (SGA_t - SGA_{t-1}), restricting to firms with positive SGA growth. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms generating disproportionately more revenue per incremental selling dollar exhibit operating leverage and scalable business models that predict rising margins.

name: Off-Balance-Sheet Lease Intensity Shift
construction: From lease commitment footnotes, capitalize operating lease obligations (discounted future minimum lease payments) and compute the year-over-year change in capitalized-lease-adjusted leverage relative to reported leverage. Rank annually.
rationale: Firms increasing reliance on off-balance-sheet operating leases carry hidden financial leverage and fixed-cost risk underappreciated by naive balance-sheet analysis.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (larger hidden-leverage increases)

name: Analyst-Coverage Deceleration
construction: Using I/B/E/S, compute the change in the number of analysts covering a firm over the trailing 12 months, scaled by prior coverage. Rank so that stocks losing coverage rank high.
rationale: Declining analyst coverage reduces information production and visibility, raising the required return via an information-risk premium that later reverses upward.
higher_returns_for: low values of the change (declining coverage)

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: From 10-K disclosures under SFAS 131 segment reporting, identify firms that disclose material customer or supplier concentration (e.g., any single customer accounting for >10% of revenue). Construct a fragility score equal to the fraction of revenue attributable to the top-3 named customers, averaged over the two most recent fiscal years. Sort stocks cross-sectionally by this score.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers bear concentrated demand risk that is slow to be priced; investors underreact to the fundamental fragility, so these firms should command a risk premium.

name: Working Capital Acceleration
construction: Compute the second difference (acceleration) of non-cash net working capital scaled by average total assets: [(WC_t - WC_{t-1}) - (WC_{t-1} - WC_{t-2})]/avg(TA), where WC = (current assets - cash) - (current liabilities - short-term debt), using annual Compustat data.
rationale: Accelerating working capital investment signals aggressive but low-quality growth and future accrual reversals, which the market fails to fully anticipate.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: Using Compustat item for order backlog (data item ob), compute year-over-year growth in order backlog scaled by sales. Rank firms cross-sectionally within reporting industries; only include firms that report backlog.
rationale: Growth in order backlog is a leading indicator of future revenue that is disclosed but under-followed by investors, generating a delayed price response.

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Gap
construction: For firms paying dividends, compute the ratio of trailing-12-month common dividends to trailing free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex). Flag firms whose dividend payout exceeds free cash flow (ratio > 1) for two consecutive years. Sort into unsustainable-payout vs sustainable-payout groups.
rationale: Firms paying dividends they cannot fund from free cash flow face future cuts and financing pressure; the market prices the current yield but underprices the sustainability risk.

name: Intangible Intensity Adjusted Value
construction: Capitalize R&D and a fraction (say 30%) of SG&A as intangible capital using perpetual inventory with 20% and 20% depreciation, add to book equity, and recompute book-to-market. Rank firms by this intangible-adjusted book-to-market cross-sectionally.
rationale: Standard book value understates the capital of R&D- and brand-intensive firms; adjusting book equity recovers a cleaner value signal that predicts returns better than raw book-to-market.

name: Analyst Coverage Deceleration
construction: Using I/B/E/S, compute the change in the number of analysts issuing FY1 estimates over the trailing 12 months, scaled by prior coverage. Focus on the sign and magnitude of coverage decline.
rationale: Declining analyst coverage reduces information production and increases neglect, so these stocks become more mispriced and require higher expected returns as compensation.

name: Seasonal Earnings Surprise Repeat
construction: For each firm-quarter, compute standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) using a seasonal random walk. Construct a signal equal to the average SUE in the same fiscal quarter over the prior three years. Sort stocks by this same-quarter historical SUE ahead of the current quarter's announcement.
rationale: Some firms have persistent same-calendar-quarter earnings strength (e.g., seasonal business) that recurs and is underappreciated, leading to predictable positive surprises.

name: Asset Growth Composition Divergence
construction: Decompose total asset growth into operating-asset growth (PP&E + inventory + receivables) versus financial-asset growth (cash + short-term investments). Compute the spread: operating-asset growth minus financial-asset growth, scaled by lagged total assets.
rationale: Firms whose growth is concentrated in operating (hard-to-reverse) assets tend to overinvest and underperform, while cash accumulation is less prone to overinvestment; the composition refines the asset-growth anomaly.

name: Volume-Weighted Price Impact Sensitivity
construction: Using daily CRSP data, estimate Amihud-style price impact but weight the daily |return|/dollar-volume ratio by the deviation of that day's volume from its 60-day average, averaged over 12 months. This isolates illiquidity that manifests specifically on high-volume days.
rationale: Stocks that show large price moves precisely when trading volume spikes are more exposed to fragile liquidity and forced-trading risk, commanding an illiquidity premium beyond standard Amihud.

name: Capital Expenditure Timing Reversal
construction: Compute the ratio of current-year capex to the average capex over the prior three years, then take the negative of its two-year change so that firms sharply cutting capex after a prior expansion score high. Scale all capex by lagged net PP&E.
rationale: Firms retrenching capex after an investment boom are entering a harvesting phase with rising free cash flow and reduced overinvestment, which the market is slow to reward.
higher_returns_for: high capex retrenchment score (firms cutting capex after prior expansion)

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using annual 10-K disclosures, compute the fraction of a firm's cost of goods sold attributable to its largest few disclosed suppliers (or, absent explicit disclosure, proxy via inventory turnover volatility combined with segment input dependence). Score firms into deciles by concentration each June and rebalance annually.
rationale: Firms dependent on few suppliers face underpriced input-disruption risk; investors underweight this fragility until shocks materialize, so they must be compensated with higher expected returns.

name: R&D Acceleration
construction: Compute the year-over-year change in R&D-to-sales ratio scaled by its own three-year standard deviation: (RD_t/Sales_t - RD_{t-1}/Sales_{t-1}) / stdev(RD/Sales over 3 years). Form deciles annually using Compustat data lagged six months.
rationale: Sharp acceleration in innovation intensity signals management conviction about future growth options that the market is slow to capitalize into prices.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: From Compustat item ORDER BACKLOG (data item OB), compute growth in backlog scaled by lagged total assets, then subtract contemporaneous sales growth to isolate unbilled demand buildup. Rank cross-sectionally each fiscal year, lagged four months.
rationale: Rising backlog relative to recognized revenue reflects future demand not yet in earnings; the accrual-focused market underreacts to this off-income-statement signal.

name: Advertising-to-Market Cap Value Tilt
construction: Divide annual advertising expense (Compustat XAD) by market capitalization at fiscal year end. Form deciles among firms with nonzero advertising, rebalanced each June.
rationale: Advertising builds intangible brand capital not on the balance sheet; high advertising relative to price indicates understated intangible book value, mimicking a value effect that standard B/M misses.

name: Dispersion in Quarterly Earnings Signs
construction: Over the trailing 12 quarters, count the number of sign changes in seasonally-differenced quarterly earnings (positive-to-negative or negative-to-positive). Standardize and rank cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Frequent earnings sign reversals proxy for opaque, hard-to-value businesses that carry an information-uncertainty premium demanded by investors.

name: Capital Expenditure Smoothness
construction: Compute the coefficient of variation of annual capex-to-assets over the trailing five years. Rank firms into deciles annually with standard accounting lag.
rationale: Firms with lumpy, volatile investment face higher real-option and financing risk that is compensated, whereas smooth investors are safer and earn lower returns.

name: Insider Trading Breadth
construction: From SEC Form 4 filings over the trailing six months, compute the net number of distinct insiders buying minus selling, scaled by total number of insiders. Rank monthly.
rationale: Broad insider consensus (many distinct insiders buying) conveys more credible private information than concentrated trades by a single officer, and the market underweights the breadth dimension.

name: Deferred Revenue Growth
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in deferred/unearned revenue liabilities (Compustat) scaled by lagged total assets. Rank cross-sectionally each fiscal year with a four-month lag.
rationale: Growth in customer prepayments signals contracted future revenue and pricing power not yet recognized in earnings; the market underreacts to this liability-side growth signal.

name: Tax-Book Income Gap Persistence
construction: Estimate the gap between book pretax income and taxable income (inferred from current tax expense divided by statutory rate), scaled by assets, and measure its three-year average persistence. Rank annually.
rationale: Persistent positive book-tax gaps signal aggressive accruals and lower-quality earnings, so such firms subsequently underperform as reversals occur.

name: Geographic Sales Diversification Discount
construction: Using segment disclosures, compute a Herfindahl index across geographic revenue segments; higher values mean concentrated domestic sales, lower values mean globally diversified. Rank annually with accounting lag.
rationale: Geographically concentrated firms bear undiversified regional demand risk that is underpriced by investors focused on product-market rather than geographic exposure, earning a compensating premium.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using 10-K segment and MD&A disclosures on major customers (SFAS 131), compute the fraction of revenue attributable to the largest single customer. Rank firms cross-sectionally; use the trailing fiscal year. Combine with revenue volatility (std of YoY quarterly sales growth over 8 quarters) into a composite z-score.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk and bargaining-power disadvantages; investors underprice this fragility, so it commands a risk premium.

name: Inventory-Sales Divergence
construction: Compute YoY growth in inventory (Compustat INVT) minus YoY growth in sales (SALE), measured at the most recent fiscal quarter. Rank cross-sectionally each month using the latest available quarterly data.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns/write-offs that the market is slow to incorporate.
higher_returns_for: low inventory-minus-sales growth (inventory lean relative to sales)

name: Accrual Reversal Acceleration
construction: For each firm compute total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, from balance sheet) for the two most recent fiscal years; take the second difference (this year's accruals minus last year's accruals). Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Beyond the level of accruals, the acceleration of accruals captures the point at which earnings quality is deteriorating fastest, predicting sharper future earnings disappointments.

name: Capex Burst Relative to History
construction: Compute current-year capital expenditure (CAPX) divided by the average CAPX over the prior three years. Rank firms cross-sectionally at fiscal year-end.
rationale: Sudden capital-spending bursts reflect empire-building and overinvestment that erode future returns on capital, which investors extrapolate too optimistically.

name: Dividend Initiation Persistence Score
construction: Flag firms that initiated a cash dividend within the last 4 quarters (from CRSP distribution codes) and scale by the payout as a fraction of trailing free cash flow (OANCF minus CAPX). Rank the continuous payout-coverage measure among initiators.
rationale: Dividend initiations backed by ample free-cash-flow coverage signal credible, sustainable profitability improvements that the market underreacts to.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: Using disclosed order backlog (Compustat OB) scaled by total assets, compute the YoY change. Rank firms cross-sectionally at fiscal year-end; restrict to firms that report backlog.
rationale: Rising backlog is a leading indicator of future revenue that is not yet in reported earnings, and analysts underweight this soft-order information.

name: R&D Reversal Post-Cut
construction: Compute YoY change in R&D expense (XRD) scaled by sales for the most recent fiscal year. Rank firms; focus on firms cutting R&D (negative change).
rationale: Cutting R&D to hit near-term earnings targets sacrifices future growth and signals managerial short-termism, leading to lower long-run returns.

name: Geographic Revenue Dispersion
construction: From segment geographic disclosures (SFAS 131), compute a Herfindahl index across geographic revenue segments (sum of squared revenue shares). Rank cross-sectionally; higher index = more geographically concentrated.
rationale: Geographically concentrated firms carry undiversified macro and regulatory exposure that investors underprice, earning a risk premium.

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute SG&A (XSGA) divided by sales for the current and prior fiscal year; take the change. Rank cross-sectionally, favoring firms whose SG&A-to-sales ratio is declining.
rationale: Improving operating efficiency (falling SG&A intensity) reflects durable margin expansion that the market recognizes only gradually.

name: Short-Term Debt Rollover Pressure
construction: Compute debt in current liabilities (DLC) divided by total debt (DLC + DLTT) at fiscal year-end. Rank firms cross-sectionally; higher ratio = greater near-term rollover need.
rationale: High reliance on short-maturity debt exposes firms to refinancing and rollover risk in tightening credit conditions, commanding a risk premium.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: From annual 10-K disclosures, count the number of major customers/suppliers a firm names (segment and customer-concentration footnotes) and compute the fraction of revenue attributable to the top customer. Rank firms by revenue-weighted customer concentration. Update annually at fiscal year end, lagged 4 months.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk that is slow to be priced, and investors underappreciate the tail risk of customer loss.

name: Inventory-Sales Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventory (Compustat INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (SALE). Sort stocks cross-sectionally each month using the most recent lagged annual figures.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals overoptimistic demand expectations and future markdowns, which the market is slow to discount.

name: Accrual Volatility
construction: For each firm compute total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, scaled by average assets) each year, then take the standard deviation of annual accruals over the trailing 5 fiscal years. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Unstable accruals proxy for low earnings quality and information risk, commanding a return premium as investors demand compensation for opacity.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: Using the order-backlog item disclosed in 10-Ks (Compustat OB when available), compute year-over-year change in backlog scaled by total assets. Rank firms with reported backlog; update annually with a 4-month lag.
rationale: Growing backlog is a forward-looking signal of future revenue that is under-weighted because it sits outside standard income-statement metrics.

name: Dividend Initiation Recency
construction: Flag firms that initiated a cash dividend (first nonzero dividend after 3+ years of zero) within the trailing 12 months using CRSP distribution codes. Within dividend-initiators, sort by size of the initiated yield.
rationale: Dividend initiation is a costly credible signal of sustainable cash flows that the market underreacts to over subsequent quarters.
higher_returns_for: recent initiators with higher initiated yield

name: R&D Acceleration
construction: Compute the second difference in R&D intensity: (R&D/sales in year t minus R&D/sales in year t-1) minus (R&D/sales in t-1 minus R&D/sales in t-2), using Compustat XRD and SALE. Rank cross-sectionally, treating missing R&D as zero only for R&D-reporting industries.
rationale: Accelerating R&D investment reflects intensifying growth options that are systematically underpriced due to conservative accounting expensing.

name: Turnover-Adjusted Illiquidity
construction: Compute Amihud illiquidity (mean of |daily return|/dollar volume over the year) and divide by share turnover (annual volume/shares outstanding), forming an illiquidity measure orthogonalized to trading activity. Rank monthly.
rationale: Isolating price-impact illiquidity from trading intensity better captures the illiquidity premium than raw measures conflated with turnover.

name: Capital Expenditure Smoothness
construction: Compute the coefficient of variation of annual capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX scaled by lagged assets) over the trailing 5 years. Rank cross-sectionally each year.
rationale: Lumpy, volatile investment reflects real-options exercise timing and investment risk; smooth investors face lower ex-ante risk and lower required returns.

name: Gross Margin Trend
construction: Compute the slope of a trailing 5-year regression of gross margin (GP/SALE, i.e., (SALE-COGS)/SALE) on time. Rank firms by the fitted slope, updated annually with a lag.
rationale: Improving margins signal strengthening competitive position and pricing power that analysts extrapolate too slowly.

name: Financing Deficit Persistence
construction: For each year compute the external financing deficit (investment plus dividends minus internal cash flow, scaled by assets) and count how many of the trailing 3 years the firm ran a positive deficit requiring external funding. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Chronically cash-hungry firms tend to issue overvalued securities and disappoint, so persistent deficit firms underperform.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using 10-K segment and MD&A disclosures, count the number of major customers/suppliers each firm reports as accounting for >10% of revenues or purchases. Build a Herfindahl-style concentration index from the disclosed percentages. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June; the measure is the customer-revenue Herfindahl.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk and bargaining-power disadvantages, requiring a risk premium that is slow to be priced by investors who ignore relationship disclosures.

name: Accrual Volatility
construction: Compute total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, scaled by average total assets) each year for the prior 5 fiscal years, then take the standard deviation of these annual accruals. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: High variability in accruals signals low earnings quality and greater information risk about true cash-generating ability, commanding higher expected returns as compensation.

name: Order Backlog Growth
construction: For firms reporting order backlog in the 10-K (common in manufacturing/aerospace/tech), compute year-over-year growth in reported backlog scaled by total assets or sales. Rank firms cross-sectionally annually.
rationale: Growing backlog is a forward-looking demand signal not captured in current earnings; markets underreact to this soft-order information, so high backlog growth predicts positive future returns.

name: R&D Acceleration
construction: Compute R&D expense scaled by sales for the current year minus the average R&D-to-sales over the prior three years. This captures the second-order change (acceleration) in innovation intensity. Rank cross-sectionally each June among R&D-reporting firms.
rationale: Firms accelerating R&D investment signal expanding growth opportunities that are conservatively expensed and undervalued, leading to positive drift as innovation outputs materialize.

name: Dividend-Repurchase Mix Shift
construction: Measure total share repurchases (from cash flow statement, purchase of common stock) as a fraction of total payout (dividends plus repurchases) over the trailing year, and compute the change versus the prior year. Rank firms cross-sectionally.
rationale: A shift toward repurchases over dividends reflects management's belief that shares are undervalued and offers flexibility; markets underprice this signaling content.
higher_returns_for: high increase in repurchase share of payout

name: Inventory-Sales Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventories minus year-over-year growth in sales, scaled to a comparable basis. A positive value indicates inventory building faster than demand. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Inventory outpacing sales foreshadows future markdowns, write-offs, and weakening demand that investors are slow to recognize; low divergence firms outperform.
higher_returns_for: low inventory-sales divergence (sales growing faster than inventory)

name: Tax-Book Income Gap
construction: Estimate taxable income by grossing up current tax expense by the statutory rate, then compute the ratio of estimated taxable income to pre-tax book income. Rank firms cross-sectionally; the measure flags large book-over-tax positive gaps.
rationale: Large positive book-tax gaps indicate aggressive earnings management inflating reported book income relative to conservative tax income, predicting lower future returns as gaps reverse.
higher_returns_for: low book-tax gap (taxable income high relative to book income)

name: Capital Expenditure Smoothness
construction: Compute the coefficient of variation of annual capital expenditures (capex/total assets) over the prior 5 fiscal years. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Lumpy, erratic investment reflects poor planning and greater real-option uncertainty; smooth, predictable investors are lower-risk and command lower returns, so the risk premium accrues to erratic-capex firms.

name: Analyst Coverage Change per Size
construction: Compute the change in the number of I/B/E/S analysts covering the firm over the trailing 12 months, orthogonalized to (divided by) log market capitalization. Rank cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: An increase in analyst coverage beyond what size predicts reflects rising institutional attention and reduced information asymmetry, generating positive returns as the investor base broadens.

name: Gross Margin Stability Score
construction: Compute quarterly gross margin (gross profit/sales) over the prior 12 quarters and calculate the standard deviation. Combine with the level of gross margin into a z-score composite favoring high-and-stable margins. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Firms with high, stable gross margins possess durable competitive advantages and pricing power that the market underappreciates relative to headline earnings, producing sustained outperformance.

name: Customer Concentration Fragility
construction: From firm 10-K disclosures under SFAS 131, identify major customers accounting for >10% of revenue. Compute a Herfindahl index of disclosed customer revenue shares. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June on this concentration index, updated annually.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified cash-flow risk from customer bargaining power and potential loss, which is not fully priced and commands a risk premium.

name: Inventory-Sales Momentum Divergence
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in inventory (Compustat INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (SALE) using the most recent quarterly data. Rank firms each month on this divergence.
rationale: Inventory building faster than sales signals demand overestimation by management and impending markdowns, so high-divergence firms subsequently underperform.
higher_returns_for: low inventory-sales divergence (inventory growing slower than sales)

name: Order Flow Roundness Clustering
construction: Using TAQ intraday trade data over the prior month, compute the fraction of a stock's share volume executed in round-lot sizes that are multiples of 1000 shares. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: A high fraction of round-number institutional block trades proxies for informed institutional accumulation, predicting positive future returns.
higher_returns_for: high fraction of large round-lot volume

name: Analyst Forecast Dispersion Acceleration
construction: From I/B/E/S, compute the monthly change in the standard deviation of analyst EPS forecasts scaled by price (change in dispersion). Rank firms on the two-month acceleration in forecast dispersion.
rationale: Rising disagreement combined with short-sale constraints (Miller effect) leads to overpricing that reverses, so accelerating dispersion predicts lower returns.

name: Capex Timing Concentration
construction: Using quarterly Compustat capital expenditures (CAPXY differenced), compute the coefficient of variation of the firm's four quarterly capex figures over the trailing year. Rank firms on this seasonality/lumpiness measure.
rationale: Lumpy, poorly-timed investment spikes reflect agency-driven or reactive capital allocation that destroys value, predicting lower future returns.

name: Deferred Revenue Growth
construction: Compute year-over-year growth in the deferred revenue liability (Compustat DRC plus DRLT) scaled by total assets. Rank firms annually each June.
rationale: Growing deferred revenue reflects prepaid customer commitments and future recognized sales that the market underweights relative to reported earnings, predicting higher returns.

name: Working Capital Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle (days inventory + days receivables - days payables) using Compustat INVT, RECT, AP, COGS, SALE, and take the change over the trailing two years. Rank firms on the improvement (decrease) in the cycle.
rationale: Firms shortening their cash conversion cycle are improving operational efficiency and liquidity generation ahead of market recognition, predicting higher returns.
higher_returns_for: large improvement (decrease) in cash conversion cycle

name: Geographic Revenue Diffusion
construction: From segment disclosures in 10-Ks, count the number of distinct geographic segments and compute a diversification Herfindahl of foreign vs domestic revenue. Rank firms on foreign revenue share change year-over-year.
rationale: Rising foreign revenue share exposes firms to underpriced currency and macro risks and demand shifts, commanding a return premium not captured by domestic beta.

name: Short-Interest Velocity
construction: Using semi-monthly short interest data from exchanges, compute the change in shares-short scaled by shares outstanding over the most recent two settlement periods (the velocity of short accumulation). Rank stocks each month.
rationale: Rapid new short accumulation reflects informed negative sentiment that predicts subsequent underperformance beyond the level of short interest.

name: Employee Productivity Shock
construction: Compute sales per employee (Compustat SALE / EMP) and take the year-over-year growth, then subindustry-adjust by subtracting the median growth of the firm's 3-digit SIC peers. Rank firms annually each June.
rationale: Above-peer improvement in labor productivity signals durable operational quality and margin expansion that the market is slow to incorporate, predicting higher returns.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: From 10-K MD&A and note disclosures, count the number of named major suppliers accounting for >10% of cost of goods sold. Construct a Herfindahl-style concentration index of disclosed supplier dependence, scaled by COGS/total assets. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the most recent annual filing.
rationale: Firms dependent on few suppliers face uninsurable input-disruption risk that is slow to be priced, commanding a risk premium once supply-chain fragility materializes.

name: Order Backlog Growth Acceleration
construction: Using Compustat item order backlog (OB), compute the second difference of log backlog scaled by sales over the trailing four annual reports (acceleration = current backlog growth minus prior-year backlog growth). Rank firms with reported backlog each June.
rationale: Accelerating backlog signals demand momentum that analysts underweight relative to earnings, generating underreaction and subsequent positive drift.

name: Intraday Range Compression
construction: For each stock, compute the average daily (high-low)/close range over the prior 60 trading days, then divide by the same range measured over the prior 250 days. Values below 1 indicate volatility compression. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.
rationale: Compressed intraday ranges reflect building latent uncertainty and reduced liquidity provision, which precede volatility expansion and demand a premium.

name: Deferred Revenue Momentum
construction: From quarterly balance sheets, compute the year-over-year growth in deferred/unearned revenue (Compustat DRC/DRLT) scaled by total assets, using the four most recent quarters. Rank firms with nonzero deferred revenue monthly following the earnings filing.
rationale: Rising deferred revenue is a leading indicator of future recognized sales and cash flows that is under-scrutinized versus headline earnings, causing predictable drift.

name: Capex Timing Asymmetry
construction: Compute the ratio of fourth-quarter capital expenditures to full-year capital expenditures (from quarterly cash-flow statements). Firms concentrating investment in Q4 score high. Rank annually each March.
rationale: Year-end concentrated capex reflects opportunistic, less-disciplined budget-exhausting spending associated with weaker future returns on investment.

name: Analyst Coverage Dispersion Decay
construction: Using I/B/E/S, measure the change in the standard deviation of analyst long-term growth forecasts over the trailing 6 months, scaled by consensus growth. Negative values (converging opinions) rank high. Update monthly.
rationale: Converging analyst opinions signal resolving uncertainty and declining ambiguity risk, which is followed by positive returns as disagreement-based discounts unwind.

name: Working Capital Efficiency Shock
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle (days inventory + days receivable - days payable) from quarterly data, then measure its year-over-year change. Firms with large improvements (declines) rank high. Update after each quarterly filing.
rationale: Sudden improvements in working-capital efficiency reveal operational discipline and free cash generation that markets are slow to capitalize.
higher_returns_for: large improvement (decline) in cash conversion cycle

name: Debt Maturity Wall Proximity
construction: From long-term debt maturity schedules in 10-K notes, compute the fraction of total debt maturing within the next 24 months, scaled by trailing operating cash flow. Rank firms annually each March.
rationale: A near-term maturity wall relative to internal cash generation embeds refinancing risk that commands a premium when credit conditions are uncertain.
higher_returns_for: high near-term maturity share relative to cash flow

name: Employee Productivity Trend
construction: Compute sales per employee (Compustat SALE/EMP) and measure its three-year compound growth rate. Rank firms with reported employee counts each June.
rationale: Sustained gains in labor productivity reflect improving operating leverage and competitive advantage that are underpriced due to the low salience of headcount data.

name: Return Seasonality Persistence
construction: For each stock, compute the average return in the same calendar month over the prior five years, then form the cross-sectional rank of this historical same-month average each month. Trade the stocks with the highest historical same-month returns.
rationale: Firm-specific seasonal patterns in cash flows and information releases recur but are neglected by investors focused on recent overall performance.

name: Supplier-Customer Inventory Divergence
construction: Using Compustat quarterly data, compute year-over-year growth in a firm's finished-goods inventory (INVFG) minus year-over-year growth in its raw-materials inventory (INVRM). Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter after a 3-month reporting lag.
rationale: Rising finished goods relative to raw materials signals weakening demand and future markdowns not yet reflected in prices, so investors underreact to this early warning of deteriorating sales.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (raw-materials growth exceeding finished-goods growth)

name: Order Backlog Acceleration
construction: From Compustat annual item Order Backlog (OB), scale by total assets, then take the change in this ratio over the prior year minus the change the year before (second difference). Form deciles annually with a 4-month lag.
rationale: Accelerating backlog is a leading indicator of future revenue that the market prices with delay, especially for firms with sparse analyst coverage.

name: Deferred Revenue Momentum
construction: Using Compustat quarterly deferred/unearned revenue (current portion), compute the four-quarter change scaled by lagged sales. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter with a 3-month lag.
rationale: Growing deferred revenue represents cash collected for goods/services yet to be delivered, a hard-to-manipulate signal of contracted future sales that investors underweight relative to reported earnings.

name: Intra-Industry Return Dispersion Beta
construction: For each month, compute the cross-sectional standard deviation of returns within each firm's Fama-French 48 industry using daily data. Then estimate each stock's sensitivity (beta) of its daily returns to daily changes in its own-industry dispersion over a rolling 12-month window. Sort into deciles.
rationale: Stocks that suffer most when their industry's return dispersion spikes bear idiosyncratic disruption risk and should command a premium.
higher_returns_for: high sensitivity (positive dispersion beta stocks that co-move with dispersion earn higher returns, low/negative beta stocks are hedges)

name: Capitalized R&D Vintage Ratio
construction: Build an R&D capital stock via perpetual inventory (15% annual depreciation) from Compustat XRD. Compute the fraction of that stock created in the most recent two fiscal years versus the total. Scale nothing further; rank annually with a 4-month lag among R&D-positive firms.
rationale: Firms with a young R&D stock have innovation whose payoff is furthest from realization and most uncertain, so investors demand higher compensation while systematically underpricing near-term commercialization.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (young R&D vintage)

name: Selling Expense Efficiency Change
construction: From Compustat, compute SG&A (XSGA) minus R&D (XRD) minus advertising (XAD), divided by sales, then take the year-over-year change. Rank cross-sectionally annually with a 4-month lag.
rationale: A declining selling-and-administrative cost ratio reveals improving operating leverage and management discipline that translates into future margin expansion the market is slow to recognize.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (declining selling-cost ratio)

name: Working Capital Turnover Shock
construction: Compute non-cash working capital (current assets minus cash minus current liabilities) from Compustat. Calculate sales-to-working-capital turnover, then measure the standardized change relative to the firm's own prior 8-quarter mean and standard deviation. Sort quarterly with a 3-month lag.
rationale: A positive shock to working-capital turnover indicates the firm is generating more sales per unit of tied-up capital, a sign of improving operational efficiency underappreciated in the short run.

name: Dividend Announcement Timing Consistency
construction: Using CRSP distribution history, measure the standard deviation (in calendar days) of the announcement date of regular dividends over the prior 12 quarters for dividend payers. Sort into deciles.
rationale: Firms with highly regular dividend announcement timing signal managerial stability and low information uncertainty; erratic timing proxies for governance and cash-flow uncertainty that requires a risk premium.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (erratic timing)

name: Tax-Book Income Gap Trend
construction: Estimate taxable income as current tax expense (TXT minus deferred TXDI) divided by the statutory rate. Compute the ratio of estimated taxable income to pretax book income (PI), then take its three-year trend (slope of a regression on time). Rank annually with a 4-month lag.
rationale: A rising taxable-to-book income ratio indicates book earnings are becoming higher quality and less inflated by accruals, predicting fewer future write-downs and positive earnings persistence.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising ratio)

name: Geographic Revenue Concentration
construction: From Compustat geographic segment data, compute a Herfindahl index of sales across reported geographic segments each year. Rank firms into deciles annually with a 4-month lag, within multi-segment reporters.
rationale: Geographically concentrated firms carry undiversified demand and regulatory risk that is not spanned by standard factors, commanding a return premium, while diversified firms are more insulated.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (geographically concentrated firms)

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using firm 10-K disclosures of major customers (SFAS 131 segment data) and Compustat, compute the fraction of a supplier firm's revenue attributable to its largest disclosed customer. For each firm, aggregate the equity return volatility of its top customers (weighted by revenue share) over the trailing 12 months of daily returns. The measure is customer-revenue-share times customer stock volatility, summed across disclosed customers.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few volatile customers bear concentrated demand risk that is slow to be priced due to limited investor attention to supply-chain linkages.

name: Working Capital Acceleration
construction: From quarterly Compustat, compute non-cash working capital (receivables + inventory - payables) scaled by sales for each quarter. Take the second difference across the last three quarters (acceleration), i.e., the change in the change of scaled working capital. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Accelerating working capital signals deteriorating operating efficiency and future earnings disappointments that the market underreacts to relative to level and first-difference signals.

name: Intra-Year Sales Seasonality Shift
construction: Using eight quarters of Compustat quarterly sales, estimate each firm's typical seasonal distribution of sales across the four fiscal quarters from years t-2 and t-1. Compute the absolute deviation of the most recent four quarters' seasonal pattern from the historical pattern. Higher deviation indicates a disrupted seasonal profile.
rationale: Shifts in a firm's habitual seasonal sales pattern reveal changing demand or channel behavior that predicts future fundamentals before analysts adjust expectations.

name: Dispersion of Intangible Investment
construction: Combine R&D expense, advertising expense (SG&A component), and capitalized software from Compustat. Compute the coefficient of variation of these three scaled-by-assets intensities within the firm, measuring how balanced versus lopsided intangible investment is. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Firms with diversified intangible investment portfolios face lower idiosyncratic obsolescence risk, and the market underprices the resilience of balanced intangible strategies.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: From Compustat annual order backlog (Compustat item OB) scaled by total assets, compute the year-over-year change. Where backlog is disclosed, form deciles on the change in scaled backlog. Update annually.
rationale: Growing order backlog is a forward-looking demand signal that leads reported revenue, and investors underreact to this non-earnings fundamental.

name: Debt Maturity Wall Proximity
construction: Using Compustat's schedule of long-term debt maturing in years 1 through 5 (items DD1-DD5), compute the fraction of total debt maturing within the next 24 months. Interact with the firm's interest coverage ratio to flag refinancing stress.
rationale: Firms facing a near-term maturity wall combined with weak coverage bear refinancing risk that is underpriced until rollover becomes imminent.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (less near-term maturing debt earns higher returns; high wall proximity underperforms)

name: Gross Margin Stability Premium
construction: Compute quarterly gross margin (sales minus COGS over sales) over the trailing 12 quarters. Calculate the standard deviation of quarterly gross margin. Rank firms by margin volatility cross-sectionally, controlling for industry.
rationale: Firms with unstable gross margins face uncertain pricing power and input costs, a fundamental risk that carries a return premium under-recognized separately from earnings volatility.

name: Tax Aggressiveness Reversal
construction: Compute the effective tax rate (income tax expense over pretax income) each year. Measure the deviation of the current-year effective rate from the firm's five-year average. Large negative deviations indicate aggressive tax positions likely to reverse.
rationale: Unusually low current tax rates often reflect temporary items that mean-revert, causing future earnings drag that the market fails to anticipate.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (effective rate near or above historical average)

name: Employee Productivity Surprise
construction: Using Compustat number of employees (EMP) and sales, compute sales-per-employee. Calculate the year-over-year growth in sales-per-employee minus the industry-median growth. Rank the abnormal productivity change cross-sectionally, updated annually.
rationale: Improving labor productivity relative to peers signals operational improvement and future margin expansion that is slowly incorporated into prices.

name: Institutional Ownership Breadth Acceleration
construction: From 13F filings, count the number of distinct institutional holders each quarter. Compute the second difference (acceleration) in the number of holders over three quarters, scaled by the prior holder count. Rank cross-sectionally.
rationale: Accelerating breadth of institutional ownership reflects diffusion of positive information and relaxation of short-sale/attention constraints, predicting continued positive returns beyond the level of breadth.

name: Supplier-Customer Inventory Divergence
construction: For each firm, compute year-over-year change in inventory-to-sales ratio from quarterly Compustat (INVTQ/SALEQ). Using the FASB-mandated major customer disclosures (Compustat Segment Customer files), link each firm to its principal customers and compute the customer-weighted change in the customers' inventory-to-sales. The predictor is the firm's own inventory change minus its customers' inventory change, averaged over the trailing 4 quarters.
rationale: When a firm builds inventory while its downstream customers are drawing theirs down, it signals unanticipated demand weakness not yet impounded in the supplier's price, forecasting negative future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (customers building inventory faster than the firm)

name: Order Backlog Momentum Acceleration
construction: Using Compustat annual order backlog (item OB) scaled by total assets, compute the change in backlog/assets from t-2 to t-1 minus the change from t-3 to t-2, i.e., the second difference (acceleration) of scaled backlog over three consecutive fiscal years.
rationale: Accelerating order backlog reflects an improving demand trajectory that investors underweight relative to level information, predicting higher subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (accelerating backlog)

name: Intra-Firm Return Dispersion Across Segments
construction: For multi-segment firms, use Compustat Business Segment data to obtain each segment's SIC code. Assign each segment a value-weighted industry return over the trailing 12 months. Compute the sales-weighted standard deviation of these implied segment industry returns within the firm.
rationale: High dispersion in the fortunes of a firm's constituent businesses creates valuation complexity and limits-to-arbitrage, and diversified firms with wide segment-return dispersion tend to be undervalued, earning higher subsequent returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (wide cross-segment return dispersion)

name: Deferred Revenue Growth Surprise
construction: Extract deferred/unearned revenue from Compustat (current DRC and long-term DRLT). Compute year-over-year growth in total deferred revenue scaled by lagged total assets, then take the residual from a cross-sectional regression on total sales growth. Rank on the residual.
rationale: Rising deferred revenue represents pre-paid future obligations and a leading indicator of subscription/contract demand not reflected in current recognized sales, forecasting higher future earnings and returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (positive deferred revenue growth surprise)

name: Trading Volume Clustering at Round-Number Prices
construction: Using daily CRSP data over the trailing 6 months, compute the fraction of dollar trading volume occurring on days where the closing price is within 0.5% of a round dollar threshold (integer or 0.50 multiples), relative to total volume. Higher clustering indicates greater retail/noise-trader participation.
rationale: Stocks with heavy round-number volume clustering attract sentiment-driven noise traders, leading to overpricing that reverses, so high clustering predicts lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (little round-number clustering)

name: Capitalized R&D-to-Market Momentum
construction: Build an R&D capital stock by accumulating Compustat XRD with a 20% annual depreciation rate over the prior 5 years. Scale this R&D capital by market equity. Interact by sorting: within the high R&D-capital-to-market group, further rank on trailing 6-month price momentum. The signal is the product of standardized R&D-capital/market and standardized momentum.
rationale: Innovation-intensive firms are hard to value; when high intangible intensity coincides with positive momentum, information about R&D payoffs is being gradually incorporated, predicting continued higher returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (high R&D intangibles combined with positive momentum)

name: Analyst Coverage Change Relative to Peers
construction: Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts issuing FY1 estimates for each firm each month. Compute the 12-month change in coverage for the firm minus the median 12-month coverage change of its Fama-French 48-industry peers. Rank on the peer-adjusted change.
rationale: A relative increase in analyst coverage signals rising institutional interest and reduced information asymmetry ahead of good news, whereas relative coverage declines precede neglect and underperformance.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (rising coverage relative to peers)

name: Working Capital Efficiency Trend
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle (days receivable + days inventory - days payable) using Compustat quarterly items (RECTQ, INVTQ, APQ, SALEQ, COGSQ). Fit a linear trend to the trailing 8 quarters of the cash conversion cycle and use the negative of the slope (improving efficiency = shrinking cycle) as the signal.
