rationale: A consistently shortening cash conversion cycle reflects improving operational efficiency and management quality that the market underappreciates, forecasting higher returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (steadily improving/shrinking cash conversion cycle)

name: Idiosyncratic Volatility Asymmetry (Up vs Down Days)
construction: Using daily returns over the trailing 12 months, regress firm returns on the Fama-French three factors. Compute the residual standard deviation separately on days when the market return was positive versus negative. The signal is downside residual volatility minus upside residual volatility.
rationale: Stocks whose idiosyncratic risk concentrates on market-down days carry undesirable crash exposure and must offer higher expected returns as compensation.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (higher downside than upside idiosyncratic volatility)

name: Pension Plan Asset Allocation Aggressiveness
construction: From Compustat pension footnote data, compute the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets (PPROR) and the equity allocation of plan assets. Rank firms on the residual of expected return regressed on funded status and firm size; high residuals indicate aggressive return assumptions.
rationale: Firms setting aggressive pension return assumptions inflate reported earnings and signal lower-quality accruals, leading to negative future return correction as reality falls short.
higher_returns_for: low values of the measure (conservative pension return assumptions)

name: Supplier-Concentration Fragility
construction: Using 10-K disclosures and the Compustat Segment/Customer files, count the number of major suppliers a firm depends on and compute a Herfindahl index of purchase concentration when disclosed; where supplier detail is sparse, proxy using cost-of-goods-sold volatility (standard deviation of quarterly COGS/sales over trailing 12 quarters) as an inverse measure of supply diversification. Rank firms cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Firms reliant on few suppliers bear un-diversified input-cost and disruption risk that is not fully priced, commanding a risk premium.
higher_returns_for: high supplier concentration / high COGS volatility

name: Inventory-Mix Shift
construction: For manufacturers, decompose total inventory into raw materials, work-in-process, and finished goods from Compustat (INVRM, INVWIP, INVFG). Compute the year-over-year change in the finished-goods share of total inventory. Rank firms by this change each quarter after earnings.
rationale: A rising finished-goods share signals weakening demand and future markdowns not yet reflected in prices, predicting lower returns.

name: Deferred Revenue Acceleration
construction: Using quarterly Compustat deferred revenue (current plus long-term), compute the second difference (acceleration) in deferred revenue scaled by lagged total assets over trailing four quarters. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Accelerating deferred revenue reflects growing bookings of future obligations and recurring demand that the market underweights relative to reported earnings.

name: Intra-Year Earnings Seasonality Strength
construction: For each firm, regress the last 20 quarters of seasonally-differenced earnings surprises and compute the autocorrelation of same-quarter-prior-year earnings growth. Form a score capturing how strongly a firm's same-calendar-quarter earnings tend to repeat. Buy stocks entering their historically strong quarter.
rationale: Predictable calendar-quarter earnings patterns are underreacted to by investors who anchor on recent quarters rather than seasonal analogs.
higher_returns_for: high seasonality score entering a historically strong quarter

name: Capitalized R&D Vintage Skew
construction: Build an R&D capital stock using perpetual inventory (15% annual depreciation) from Compustat XRD, then compute the fraction of the stock originating in the most recent two fiscal years versus older vintages. Rank firms by the recent-vintage fraction.
rationale: Firms with young, fresh R&D pipelines have optionality and innovation not yet monetized, which the market values with a lag.

name: Dividend-Timing Consistency
construction: For dividend payers, compute the standard deviation of the calendar day-of-quarter on which dividends are declared and paid over the trailing 12 quarters using CRSP distribution dates. Lower dispersion means highly punctual payers. Rank firms by punctuality.
rationale: Managerial discipline in payout timing proxies for governance quality and cash-flow predictability, earning a modest premium mispriced by investors focused only on yield.

name: Asset-Liquidation Value Gap
construction: Estimate liquidation value as cash + 0.75*receivables + 0.5*inventory + 0.5*net PP&E from Compustat, minus total liabilities. Scale by market cap to form a liquidation-to-price ratio. Rank cross-sectionally, focusing on the extreme high tail.
rationale: Stocks trading below tangible liquidation value carry a downside-protected deep-value premium under-arbitraged in small caps.

name: Short-Horizon Volume-Volatility Divergence
construction: Over the trailing 21 trading days, compute the correlation between daily dollar volume and daily absolute return using CRSP. A low or negative correlation indicates trading not driven by information. Rank firms by this correlation.
rationale: When volume decouples from volatility, trading is liquidity- or noise-driven, creating temporary mispricing that reverses, so low-divergence names outperform.

name: Tax-Loss Carryforward Utilization Momentum
construction: From Compustat and 10-K tax footnotes, track net operating loss carryforwards and compute the trailing-year decline in NOL balance as a share of pretax income (utilization rate). Rank firms by rising utilization.
rationale: Accelerating NOL utilization signals a durable return to profitability and shielded future cash flows that analysts capitalize slowly.

name: Geographic Revenue Dispersion
construction: Using Compustat geographic segment data, compute a Herfindahl index of revenue across reported geographic regions. Low concentration means geographically diversified revenue. Rank firms cross-sectionally by dispersion.
rationale: Geographically concentrated firms bear un-diversifiable regional macro risk that commands a premium, while the market underprices this exposure.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using 10-K disclosures under SFAS 131 that require reporting of major customers accounting for >10% of revenue, and Compustat segment data, construct a Herfindahl index of a firm's customer-revenue concentration. Combine with the customer firms' trailing 12-month stock return volatility (from CRSP) weighted by revenue share to form a 'demand fragility' score. Reconstitute annually after fiscal-year 10-K filings.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few volatile customers bear undiversified demand risk that is slow to be priced because customer linkages are disclosed only in footnotes; investors underweight this concentration risk.
higher_returns_for: high customer concentration combined with high customer volatility

name: Intra-Year Earnings Seasonality Persistence
construction: For each firm, regress quarterly earnings surprises (actual minus seasonal-random-walk expectation, scaled by price) over the prior 20 quarters on calendar-quarter dummies. Measure the fraction of a firm's earnings surprise historically concentrated in its strongest fiscal quarter. Rank stocks in the month before that historically strong quarter's earnings announcement.
rationale: Firms with a persistent same-quarter positive surprise pattern have predictable earnings news that a slow-moving market does not fully anticipate ahead of the announcement.
higher_returns_for: high historical surprise concentration in the upcoming quarter

name: Working Capital Acceleration
construction: Compute the second difference (acceleration) of non-cash net working capital scaled by average total assets: change in the year-over-year change of (current assets minus cash minus current liabilities plus short-term debt). Use annual Compustat. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Accelerating working capital investment signals aggressive over-expansion and lower-quality growth that reverses, extending the accruals anomaly to its rate of change rather than its level.

name: Text-Based Risk Factor Growth
construction: Parse the Item 1A 'Risk Factors' section (mandated for 10-Ks since 2005) and count the number of distinct risk-factor bullet items and total word count. Compute the year-over-year percentage change in risk-section length after removing boilerplate. Rank firms annually.
rationale: A rising volume of disclosed risk language reflects managers signaling deteriorating fundamentals and rising uncertainty that the market underreacts to given the qualitative, unstructured nature of the disclosure.
higher_returns_for: low growth in risk-factor disclosure length

name: Dispersion of Intraday Return Signs
construction: Using TAQ or daily high-low-open-close data, for each stock compute over the prior quarter the fraction of days where the intraday (open-to-close) return sign differs from the overnight (prior close-to-open) return sign. Standardize cross-sectionally each month.
rationale: Frequent disagreement between overnight (information-driven) and intraday (liquidity/noise-trader-driven) returns indicates information asymmetry and unresolved uncertainty, commanding a risk premium.

name: Capitalized R&D Vintage Skew
construction: Build a stock of R&D capital using a 20% annual depreciation of the prior five years of R&D expense (Compustat XRD). Compute the share of the R&D capital stock that is from the most recent year ('young R&D fraction'). Rank R&D-active firms annually each June.
rationale: Firms whose innovation capital is dominated by recent, unproven spending carry greater intangible-value uncertainty that is mispriced because standard accounting expenses R&D immediately, obscuring the age profile.
higher_returns_for: low young-R&D fraction (mature, seasoned innovation capital)

name: Institutional Ownership Breadth Momentum
construction: From 13F filings, compute the quarter-over-quarter change in the number of distinct institutions holding a stock, scaled by prior count. Take a two-quarter change to capture the trajectory of breadth. Rank stocks the month after 13F filing deadlines.
rationale: Accelerating breadth of institutional ownership signals gradual relaxation of short-sale and information constraints, predicting continued positive revaluation as more investors enter, extending breadth-of-ownership effects to their dynamics.

name: Cost Stickiness Asymmetry
construction: Estimate for each firm, over rolling 16 quarters, the differential response of SG&A costs to sales increases versus sales decreases (regress log change in SG&A on log change in sales plus an interaction with a sales-decrease dummy). The stickiness coefficient measures how slowly costs fall when sales fall. Rank annually.
rationale: Firms with sticky costs have operating leverage that amplifies earnings declines during downturns; this asymmetric risk is underpriced because it only manifests in bad states.
higher_returns_for: high cost stickiness (higher compensation for downside operating risk)

name: Pension Discount Rate Aggressiveness
construction: From 10-K pension footnotes, extract the assumed discount rate and expected return on plan assets. Compute the firm's assumptions minus the industry median for the same year. Higher positive deviations indicate aggressive assumptions that understate liabilities and inflate reported earnings. Rank firms with defined-benefit plans annually.
rationale: Aggressive pension assumptions inflate current earnings quality and mask future funding obligations; the market underweights these footnote assumptions, so aggressive firms subsequently underperform.

name: Order Backlog Conversion Ratio
construction: For firms reporting order backlog (Compustat item OB), compute the ratio of current-year revenue to prior-year-end backlog, and its change versus the prior year. A declining conversion ratio indicates backlog growth outpacing realized sales. Rank annually among backlog-reporting firms.
rationale: Growing backlog that is not converting into revenue signals either demand strength not yet in earnings (positive) or execution problems; the disclosed but non-standard backlog data is slow to be incorporated into prices.
higher_returns_for: high backlog relative to realized revenue (unconverted demand pipeline)

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: From annual 10-K disclosures under SFAS 131, identify firms that report dependence on one or more major suppliers accounting for 10%+ of purchases (parsed from text). Construct a dummy = 1 if the firm reports a concentrated supplier base, refined by counting the number of named critical suppliers scaled inversely. Combine with inventory-to-COGS ratio to proxy buffer capacity. Rank cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms reliant on few suppliers face under-priced disruption risk; investors underweight the tail risk of input shocks, requiring a return premium.
higher_returns_for: high supplier concentration (few critical suppliers, low inventory buffer)

name: Deferred Revenue Momentum
construction: Using quarterly balance-sheet deferred revenue (current + long-term), compute the year-over-year growth rate in deferred revenue scaled by total assets. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter on the four-quarter trend in this ratio.
rationale: Growth in deferred revenue reflects contracted but unrecognized future sales, a leading indicator of demand that is slow to be incorporated into prices.

name: Working Capital Acceleration
construction: Compute non-cash net working capital (receivables + inventory - payables) scaled by sales for each of the last 8 quarters. Fit the second difference (acceleration) of this ratio. Rank firms on the acceleration term, controlling for level and first difference via cross-sectional regression residuals each quarter.
rationale: Accelerating working capital signals deteriorating operational efficiency and unsustainable growth financing that the market prices with a lag.

name: Analyst Coverage Dispersion Decay
construction: From I/B/E/S detail files, measure the month-over-month change in the standard deviation of individual analyst FY1 EPS estimates, scaled by price. Compute the 3-month change in dispersion. Rank firms cross-sectionally on the decline (convergence) of estimates.
rationale: Converging analyst estimates signal resolving information uncertainty; as ambiguity resolves favorably, prices drift upward before full incorporation.

name: Capital Expenditure Text Intensity
construction: Parse the MD&A section of 10-K filings for frequency of forward-looking capex and expansion language (terms like 'expand capacity', 'new facility', 'capital investment') normalized by document length. Combine with realized capex/assets to form a residual of 'talk vs. spend'. Rank firms each June.
rationale: Firms that announce expansion intentions beyond realized spending exhibit managerial overconfidence and overinvestment, predicting lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: low text-to-spend residual (spending exceeds announced intentions)

name: Seasonal Earnings Persistence Gap
construction: For each firm, regress quarterly earnings on the same-quarter earnings one year prior over a rolling 5-year window to estimate seasonal persistence. Separately estimate adjacent-quarter persistence. Rank firms on the gap (seasonal minus adjacent persistence coefficient).
rationale: Firms with strong seasonal but weak sequential earnings persistence have predictable earnings the market under-anticipates in specific quarters.
higher_returns_for: high seasonal persistence gap ahead of strong quarters

name: Intangible-Adjusted Asset Growth
construction: Capitalize R&D and a fraction of SG&A as intangible assets using perpetual-inventory method with standard amortization rates, add to reported total assets. Compute year-over-year growth of this adjusted asset base. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: The classic asset-growth anomaly ignores intangible investment; adjusting reveals that firms growing true (tangible+intangible) capital fastest overinvest and underperform.

name: Debt Maturity Wall Proximity
construction: From Compustat debt maturity schedule (debt due in years 1-5), compute the share of total debt maturing within the next 12 months, scaled by cash plus operating cash flow. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Firms facing imminent large refinancing relative to liquidity bear rollover risk that is under-priced outside of crisis periods, commanding a premium.
higher_returns_for: high near-term maturity relative to liquidity

name: Order Backlog Surprise
construction: Using reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) scaled by sales, compute the change relative to its own 3-year average and relative to the seasonal norm. Rank firms cross-sectionally on positive backlog surprises each fiscal period.
rationale: Backlog is a forward demand signal disclosed by manufacturers that receives limited investor attention, generating post-disclosure drift.

name: Gross Margin Volatility Compression
construction: Compute the rolling 12-quarter standard deviation of quarterly gross margin (gross profit/sales). Measure the ratio of recent 4-quarter volatility to the trailing 12-quarter volatility. Rank firms on the compression (recent volatility falling relative to history).
rationale: Declining margin volatility signals stabilizing competitive position and pricing power, a fundamental improvement priced with delay.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using footnote disclosures in 10-K filings (SFAS 131 segment/customer data) and the Compustat Segment file, count the number of major customers accounting for >10% of a firm's revenue. Construct a Herfindahl index of revenue concentration across disclosed major customers. Firms are sorted each June on this concentration index.
rationale: Firms dependent on a few large customers face idiosyncratic demand-shock risk that is imperfectly priced, and the market underreacts to the fragility of concentrated revenue streams until shocks materialize.
higher_returns_for: high customer concentration (compensation for bearing customer-specific risk)

name: Working Capital Acceleration
construction: For each firm-quarter, compute non-cash working capital = (current assets - cash) - (current liabilities - short-term debt), scaled by total assets. Compute the second difference (acceleration) over the trailing four quarters: change in the year-over-year change of scaled working capital. Sort stocks each quarter.
rationale: Accelerating working capital signals deteriorating operating efficiency and aggressive accrual buildup beyond simple accrual levels, which the market fails to fully discount.

name: Intra-Year Earnings Volatility Trend
construction: Using quarterly EPS over the trailing eight quarters, compute the standard deviation of the four most recent quarterly earnings surprises minus the standard deviation of the prior four. A positive value indicates rising earnings noise. Sort stocks each quarter on this change in earnings dispersion.
rationale: Rising quarter-to-quarter earnings instability reflects increasing fundamental uncertainty and lower earnings quality that investors underweight relative to point-estimate surprises.

name: Order Flow Persistence Signature
construction: Using daily TAQ trade data, classify trades via the Lee-Ready algorithm into buyer/seller initiated. Compute the first-order autocorrelation of daily signed order-flow imbalance over the trailing 60 trading days. Sort stocks monthly on this autocorrelation.
rationale: Persistent one-sided order flow indicates gradual informed accumulation or distribution not yet reflected in price, predicting continuation.
higher_returns_for: high positive order-flow autocorrelation combined with net buying

name: R&D Reinvestment Momentum
construction: From Compustat, compute the trailing three-year growth rate of R&D expense scaled by sales, and separately the two-year change in gross margin. Rank firms on the interaction: high R&D-intensity growth accompanied by improving gross margins. Form the composite score annually each June.
rationale: Rising research investment that coincides with margin expansion signals successful innovation whose payoff the market underappreciates due to R&D's delayed, uncertain returns.
higher_returns_for: high R&D growth paired with improving margins

name: Debt Maturity Wall Proximity
construction: From Compustat, compute the fraction of total long-term debt scheduled to mature within the next two years (using debt-maturity structure items dd1, dd2). Interact with the firm's interest coverage ratio. Sort firms annually, isolating those with a high near-term maturity fraction and weak coverage.
rationale: Firms facing imminent refinancing needs bear rollover and credit-spread risk that is undercompensated during calm periods and severely penalized in stress, generating a risk premium.
higher_returns_for: high near-term maturity fraction with weak coverage (refinancing risk premium)

name: Analyst Coverage Breadth Change
construction: Using I/B/E/S, compute the twelve-month change in the number of unique analysts issuing estimates, scaled by firm size decile. Focus on the residual change after controlling for size and past returns. Sort stocks monthly.
rationale: Increasing analyst attention reduces information asymmetry and expands the investor base, predicting positive returns as the stock is gradually incorporated into more portfolios.

name: Capitalized Operating Lease Intensity Shock
construction: From 10-K lease footnotes, capitalize future minimum operating lease commitments (discounted at 8%) to build an adjusted asset base. Compute the year-over-year change in capitalized-lease-to-total-adjusted-assets. Sort firms annually on this change.
rationale: Rapid expansion of off-balance-sheet lease obligations increases hidden operating leverage and financial fragility that standard leverage measures miss, and is undervalued as risk.
higher_returns_for: high increase in capitalized lease intensity (hidden leverage risk premium)

name: Seasonal Sales Dispersion
construction: Using quarterly sales over the trailing five years, compute each firm's seasonal concentration as the Herfindahl index of the four calendar-quarter sales shares. Then compute the deviation of the most recent year's seasonal pattern from the historical average. Sort stocks quarterly on this seasonal-pattern deviation.
rationale: Departures from a firm's established seasonal sales rhythm signal changing demand conditions that investors, anchored to historical seasonality, are slow to price.
higher_returns_for: positive deviation (recent sales stronger than seasonal norm)

name: Insider Trading Cluster Divergence
construction: From SEC Form 4 filings (Thomson Reuters insider data), compute the net dollar value of open-market insider purchases minus sales over the trailing six months, scaled by market cap. Separately measure the dispersion of directions across distinct insiders. Rank firms with strong net buying and high insider agreement (low dispersion).
rationale: Consensus buying across multiple insiders conveys stronger private information about undervaluation than isolated trades, predicting positive future returns.
higher_returns_for: high net insider buying with strong cross-insider agreement

name: Customer Concentration Drift
construction: Using SFAS 131 segment disclosures from 10-K filings, identify firms reporting major customers (each >10% of sales). Compute the fraction of total sales attributable to named major customers for the current and prior fiscal year, and take the year-over-year change (drift). Sort stocks cross-sectionally on this drift each June.
rationale: Rising dependence on a few customers increases cash-flow fragility and bargaining-power risk that is slow to be priced, so firms whose customer base is diversifying should earn a premium reduction while concentrating firms carry undercompensated risk.

name: Accrual Volatility Scaled by Cash Flow
construction: For each firm compute total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation) each quarter for the trailing 12 quarters. Take the standard deviation of quarterly accruals and divide by the mean absolute operating cash flow over the same window. Rank stocks each quarter.
rationale: Erratic accruals relative to stable cash generation signal low earnings quality and information risk that investors underappreciate, leading to future underperformance.
higher_returns_for: low accrual volatility relative to cash flow

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: Extract reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) at fiscal year end, scale by total assets, and compute the change in backlog-to-assets from the prior fiscal year. Form cross-sectional deciles each year using data with a 4-month reporting lag.
rationale: Growing backlog is a forward-looking demand signal that predicts future revenue and earnings but is buried in filings and slowly incorporated into prices.

name: Intangible-Adjusted Book-to-Market Gap
construction: Capitalize R&D and advertising expenses using a perpetual-inventory method (R&D amortized over 5 years, advertising over 2), add the capitalized stock to reported book equity, and compute an adjusted book-to-market. Take the difference between adjusted and unadjusted book-to-market as the gap and rank stocks.
rationale: Firms whose value is understated by GAAP due to expensed intangibles are systematically underpriced, and the size of the accounting distortion proxies for the mispricing.

name: Dispersion of Intraday Returns
construction: Using daily open, high, low, close prices over the prior month, compute the Parkinson high-low range volatility for each day and take the standard deviation of these daily range measures across the month, scaled by average price. Sort stocks monthly.
rationale: Instability in intraday price ranges reflects heightened disagreement and lottery-like demand that leads to overpricing and subsequent low returns.

name: Supplier-Side Inventory Buildup
construction: Decompose inventory into raw materials, work-in-process, and finished goods using Compustat detail items. Compute the growth in finished-goods inventory relative to sales growth over the trailing year. Rank firms on this excess finished-goods growth.
rationale: Finished-goods accumulation outpacing sales signals weakening demand and future markdowns that the market prices with a lag.

name: Financing Activity Consistency
construction: Over the trailing 5 years, count the number of years in which the firm was a net issuer of equity plus debt (positive external financing from the cash flow statement). Combine with the sign persistence to build a consistency score, then rank firms.
rationale: Persistent reliance on external financing indicates value-destroying overinvestment and agency problems that erode future returns, beyond a single-year issuance signal.
higher_returns_for: low financing activity consistency (persistent net repurchasers/de-levering firms)

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Compute quarterly gross margin (gross profit / sales) over trailing 16 quarters and measure the coefficient of variation. Combine with the trailing average margin level and rank on the ratio of average margin to its volatility (a margin Sharpe ratio).
rationale: Stable high margins reflect durable competitive advantage that is undervalued relative to volatile margins, generating persistent excess returns.
higher_returns_for: high gross margin stability (high margin-to-volatility ratio)

name: Tax Expense Surprise
construction: Estimate an expected effective tax rate from the trailing 3-year average, apply it to current pretax income to get expected tax, and compute the standardized difference between actual and expected tax expense. Rank stocks quarterly using the sign and magnitude of the surprise (unexpectedly low taxes = positive signal).
rationale: Lower-than-expected tax burdens reveal favorable private information about future profitability that management manages into taxes before it appears elsewhere in earnings.
higher_returns_for: high positive tax expense surprise (unexpectedly low taxes)

name: Analyst Coverage Momentum
construction: Using IBES, compute the change in the number of distinct analysts issuing estimates over the trailing 6 months, scaled by the beginning count. Sort stocks monthly into deciles on this coverage growth.
rationale: Rising analyst attention brings previously neglected, underpriced stocks into investor awareness, resolving information frictions and driving positive drift.

name: Supplier Concentration Fragility
construction: Using segment and 10-K text data (Compustat segments plus disclosed major-customer concentration under SFAS 131), compute the fraction of a firm's cost of goods sold attributable to its top identified suppliers, proxied by inventory/COGS volatility combined with a Herfindahl index of reported input categories. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.
rationale: Firms dependent on a concentrated set of suppliers face under-priced disruption risk; investors underweight the tail risk of input-side shocks, so these firms must offer a return premium.

name: Order Backlog Momentum
construction: For firms reporting order backlog (Compustat item OB), compute the year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by lagged total assets, then take the change in that growth rate over the trailing four quarters. Form deciles at each fiscal quarter-end.
rationale: Accelerating backlog signals future revenue not yet in reported earnings; the market underreacts to this forward-looking non-price demand signal.

name: Working Capital Efficiency Surprise
construction: Compute the cash conversion cycle (days inventory + days receivable - days payable) each quarter. Define the surprise as the current CCC minus the trailing 8-quarter average CCC, standardized by its own historical standard deviation. Sort into deciles.
rationale: Unexpected improvements in operating working capital efficiency reveal management quality and future free-cash-flow gains that the market prices slowly.

name: Intangible Investment Intensity Gap
construction: Estimate a firm's knowledge-and-organization capital by capitalizing 30% of SG&A and 100% of R&D with perpetual-inventory depreciation, then compute the ratio of this intangible capital to book value of physical assets (PPE). Compare each firm to its industry median and rank the gap.
rationale: Accounting understates intangible-heavy firms' true asset base, causing systematic mispricing that resolves as intangibles convert to earnings.

name: Dividend Smoothness Ratio
construction: Over the trailing 20 quarters, regress quarterly dividends per share on quarterly earnings per share; the smoothness measure is one minus the ratio of dividend volatility to earnings volatility. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Firms that deliberately smooth dividends signal confidence in persistent cash flows; the market underappreciates the information content of dividend-policy stability.

name: Analyst Coverage Attrition
construction: Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts issuing estimates each month and compute the trailing 12-month net decline in coverage scaled by prior coverage. Sort firms losing the most coverage into a short-leg and stable/rising coverage into a long-leg.
rationale: Declining analyst attention increases information asymmetry and neglect; among neglected stocks with intact fundamentals, a return premium accrues to compensate for reduced visibility.
higher_returns_for: high coverage attrition among fundamentally stable firms

name: Capex Cyclicality Beta
construction: For each firm, estimate the sensitivity (beta) of annual capital-expenditure growth to aggregate industrial-production growth over a rolling 5-year window using annual Compustat capex. Rank firms by this cyclicality beta.
rationale: Firms whose investment strongly co-moves with the macro cycle bear higher systematic investment-timing risk that is not captured by market beta, demanding a premium.

name: Earnings Announcement Return Consistency
construction: Over the trailing eight earnings announcements, compute the fraction that generated positive 3-day abnormal returns and the mean of those abnormal returns; combine into a consistency z-score. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.
rationale: Persistent positive announcement reactions reflect a durable pattern of positive surprises that the market fails to fully extrapolate, creating an under-reaction premium.

name: Debt Maturity Concentration
construction: From Compustat debt-maturity schedule items (debt due in years 1-5), compute a Herfindahl index of the maturity distribution; higher values indicate large debt maturing in a single near-term year. Rank firms each fiscal year.
rationale: Concentrated near-term refinancing needs expose firms to rollover and credit-market risk that is under-priced, so these firms carry a risk premium.

name: Gross Margin Stability Premium
construction: Compute the coefficient of variation of quarterly gross margin (gross profit / sales) over the trailing 12 quarters. Sort firms into deciles by the inverse of this variability (stability).
rationale: Stable gross margins indicate pricing power and defensible economics that the market undervalues relative to headline growth, yielding superior risk-adjusted returns.

name: Customer Concentration
construction: Calculate the percentage of sales derived from a firm's major customers. Use annual report disclosures.
rationale: Firms with high customer concentration may face higher business risks.

name: Product Diversity
construction: Compute the number of distinct product lines offered by a firm. Use annual report disclosures.
rationale: Firms with a diverse product portfolio may be more resilient to industry shocks.
higher_returns_for: Firms with more diverse product lines

name: Employee Satisfaction
construction: Collect data on employee satisfaction from public surveys and compute a firm-level average. Normalize by industry.
rationale: Firms with satisfied employees may have higher productivity.

name: M&A Activity
construction: Count the number of M&A deals a firm has completed in the past year. Use SEC filings and news sources.
rationale: Firms actively participating in M&A may be seeking growth or strategic advantages.

name: Geographic Expansion
construction: Measure the number of countries a firm is operating in. Use annual report disclosures.
rationale: Firms operating internationally may have diversified risks.

name: Patent Activity
construction: Count the number of patents a firm has applied for in the past year. Use USPTO data.
rationale: Firms with high patent activity are likely investing in innovation.

name: Political Connections
construction: Measure the number of ex-politicians or high-ranking government officials serving in executive or board positions. Use annual report disclosures.
rationale: Firms with political connections may have competitive advantages.

name: Quality of Management
construction: Create a score for the quality of management based on surveys or expert opinions. Normalize by industry.
rationale: Firms with high-quality management may perform better.

name: Environmental Performance
construction: Assess the firm's environmental impact using publicly available data on waste production, energy use, etc. Normalize by industry.
rationale: Firms with better environmental performance may face fewer regulatory risks and may be more sustainable in the long run.

name: Supply Chain Efficiency
construction: Create a score for supply chain efficiency based on factors like inventory turnover, delivery times, etc. Use annual report disclosures and normalize by industry.
rationale: Firms with efficient supply chains may have lower operating costs and higher profit margins.
higher_returns_for: Firms with more efficient supply chains

name: Debt Maturity Structure
construction: The proportion of a firm's debt that is due to mature in the next year. Calculated as short-term debt divided by total debt.
rationale: Firms with a larger proportion of short-term debt may face higher refinancing risk, which could signal financial distress and lead to higher expected returns.

name: Earnings Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of the firm's earnings over the past five years.
rationale: Firms with more volatile earnings might be riskier and require a higher expected return to compensate investors.

name: Investment Age
construction: The weighted average age of the firm's capital stock, using depreciation rates to weight the age of each vintage.
rationale: Older capital may be less productive or more prone to obsolescence, requiring higher expected returns to compensate for the risk.

name: Product Market Competition
construction: Inverse of the firm's market share in its primary industry.
rationale: Firms in more competitive markets may face higher business risk, leading to higher expected returns.

name: R&D Intensity
construction: Research and development expenditures divided by total sales.
rationale: Firms that invest heavily in R&D may be taking on higher risk projects with uncertain outcomes, leading to higher expected returns.

name: Dividend Persistence
construction: Number of consecutive years a firm has paid dividends.
rationale: Firms with a longer history of dividend payments may be perceived as less risky, leading to lower expected returns.

name: Labor Intensity
construction: Ratio of employee compensation to total assets.
rationale: Firms with higher labor intensity might be more vulnerable to wage shocks, leading to higher expected returns to compensate for the risk.

name: Geographic Diversification
construction: Number of different geographic markets in which the firm operates.
rationale: Firms that are more geographically diversified may be less vulnerable to local economic shocks, leading to lower expected returns.

name: Tax Exposure
construction: Ratio of total taxes paid to pre-tax income.
rationale: Firms with higher tax exposure might face higher financial distress risk, requiring higher expected returns to compensate investors.

name: Customer Concentration
construction: Revenue from the firm's largest customer as a percentage of total revenue.
rationale: Firms that rely heavily on a single customer may face higher business risk, leading to higher expected returns.

name: Dividend Revision
construction: Measure as the change in a firm's annual dividend announcement from the previous year.
rationale: An increase in dividends may signal future profitability and strong financial health to the market.
higher_returns_for: Firms with larger positive dividend revisions.

name: Inventory Turnover Growth
construction: Measure as the change in the ratio of cost of goods sold to the average inventory level over the past year.
rationale: Growing inventory turnover could signify increasing sales efficiency, likely leading to boosted profitability.
higher_returns_for: Firms with higher growth in inventory turnover.

name: Debt Coverage Momentum
construction: Calculate the change in the ratio of earnings before interest and taxes to interest expenses.
rationale: Increasing ability to cover debt obligations may signal a strengthening of the firm's financial stability.
higher_returns_for: Firms with larger positive changes in debt coverage ratio.

name: Asset Efficiency Evolution
construction: Measure as the change in the ratio of sales to total assets over the past year.
rationale: Improvements in asset efficiency may suggest better management or healthier financial status.
higher_returns_for: Firms with larger positive changes in asset efficiency ratio.

name: Shareholder Yield
construction: Calculate as the sum of dividend yield and buyback yield.
rationale: Firms returning more cash to shareholders may be undervalued or have excess cash.

name: Cash Flow Volatility
construction: Calculate as the standard deviation of the firm's cash flow over the past five years.
rationale: High cash flow volatility could indicate riskier, potentially higher-return investment opportunities.
higher_returns_for: Firms with high cash flow volatility.

name: CEO Tenure
construction: Measure as the number of years the current CEO has been in office.
rationale: Longer CEO tenure might imply more stability and potentially better future returns.

name: Tax Rate Persistence
construction: Calculate as the stability of the firm's effective tax rate over the past five years.
rationale: Firms with stable tax rates may have less financial uncertainty, potentially leading to lower risk and higher returns.
higher_returns_for: Firms with more persistent tax rates.

name: Employee Growth
construction: Measure as the percentage change in the number of a firm's employees over the past year.
rationale: Growing employee base could signal expansion and positive future outlook.

name: Research & Development Intensity
construction: Calculate as the ratio of a firm's research and development expenses to its total assets.
rationale: Higher R&D intensity could indicate more investment in potential growth opportunities.

name: Inventory Turnover
construction: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) divided by Average Inventory for the fiscal year
rationale: Firms with higher inventory turnover may be more efficient in managing their resources, which could lead to higher profitability and returns.

name: Dividend Surprise
construction: Actual dividends paid compared to analyst consensus estimates, computed quarterly
rationale: Firms that pay higher dividends than expected may be more profitable or financially healthy than anticipated, leading to positive price reactions.

name: Earnings Announcement Drift
construction: Cumulative abnormal return from two days after quarterly earnings announcement to the next earnings announcement
rationale: If markets are slow to incorporate earnings news, there might be a drift in stock prices following the announcement.

name: Tax Rate
construction: Total Taxes Paid divided by Pre-Tax Income for the fiscal year
rationale: Firms with lower tax rates might have more net income and cash available for growth or dividends, leading to higher returns.

name: Capital Expenditure Growth
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in capital expenditures
rationale: Firms that are investing heavily in their business might be expected to grow faster, leading to higher stock returns.

name: CEO Age
construction: Age of the CEO at the end of the fiscal year
rationale: Older CEOs might be more conservative in their business approach, which might lead to lower volatility and higher returns.

name: Productivity
construction: Revenue divided by the number of employees at the end of the fiscal year
rationale: Firms with higher productivity may be more efficient, leading to higher profitability and returns.

name: Geographic Diversification
construction: Number of countries in which the firm operates at the end of the fiscal year
rationale: Firms operating in more countries might have more diversified revenue streams, reducing risk and potentially leading to higher returns.

name: Customer Concentration
construction: Percentage of revenue that comes from the firm's largest customer
rationale: Firms that rely heavily on a single customer might have more business risk, which could be reflected in their stock returns.

name: Litigation Risk
construction: Number of ongoing lawsuits against the firm at the end of the fiscal year
rationale: Firms with more litigation risk might have more uncertainty about their future cash flows, which could lead to lower stock returns.

name: Inventory Turnover
construction: Cost of Goods Sold divided by Inventory
rationale: Firms with higher inventory turnover might be managing their resources more efficiently, leading to higher profitability and thus higher stock returns

name: Cash to Total Assets
construction: Cash and Cash Equivalents divided by Total Assets
rationale: Firms with more cash could be more financially stable and less reliant on external financing, potentially leading to higher stock returns

name: R&D Intensity
construction: R&D Expenditure divided by Sales
rationale: Firms investing more in R&D might have a higher potential for future growth

name: Employee Turnover
construction: Number of employees leaving the company divided by Total number of employees
rationale: Firms with lower employee turnover might have more stable operations and employee expertise, which could translate to higher returns

name: Debt Maturity
construction: Long-term Debt divided by Total Debt
rationale: Firms with longer debt maturity might have lower financial distress risk

name: Capital Expenditure Intensity
construction: Capital Expenditure divided by Total Assets
rationale: Firms with higher capital expenditure intensity might be investing more in their growth, potentially leading to higher stock returns

name: Dividend Payout Ratio
construction: Dividends divided by Net Income
rationale: Firms with higher dividend payout ratios might be more profitable, which could lead to higher stock returns

name: Operating Cash Flow Margin
construction: Operating Cash Flow divided by Sales
rationale: Firms with higher operating cash flow margins could be more financially healthy

name: Age of Firm
construction: Current Year minus Year of Incorporation
rationale: Older firms might have more established market positions and thus higher stock returns

name: Employee Satisfaction
construction: Employee satisfaction survey results
rationale: Firms with higher employee satisfaction might have more productive and loyal employees, leading to better operational performance and higher stock returns

name: Dividend Coverage Ratio
construction: Annual net income divided by annual dividends paid
rationale: Companies with a high dividend coverage ratio are potentially well-positioned to continue paying dividends, which might attract investors and increase demand for the stock.

name: Revenue Variability
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly revenue over the past 5 years
rationale: Higher variability in revenues might indicate higher risk, which could demand a higher risk premium and thus higher average returns.

name: Price/Earnings Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of daily price/earnings ratios over the past year
rationale: Higher volatility in P/E ratios may reflect uncertainty about a firm's earnings prospects, which could command a higher risk premium.

name: Capital Expenditures Growth
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in annual capital expenditures
rationale: Greater capital expenditures could signal future growth, potentially leading to higher future stock returns.

name: Interest Coverage Ratio
construction: Earnings before interest and taxes divided by interest expenses
rationale: A higher interest coverage ratio suggests a company is better equipped to handle its debt obligations, which might be viewed favorably by investors.

name: R&D Intensity
construction: Research and development expenses divided by total revenue
rationale: Higher R&D intensity may signal future growth opportunities, which could lead to higher stock returns.

name: Sales Per Employee
construction: Total revenue divided by the number of employees
rationale: Higher sales per employee can signify greater productivity and efficiency, which may lead to higher future stock returns.

name: Earnings Yield Spread
construction: Earnings yield minus the yield on a 3-month Treasury bill
rationale: A higher spread between the earnings yield and the risk-free rate might signal an undervalued stock, which could lead to higher future returns.

name: Inventory Turnover
construction: Cost of goods sold divided by average inventory during the period
rationale: Higher inventory turnover may suggest efficient inventory management and stronger sales, which could lead to higher future stock returns.

name: Operating Cash Flow Margin
construction: Operating cash flow divided by total revenue
rationale: A higher operating cash flow margin may indicate a firm's ability to convert sales into cash efficiently, a potentially attractive quality to investors.

name: Net Debt Issuance
construction: Calculate the change in total debt from last fiscal year. Normalize across the cross-section on each forecast date.
rationale: Firms that increase their leverage could be distressed, signaling lower future performance.

name: Change in Share of Market Capitalization
construction: Calculate the year-to-date change in a firm's share of total US equity market capitalization.
rationale: Firms gaining a larger share of the total market could be capturing a competitive advantage.

name: Earnings Announcement Volatility
construction: Calculate the 12-month trailing standard deviation of daily returns surrounding quarterly earnings announcements.
rationale: Firms with stable earnings could have lower risk and higher future returns.

name: Non-operating Expense Ratio
construction: Calculate the ratio of non-operating expenses to total revenues from the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Firms with higher non-operating expenses could have less efficient spending, leading to lower future returns.

name: Employee Growth
construction: Calculate the year-over-year change in the number of employees from the most recent annual report.
rationale: Firms that are expanding their workforce might be anticipating higher future revenues, leading to higher returns.

name: Change in Institutional Ownership
construction: Calculate the change in institutional ownership from last fiscal year to this fiscal year.
rationale: Institutions may have superior information, so increases in institutional ownership may signal higher future returns.

name: Customer Concentration
construction: Calculate the revenue from the company's largest customer as a percentage of total revenues from the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Firms with high customer concentration may have higher business risk and lower future returns.

name: Short-term Asset Turnover
construction: Calculate the ratio of sales to short-term assets (cash, receivables, and inventory) from the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Firms that use short-term assets more efficiently may have higher profitability, leading to higher future returns.

name: Change in Cash Ratio
construction: Calculate the change in the ratio of cash to total assets from last fiscal year to this fiscal year.
rationale: An increase in the cash ratio may signal a firm's improving liquidity, which could predict higher future returns.

name: Lease Expenses
construction: Calculate the ratio of leasing expenses to total assets from the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Higher lease expenses may signal a lack of capital for investment, predicting lower future performance.

name: Non-Operating Income
construction: Calculated using the difference between total revenue and operating income over the past year.
rationale: Firms with higher non-operating income may have more diversified income sources, which could lead to lower risk.

name: Capital Expenditure Growth
construction: Calculated as the year-over-year percentage change in capital expenditures.
rationale: Firms that are investing more in their business may have better future growth prospects.

name: Employee Productivity
construction: Calculated as revenue per employee over the past year.
rationale: Firms with higher employee productivity may be more efficient, which could lead to higher profitability.

name: Asset Intangibility
construction: Calculated as the ratio of intangible assets to total assets.
rationale: Firms with a high proportion of intangible assets may have a competitive advantage that results in higher returns.

name: R&D Intensity
construction: Calculated as research and development expenses divided by sales over the past year.
rationale: Firms with high R&D intensity may be more innovative, which could lead to future growth.

name: Inventory Turnover
construction: Calculated as cost of goods sold divided by average inventory over the past year.
rationale: Firms with higher inventory turnover may have better inventory management, which could lead to higher profitability.

name: Debt Maturity
construction: Calculated as long-term debt divided by total debt.
rationale: Firms with more long-term debt may have less refinancing risk, which could lead to higher returns.

name: Tax Rate
construction: Calculated as income tax expense divided by pretax income over the past year.
rationale: Firms with higher tax rates may have less after-tax income, which could lead to lower returns.

name: Capital Structure
construction: Calculated as equity divided by total capital (equity + debt).
rationale: Firms with a higher proportion of equity financing may have lower financial risk, which could lead to higher returns.

name: Foreign Sales Ratio

rationale: CEOs who communicate effectively with investors might engender more confidence, leading to higher stock returns.
higher_returns_for: Firms with higher CEO speech scores

name: Patent Applications
construction: Count the number of patent applications filed by a company over the past year.
rationale: A higher number of patent applications can indicate a firm's investment in innovation, potentially leading to higher stock returns.
higher_returns_for: Firms with a higher number of patent applications

name: Charitable Giving
construction: Calculate the ratio of a company's charitable donations to its pre-tax profits.
rationale: Corporate social responsibility might appeal to ethically-minded investors, potentially supporting stock prices.
higher_returns_for: Firms with higher ratios of charitable giving

name: Cybersecurity Investments
construction: Estimate a company's investment in cybersecurity, based on job postings for cybersecurity roles and mentions in annual reports.
rationale: Greater investment in cybersecurity might reduce a firm's risk of costly data breaches, potentially leading to higher stock returns.
higher_returns_for: Firms with higher estimated cybersecurity investments

name: Customer Satisfaction
construction: Analyze customer reviews on websites and social media. Use natural language processing to determine overall sentiment.
rationale: Companies with satisfied customers may have a stronger brand and higher sales, leading to higher stock returns.
higher_returns_for: Firms with higher average customer satisfaction scores

name: Supply Chain Efficiency
construction: Calculate the ratio of cost of goods sold to total revenue, using data from the company's financial statements.
rationale: A lower ratio could indicate more efficient supply chain management, potentially leading to higher stock returns.
higher_returns_for: Firms with lower ratios of cost of goods sold to revenue

name: Productivity Growth
construction: Measure as the change in revenue per employee over the past year.
rationale: Companies with growing productivity may be more efficient and profitable in future.

name: Brand Strength
construction: Use advertising spending as a proxy. Calculate as advertising expense divided by total revenue.
rationale: Strong brands may have more pricing power and customer loyalty.

name: Capex Efficiency
construction: Calculate as the change in capital expenditures divided by the change in total assets over the past year.
rationale: Efficient capex might signal profitable growth opportunities.

name: Customer Concentration
construction: Calculate as revenue from the largest customer divided by total revenue.
rationale: Companies reliant on few customers may be vulnerable to customer churn.

name: Debt Maturity
construction: Calculate as the average time until a company's debt comes due.
rationale: Longer debt maturity may provide more financial flexibility.

name: Management Ownership
construction: Calculate as the number of shares held by senior management divided by total shares outstanding.
rationale: Management with more skin in the game may act more in shareholders' interest.

name: Employee Satisfaction
construction: Use employee turnover rate as a proxy. Calculate as the number of employees leaving the company divided by the total number of employees over the past year.
rationale: A satisfied workforce may lead to better productivity and lower hiring costs.

name: Dividend Growth
construction: Calculate as the change in dividends per share over the past year.
rationale: Dividend growth may signal strong future cash flows.

name: R&D Efficiency
construction: Calculate as the change in revenue divided by the change in R&D spending over the past year.
rationale: Efficiency in R&D may predict successful innovation and competitive advantage.

name: Sales Stability
construction: Calculate as the standard deviation of quarterly sales growth rates over the past year.
rationale: Stable sales might indicate a reliable business model.

name: Employee Satisfaction Index
construction: Derived from employee review platforms like Glassdoor, and labor-market data from Bureau of Labor Statistics. The index would be built using a mix of job satisfaction, wage rates, and company ratings.

name: Environmental Impact Score
construction: Calculate the Environmental Impact Score using publicly available pollution data and company filings about environmental practices.
rationale: Companies with low environmental impact might be more sustainable in long run and could face fewer regulatory penalties.

name: Supply Chain Resilience
construction: Measured by diversification and geographic spread of a company's suppliers, as well as the company's past ability to manage supply shocks.
rationale: Companies with more resilient supply chains are more robust to shocks, and therefore less risky.

construction: From annual reports and other filings, measure a firm's investment in cybersecurity infrastructure and personnel.
rationale: Given the increasing importance of digital assets, firms that invest in cybersecurity may be better positioned to protect those assets and avoid costly breaches.

rationale: Companies with a diverse range of products might be less susceptible to industry-specific shocks.

name: Executive Turnover
construction: Count the number of executive-level departures in the past year.
rationale: High executive turnover may indicate instability or internal issues within the firm.

name: Dividend Coverage Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of the ratio of Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT) to dividends paid over the past 5 years
rationale: Firms with high dividend coverage volatility may face more uncertainty in their ability to maintain dividends, which could lead investors to require a higher return

name: Inventory Turnover Growth
construction: Growth rate of the ratio of cost of goods sold to inventory over the past 1 year
rationale: Firms improving their efficiency in selling their inventory are likely to have improving operating performance and may earn higher future returns

name: Sales Forecast Dispersion
construction: Standard deviation of analysts' sales forecasts for the next fiscal year, divided by the number of forecasts
rationale: High dispersion of analysts' forecasts may signal higher risk, leading to higher expected returns

construction: Sales to the largest customer as a proportion of total sales
rationale: Firms with high customer concentration may face higher business risk due to potential loss of a major customer

name: Employee Productivity
construction: Sales divided by number of employees
rationale: High employee productivity may indicate a firm's operational efficiency and competitiveness

name: Pension Fund Status
construction: Market value of pension fund assets minus pension obligations
rationale: Firms with underfunded pension plans may face higher future expenses, which could lead to higher required return

name: Off-Balance Sheet Liability
construction: Operating lease obligations from footnotes, discounted back to the present using the firm's cost of debt
rationale: Firms with high off-balance sheet liability may face higher future expenses and higher risk, leading to higher required return

name: Geographic Diversification
construction: Number of different geographic segments in which the firm operates
rationale: Firms that are more geographically diversified may have lower risk due to diversification benefits

name: Environmental Compliance Cost
construction: Costs related to environmental compliance disclosed in footnotes or MD&A
rationale: Firms with high environmental compliance cost may face higher operational cost and higher risk, leading to higher required return

name: Investment Cycle
construction: Change in capital expenditures as a percentage of property, plant, and equipment
rationale: Firms in the expansion phase of their investment cycle may have higher future growth potential

name: Net Stock Issuance
construction: Calculate the difference between shares issued and shares repurchased over the past fiscal year.
rationale: Firms issuing new shares may be overvalued, signaling low future returns, while those repurchasing may be undervalued.

name: Composite Equity Issuance
construction: Compute net equity issuance and scale by market capitalization. Sum it up over the past five years.
rationale: Sustained equity dilution may indicate overvaluation.

name: Accruals
construction: Calculate the difference between net income and cash flow from operations, scaled by total assets.
rationale: Firms with high accruals may be engaging in earnings management, implying lower future earnings.

name: Net Operating Assets
construction: Calculate the difference between total assets and total liabilities, excluding cash, and divide by total assets.
rationale: Firms with high net operating assets may be less efficient, suggesting lower future returns.

name: Gross Profitability
construction: Calculate gross profits (revenue minus cost of goods sold) over total assets.
rationale: Firms with high gross profitability might have competitive advantages, implying higher future returns.

name: Asset Growth
construction: Calculate the annual growth rate of total assets.
rationale: Firms with high asset growth may be overinvesting, implying lower future returns.

name: Return on Assets
construction: Calculate net income over total assets.
rationale: Firms with high return on assets might be more efficient, suggesting higher future returns.

name: Investment to Assets
construction: Calculate the ratio of capital expenditures to total assets.
rationale: Firms with high investment to assets may be overinvesting, implying lower future returns.

name: Change in Turnover
construction: Calculate the change in asset turnover (sales divided by total assets) from the previous year.
rationale: Increases in turnover may signal improved efficiency, implying higher future returns.

name: Change in Net Operating Assets
construction: Calculate the annual change in net operating assets.
rationale: Firms with increasing net operating assets may be less efficient, suggesting lower future returns.

name: Internet Adoption Ratio

higher_returns_for: Firms with high corporate culture scores

name: Revenue Concentration
construction: Calculate the percentage of a firm's revenue that comes from its largest customer in the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Firms that are overly reliant on a single customer may be exposed to higher risk and potential volatility in earnings.

name: Social Media Sentiment
construction: Measure the sentiment of social media posts about a company over the past month using natural language processing techniques.
rationale: Positive sentiment on social media may indicate positive future performance.

name: CEO Compensation Ratio
construction: Calculate the ratio of CEO compensation to median employee compensation.
rationale: A high ratio may indicate overcompensation of the CEO and potential misallocation of resources.
higher_returns_for: Companies with low CEO compensation ratios

name: Product Review Score
construction: Aggregate and average product review scores from online retailers over the past quarter.
rationale: High product review scores may indicate high product quality and customer satisfaction, leading to increased sales.
higher_returns_for: Companies with high product review scores

name: Patent Application Count
construction: Count the number of patent applications filed by a company over the past year.
rationale: A high number of patent applications may indicate a strong research and development pipeline.
higher_returns_for: Companies with a high number of patent applications

name: Employee Turnover Rate
construction: Calculate the annual employee turnover rate.
rationale: A high turnover rate may indicate employee dissatisfaction and potential operational issues.
higher_returns_for: Companies with low employee turnover rates

name: Customer Complaint Count
construction: Count the number of customer complaints received over the past quarter.
rationale: A high number of complaints may indicate poor product quality or customer service, potentially impacting future sales.
higher_returns_for: Companies with low customer complaint counts

name: Supplier Concentration
construction: Calculate the percentage of supplies sourced from the company's largest supplier.
rationale: High supplier concentration may indicate vulnerability to supply chain disruptions.

name: Environmental Impact Score
construction: Calculate an environmental impact score based on publicly available data on a company's carbon emissions, waste production, and water usage.
rationale: Companies with low environmental impact may be more attractive to socially conscious investors.
higher_returns_for: Companies with low environmental impact scores

name: Cybersecurity Incident Count
construction: Count the number of reported cybersecurity incidents over the past year.
rationale: A high number of incidents may indicate poor cybersecurity practices and potential future liabilities.
higher_returns_for: Companies with low cybersecurity incident counts

name: Diversity Score
construction: Calculate a diversity score based on the representation of different demographic groups in a company's workforce.
rationale: Companies with diverse workforces may benefit from a wider range of perspectives and ideas.

name: Inventory Growth Rate
construction: Annual percentage change in inventories (from Compustat item INVT) over the prior fiscal year, scaled by total assets.
rationale: Rapid inventory accumulation may reflect overproduction or expected demand shortfalls, leading to future negative earnings surprises.

name: Cash Flow Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly cash flow from operations (Compustat OANCF) over the prior three years, divided by average total assets.
rationale: Firms with stable cash flows are perceived as less risky, but riskier firms may command higher expected returns.

name: Past R&D Intensity Change
construction: Change in R&D expense (Compustat XRD) as a percentage of sales over the past two years.
rationale: Increases in R&D intensity may signal future growth opportunities not yet incorporated in prices.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth
construction: Annual growth in current assets (Compustat ACT), scaled by prior year total assets.
rationale: Aggressive expansion of current assets may signal empire-building or low investment efficiency.

name: Officers' Compensation Ratio
construction: Total officers’ compensation disclosed in annual proxy statements divided by total sales.
rationale: Higher compensation ratios may signal agency problems and weaker governance, leading to lower future returns.

name: Depreciation Policy Aggressiveness
construction: Depreciation expense (Compustat DP) as a fraction of gross property, plant, and equipment (PPENT) over the past year.
rationale: Aggressive depreciation may indicate conservative accounting or signal undervaluation.

name: Pension Expense to Assets
construction: Annual pension expense (Compustat XPR) divided by average total assets.
rationale: Higher pension expenses may indicate stronger commitments to employees but could also signal underfunded plans and future cash flow constraints.

name: Receivables to Sales Change
construction: Change in accounts receivable (Compustat RECT) as a percentage of sales over the prior year.
rationale: A rapid increase in receivables relative to sales may indicate loosening credit standards or deteriorating customer quality.

name: Auditor Size Indicator
construction: Binary indicator for whether the firm’s auditor is one of the ‘Big 8’ accounting firms (from proxy disclosures and auditor lists).
rationale: Firms audited by larger, reputable auditors may have higher transparency and lower risk of misstatement.
higher_returns_for: firms not audited by Big 8 auditors

name: Employee Count Growth
construction: Annual percentage change in number of employees (from 10-K filings), scaled by prior year employee count.
rationale: Rapid employee growth may signal overexpansion or overoptimism by management.

name: Short-Term Earnings Acceleration
construction: Compute the change in quarterly earnings growth rate: (most recent quarterly EPS - EPS one quarter ago) minus (EPS one quarter ago - EPS two quarters ago), divided by stock price.
rationale: Firms with accelerating earnings growth may signal improving fundamentals not yet fully incorporated in prices.

name: Inventory Change Ratio
construction: Inventory change over past year divided by average total assets over the same period, using Compustat data.
rationale: Sudden increases in inventories can indicate poor sales prospects or overproduction, while decreases suggest strong demand.

name: Net Insider Buying
construction: Net purchases of shares by corporate insiders over the past six months, scaled by total shares outstanding, based on SEC filings.
rationale: Insider buying may reveal private information about undervaluation or future positive developments.

name: R&D Expense Ratio
construction: R&D expenditures divided by total sales over the past fiscal year, from Compustat.
rationale: Higher R&D spending may signal growth opportunities and management’s confidence in future prospects.

name: Operating Cash Flow to Price
construction: Operating cash flow over the past year divided by current market capitalization.
rationale: Cash flow is less subject to accounting manipulation than earnings and may better capture firm health.

name: Dividend Consistency Score
construction: Number of consecutive years with non-decreasing regular dividends, as reported in CRSP and company reports.
rationale: Consistent dividends indicate stable earnings and disciplined management, reducing risk.

name: Volatility Skew
construction: Difference between stock’s 12-month daily return volatility and average industry volatility over the same period.
rationale: Stocks with idiosyncratic high volatility may be riskier or subject to mispricing.

name: Receivables Growth
construction: Annual growth rate of accounts receivable divided by sales growth over the same period.
rationale: Faster receivables growth than sales suggests earnings quality issues and potential collection problems.

name: Employee Productivity
construction: Total sales divided by number of employees at fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms with higher productivity may be more efficient and profitable, supporting higher returns.

name: Price Reaction to Earnings Announcement
construction: Cumulative abnormal return over 2 days centered on most recent quarterly earnings announcement.
rationale: Stocks with muted price reactions may reflect delayed information incorporation and underreaction.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth
construction: Percentage change in total current assets over the prior fiscal year, using data from Compustat annual balance sheets.
rationale: Rapid asset growth may signal overinvestment or empire-building, while slower asset growth may indicate disciplined capital allocation.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low short-term asset growth

name: Inventory Turnover Acceleration
construction: Year-over-year change in inventory turnover ratio (COGS divided by average inventories) calculated from Compustat annual data.
rationale: Improving inventory turnover suggests increasing operational efficiency and potential future profitability.
higher_returns_for: stocks with large positive changes in inventory turnover

name: Long-Term Debt Reduction
construction: Percentage decrease in long-term debt over the past three fiscal years, from Compustat balance sheets.
rationale: Firms reducing leverage may be de-risking, signaling stronger future performance.
higher_returns_for: stocks with large reductions in long-term debt

name: Operating Expense Slope
construction: Regression slope of SG&A expenses to sales over the past five fiscal years, using Compustat annual income statements.
rationale: A declining SG&A-to-sales ratio may indicate increasing scalability and profitability.
higher_returns_for: stocks with the most negative slopes (fastest declining SG&A-to-sales ratios)

name: Dividend Initiation
construction: Indicator variable equal to one if a firm initiates a dividend in the past year (Compustat dividend data), zero otherwise.
rationale: Dividend initiation may signal management confidence in stable cash flows.

name: Earnings Estimate Dispersion
construction: Standard deviation of IBES analyst EPS forecasts for the next fiscal year, scaled by the mean forecast.
rationale: High dispersion reflects disagreement and greater uncertainty, which may be associated with higher risk and future returns.
higher_returns_for: stocks with high earnings forecast dispersion

name: Cash Flow Consistency
construction: Standard deviation of operating cash flows divided by average cash flows over past five years (Compustat cash flow statement).
rationale: Consistent cash generators may be undervalued due to investor preference for smooth earnings.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low cash flow variability

name: Delayed Price Momentum
construction: Past 12-month stock return measured from 13 to 1 months ago, skipping the most recent month (CRSP monthly returns).
rationale: Lagged momentum signals may capture investor underreaction missed by traditional momentum measures.
higher_returns_for: stocks with high past 12-month returns excluding the last month

name: Insider Net Purchases
construction: Net purchases of shares by insiders over the past year divided by shares outstanding, from SEC Form 4 filings.
rationale: Insider buying can indicate undervaluation or positive private information.
higher_returns_for: stocks with high net insider purchases

name: R&D Intensity Change
construction: Year-over-year change in R&D expense divided by total assets, using Compustat annual data.
rationale: Increasing R&D intensity may predict future innovation and growth.
higher_returns_for: stocks with largest increases in R&D-to-assets ratio

name: Employee Growth Rate
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in total number of employees, using headcount data from annual 10-K filings.
rationale: Rapid expansion in workforce may signal aggressive growth strategies or overinvestment; slower or negative growth may indicate operational efficiency or retrenchment.
higher_returns_for: firms with low or negative employee growth rates

name: Net Operating Asset Change
construction: Change in (Operating Assets - Operating Liabilities) divided by total assets over the last fiscal year, using balance sheet data.
rationale: Firms aggressively increasing net operating assets may be overinvesting, while restrained asset growth may predict superior returns.
higher_returns_for: firms with small or negative changes in net operating assets

name: R&D Intensity
construction: Annual R&D expense divided by total sales, from income statement data, for the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: A higher fraction of spending on R&D may signal innovation and growth opportunities not captured by book value.

name: Short-Term Asset Turnover Acceleration
construction: One-year change in (Sales / Average Total Assets), using income statement and balance sheet data.
rationale: Improving asset turnover may indicate increasing operational efficiency or improving business prospects.
higher_returns_for: firms with large positive changes in asset turnover

name: Dividend Initiation Indicator
construction: Binary indicator equal to 1 if a firm initiates a dividend payment this year after not paying dividends in the prior year, using CRSP dividend history.
rationale: Dividend initiations can signal management’s confidence in future cash flows.

name: Sales Variability
construction: Standard deviation of annual sales growth rates over the past five years, using income statement data.
rationale: Firms with more stable revenue streams may be perceived as safer and less risky.

name: Depreciation Accruals
construction: Depreciation expense divided by gross property, plant, and equipment (PPE), from annual income statement and balance sheet data.
rationale: A higher depreciation-to-PPE ratio may proxy for older or less productive assets and declining investment.

name: Inventory Revaluation Ratio
construction: Change in reported inventory value divided by total assets over the past year, from balance sheet data.
rationale: Rapid inventory buildup may signal overproduction or slowing demand.
higher_returns_for: firms with low or negative inventory revaluation ratios

name: CEO Tenure
construction: Number of years the current CEO has served, based on company proxy statements.
rationale: Longer CEO tenure may reflect experienced leadership and stability, or possible entrenchment.
higher_returns_for: firms with moderate CEO tenure (neither new nor entrenched)

name: Pre-Tax Margin Expansion
construction: Current year's pre-tax income divided by sales minus the prior year's value, normalized by beginning sales, using income statement data.
rationale: Firms expanding pre-tax margins may be capturing pricing power or improving cost efficiencies.
higher_returns_for: firms with large positive changes in pre-tax margin

name: R&D Intensity Change
construction: Change in R&D expenditure over the past year, scaled by beginning-of-year total assets. Data from Compustat: (R&D_t - R&D_{t-1}) / Assets_{t-1}.
rationale: Firms increasing R&D investment may have better growth prospects not yet fully priced by the market.

name: Short-Term Debt Surge
construction: Percentage increase in short-term debt (Compustat: Data item 34) over the past fiscal year, scaled by total assets.
rationale: Large increases in short-term borrowing may signal impending liquidity needs or distressed financing, which could predict lower returns.

name: Inventory Turnover Acceleration
construction: One-year change in inventory turnover ratio: (COGS / Average Inventory)_{t} - (COGS / Average Inventory)_{t-1}.
rationale: Improving inventory turnover may indicate operational efficiency or increasing demand, both of which may predict higher returns.

name: Share Repurchase Ratio
construction: Net reduction in shares outstanding over the prior year divided by market capitalization at the start of the year.
